jobs.title: Chef d'Equipe (Team Leader) basé à Bria
Chef de Projet basé à Bria
Chef de Projet FH LAM
jobs.description:
Créée en 1922, DanChurchAid (DCA) est une organisation non gouvernementale Danoise dont l’action est basée sur les droits. Installée en RCA depuis 2015, DCA fournit une assistance aux communautés les plus démunies en situation de conflit et de post-conflit au travers de son Programme d’Action Humanitaire «Communautés Plus Sûres » : éducation aux risques des Armes Légères et Petit Calibres (ALPC), des Restes et Explosifs de Guerre (REG) ; Réduction de la Violence Armée (RVA) et consolidation de la paix & Support Psycho social , distribution des biens non alimentaires et ménagers (NFI), Cash conditionnel et inconditionnel (coupons alimentaires, etc), distribution des semences et outils, appui aux organisations de la Société Civile pour leur implication dans la réforme du Secteur de Sécurité (RSS).

DCA recherche **un (01) Chef de Projet** très expérimentés pour participer au développement et la mise en œuvre des activités dans les zones de **Amdafock, Birao, Batangafo, Kabo, Paoua, Obo, Zémio**.

**OBJECTIF DU POSTE :**

DanChurchAid (DCA) lance un appel à candidatures pour un(e) Chef (fe) de Projet Lutte Antimines Humanitaire (LAMH) pour son Bureau Pays en RCA. Le lieu de travail est Bangui avec des déplacements fréquents sur le terrain (localités de Amdafock, Birao, Bria, Batangafo, Kabo, Paoua, Obo, Zemio).

Le rôle principal du/de la Chef (fe) de projet est de :

- Assurer de la gestion du projet dans sa totalité, y compris (mais sans s’y limiter) la coordination, suivi et assurance qualité des activités ;
- Assurer le rapportage interne/externe ainsi que la coordination et renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux
- Garantir l’engagement externe vis-à-vis d’autres acteurs LAMH et de protection, ainsi que toute autre responsabilité permettant de contribuer aux objectifs envisagés dans les limites de la portée, du budget et de l'échéancier définis dans le cadre du projet.

Le/la Chef.fe de projet devra avoir d'excellentes compétences opérationnelles, en communication, en leadership et en résolution de problèmes, ainsi qu'une expérience des méthodologies et des outils de gestion de projet. Le(la) Candidat(e) idéal(e) aura également des compétences préalables et des connaissances de base dans le domaine de la lutte antimines humanitaire (éducation aux risques d’engins explosifs, enquêtes non techniques, assistance aux victimes). En plus, le/la Chef.fe de projet doit être capable de bien travailler sous pression et d’être capable de gérer plusieurs tâches simultanément.

**RÔLES & RESPONSABILITÉS**

**Gestion de projet et planification :**

- Assurer la planification globale des activités du projet et veiller au respect des délais et de la qualité dans la mise en œuvre,
- Organiser avec l’équipe MEAL les activités d’évaluation du projet (Baseline, enquête de satisfaction, Endline) et de mise à jour des outils de pilotage du projet,
- Coordonner et suivre l’implémentation des activités (lancement, ciblage, renforcement des capacités etc.) en lien avec d’autres collègues de DCA, tout en assurant la qualité technique des activités de mise en œuvre,
- Faire le suivi de la mise en œuvre des planifications conformément aux planning établis par le biais de rencontres périodiques avec les partenaires et/ou autres parties prenantes du projet,
- Veiller à l’efficacité des planifications par rapport aux réalisations et analyser les facteurs de blocage dans la mise en œuvre.

**Gestion du budget :**

- Être responsable de tout aspect lié à la bonne gestion budgétaire, notamment la planification mensuelle, la mise à jour régulière des outils de suivi budgétaire, le tracking des taux de dépense, en lien avec l’équipe support (finance et logistique),
- Participer à l’élaboration et à la mise à jour continue du plan d’achat du projet, et contribuer à sa mise en œuvre (préparation de la documentation requise, participation au processus de sélection des fournisseurs, coordination des activités de distribution, au besoin), conformément aux procédures internes de DCA,
- Veiller au respect des procédures de DCA et bailleurs dans le cadre de la réalisation des activités,

**Communication et coordination :**

- Assurer la liaison avec les parties prenantes (autorités locales, services techniques de l’Etat, etc.), les membres de l'équipe et les bénéficiaires du projet afin de garantir une communication et une coordination efficaces tout au long du projet,
- Documenter les avancées du projet, l’impact des activités et assurer le partage d’informations clés avec les équipes de mise en œuvre et en lien avec l’équipe MEAL de DCA,
- Favoriser le partage d’informations et la coordination entre les partenaires de mise en œuvre, notamment pour assurer le lien entre les activités terrain et les activités de recherche-action participative.

**Gestion de l’information, rapportage et capitalisation :**

- Mettre à jour les documents clés du projet, y compris le plan de travail, les calendriers, les budgets et les rapports, ainsi que contribuer au suivi du cadre logique et des résultats du projet,
- Documenter les leçons apprises et les cas de succès en collaboration avec l’équipe MEAL,
- Assurer la bonne gestion, stockage et partage des documents clés du projet,
- Communiquer régulièrement avec le Responsable des Programmes LAMH de DCA sur les avancées du projet ainsi que les défis rencontrés par les équipes de DCA et des organisations partenaires,
- Collecter et analyser les informations qualitatives et quantitatives par le biais des équipes terrain,
- Rédiger tous les rapports narratifs internes et bailleur en respect strict des échéances prévues et des formats,
- Participer mensuellement aux réunions de suivi budgétaire organisées au niveau de la coordination de DCA,
- Centraliser et compiler les leçons apprises et les recommandations aux différentes étapes clés du projet et à la suite de l’atelier de capitalisation/ clôture,
- Rédiger de façon ad hoc selon les demandes et besoins de la mission des histoires à succès et/ou études de cas pour mettre en avant l’impact et les approches des projets.

**Mise en œuvre et suivi opérationnel :**

- Faciliter l’organisation des sessions de formations thématiques avec les équipes DCA et partenaires,
- Participer aux instances de coordination humanitaires,
- Veiller au respect des règles de sécurité par le personnel sous sa supervision et la coordination avec les ONG nationales partenaires,
- S’assurer de la bonne planification et suivi des activités terrain en collaboration avec le Coordinateur de projet de l’ONG partenaire,
- Veiller à une mise en œuvre conforme aux directives et approches du projet et conformément aux procédures de DCA et du bailleur, ainsi que des procédures spécifiques au domaine de la lutte antimines.

**Contrôle qualité :**

- Être responsable de la qualité de toute activité de mise en œuvre, ainsi que des livrables prévues dans le cadre du projet ; garantir la qualité des produits et activités envisagés dans le cadre du projet,
- S’assurer que les livrables du projet répondent aux normes de qualité requises par le bailleur ainsi que les normes de qualité de DCA,
- S’assurer de la mise en œuvre des opérations conformément aux exigences de DCA en matière de gestion de la qualité des activités LAMH (SOP), en collaboration avec le Responsable des Programmes LAMH de DCA,
- Réaliser des missions de suivi régulières permettant de veiller à la qualité des livrables du projet, et accompagner le processus de renforcement des capacités techniques des partenaires locaux,
- Partager avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre des recommandations issues des missions et assurer leurs suivis afin d’améliorer la qualité des interventions,
- Assurer le respect des principes humanitaires, y compris la redevabilité envers les bénéficiaires et l’efficacité des interventions, tout en veillant à la mise en œuvre des activités selon les bonnes pratiques de la programmation humanitaire et de développement,
- Contribuer à l’élaboration, planification et facilitation des évaluations effectuées sur le terrain par les équipes des projets et l’équipe MEAL DCA,
- Evaluer la pertinence des activités menées, l’efficacité des interventions et leur adéquation au regard de l’évolution du contexte et des besoins des populations,
- S’assurer de l’atteinte des résultats et des indicateurs du projet en lien avec l’équipe MEAL de DCA, tout en contribuant à renseigner les outils de suivi demandés par le bailleur,
- S’assurer de l’exigence de durabilité des objectifs du projet, de la pérennité des actions et, le cas échéant, du respect des normes et standards établis,
- Contribuer à l’élaboration, planification et facilitation des évaluations effectuées par le Chargé MEAL,
- Coordonner et contribuer à la production de supports de communication sur le projet.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Pré-requis :**

- Nationalité centrafricaine,
- Une qualification académique pertinente de niveau maitrise en gestion, études de développement, ou tout autre sujet pertinent ou une expérience professionnelle équivalente,
- Au moins 4 ans d'expérience, de préférence au sein d'organisations non gouvernementales dans le domaine de l’action contre les mines (Education aux risques des engins explosifs, assistance aux victimes, enquêtes non-techniques)
- Bonne capacité d'analyse et de recherche,
- Expérience de travail dans un contexte instable et capacité à travailler sous pression,
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint),
- Langues : excellente maîtrise du français à l’écrit et à l’oral nécessaire ; une connaissance de l'anglais est un atout,
- Solides compétences en matière de leadership, de constitution d'équipes et de communication,
- Attitude de résolution de problèmes, approche organisée et structurée et capacité à planifier, coordonner et diriger des processus incluant de multiples parties prenantes et intérêts,
- Engagement, flexibilité, orientation vers les résultats et fortes compétences interpersonnelles, y compris la capacité à gérer une journée de travail chargée avec des délais contradictoires dans un environnement multiculturel.

**Le poste est réservé uniquement aux candidats de la nationalité centrafricaine.**

jobs.title: Head of MENA
jobs.description:
**Head of Middle East and North Africa**

Front Line Defenders are recruiting a **Head of Middle East and North Africa (MENA)** to join our team. This is a permanent role based in the region reporting to the Director of Global Protection.

**Overview**

The Regional Team leads Front Line Defenders’ work in the Region, with responsibility for defining priorities, directing organisational protection responses, and ensuring that resources are deployed where they have the greatest impact for human rights defenders (HRDs). Grounded in sustained engagement with HRDs and regional ecosystems, the team determines where the organisation acts, who and how it supports, and how it responds to evolving risks. The Regional Team plays a central role in shaping organisational direction by ensuring that strategies, approaches and interventions are driven by regional priorities, while contributing directly to global strategy and positioning.

The Head of Region leads the Regional Protection Team and is responsible for setting the strategic direction, priorities, and protection responses of Front Line Defenders within the region. The role ensures that the organisation’s work is grounded in the realities, needs, and priorities of human rights defenders, with resources directed where they can make the greatest impact. They play a crucial role in aligning regional priorities with organisational strategy by translating contextual insights into organisational priorities and actively shaping global strategy and positioning. Working closely with various Heads of Programmes, the Head of Region/Protection ensures that all organisational programmes are aligned with and responsive to regional priorities. The role also assumes overall management and operational responsibility for the regional team, ensuring the coordinated, effective, and secure delivery of work across various contexts. This includes oversight of implementation of workplans, risk management, operations, cross-team coordination, and leadership of a geographically dispersed team.

**Background**

Front Line Defenders is an international organisation based in Ireland that works exclusively for the protection of human rights defenders at risk. Human rights defenders are people who are persecuted because of their peaceful work for the rights of others. Front Line Defenders provides practical help through protection grants, physical and digital protection training, lobbying, advocacy and campaigning.

**Role responsibilities**

**Key duties include:**

- Nurture an inclusive, values-driven, supportive team culture with a focus on delivering impact for human rights defenders in line with the organisation’s vision, values and mission.
- Lead the regional team to develop, monitor, and implement work plans to ensure the delivery of regional strategies. The Head of Region will provide spaces for learning, analysis and strategic planing, as well as convene and chair regular meetings for team coordination and collaboration in the implementation of work plans.
- Work with the regional team across the different areas of response to HRDs, sustaining core workflows while leading initiatives to optimize underperforming processes.
- Support Protection Coordinators’ to spearhead the identification of emerging trends and regional strategic prioritisation, amplifying their voice to inform organisational strategy, and set priorities for coordination with programmes (Resilience and Well being, Protection Grants, Advocacy, Development, Comms&Events, ME).
- In cooperation with the Operations team, contribute to organisational operations systems, procedures and policies to support the efficient functioning of the organisation in their region.
- In close cooperation with respective team members, assess key financial, legal, operational and reputation issues and risks involving the staff and FLD work in the region, and feed into organisation risk management systems.
- Foster healthy behaviour at work, ensuring regular check-ins with staff, spotting early warning signs of stress and burnout, making supportive adjustments at work, and nurturing positive relationships.
- Contributing to active risk management to identify, analyse and mitigate against risks that may impact staff and the delivery of programmes.
- Supporting FLD to be a learning organisation, which continually measures, evaluates, reviews and learns in order to improve and enhance our delivery and responsiveness to HRD’s by anticipating, identifying and solving problems and that we share learning to ensure continuous improvements across teams.
- Plan, manage and monitor the regional annual budget, ensuring strong financial stewardship and effective delivery within agreed parameters.
- Maintain and develop relationships with key partners, supporters, funders, and potential funders.

For further information, please view:

[https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/sites/default/files/head_of_mena_jd_fd_october_2026.pdf](https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/sites/default/files/head_of_mena_jd_fd_october_2026.pdf)

**Salary & Benefits**

- €73,327 - €91,382 per annum
- 26 annual leave days
- Pension
- Paid Health Insurance
- Income Protection & Life Assurance
- Employee Assistance Scheme (EAP)
- Monthly Well-Being Provisions

**Requirements**

**Interested applicants must have:**

- Considerable knowledge and understanding of international human rights work, including the role and holistic protection needs of human rights defenders.
- Strong understanding of the political and human rights contexts across the MENA region.
- Excellent political judgement, including the ability to make strategic choices based on sound analysis of potential costs and benefits.
- Demonstrated strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify and resolve potential issues before they arise.
- Sound decision making, particularly in high-pressure and high-risk situations.
- High level of competence in English and Arabic,.
- Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills, including the ability to clearly and concisely communicate ideas.
- Strong drafting, editing, and proofreading skills with the ability to produce clear and accurate documents efficiently.
- Excellent interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues across the organisation, as well as with HRDs, NGOs, and government / institution officials.
- Ability to supervise, mentor, and provide guidance to a diverse team, while contributing effectively within multi-level team environments.
- Lead by example to motivate staff and ensure the values and culture of the organisation are maintained.
- Demonstrates personal leadership, initiative and pro-activity.
- Capacity to plan, prioritise and manage multiple, sometimes competing demands efficiently in a challenging, fast-paced environment.
- Strong organisational skills including an ability to prioritise initiatives across several countries in multiple time zones.
- Basic skills for budgeting management.
- At least 10 years’ experience working at a senior level in a human rights organisation, or equivalent experience in a similar organisation in a leadership role.
- Experience of working in an international context in the protection of human rights and/or human rights defenders, ideally within an international or regional human rights organisation.
- Significant management experience in a relevant field, people management, staff well-being, strategic planning, and evaluation.
- Experience of building and working effectively with teams of people from diverse professional and/or cultural backgrounds, including managing remote staff and working across multiple time zones.
- Experience of managing budgets and delivering organisational objectives, including fundraising experience.
- Experience of driving innovation and developing programming in a relevant field.
- Documented experience working with human rights defenders and/or human rights organisations.

jobs.title: Chargé-e des Opérations - SENEGAL (JPO)
jobs.description:
**Entrée en fonction :** 1.12.26

**Durée :** 12 mois

**Lieu :** Dakar, Sénégal

**Statut :** non accompagné

Terre des hommes ne fixe pas de date de clôture pour ce poste ; le recrutement se poursuit jusqu'à ce que le poste soit pourvu.

**Tdh :**

La Fondation Terre des hommes (Tdh), dont le siège est à Lausanne et le bureau à Zurich, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant avec plus de 2000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices dans le monde. Nous nous engageons aux côtés des enfants pour garantir leurs droits, protéger leur vie et améliorer leur bien-être. Nous y parvenons grâce à nos programmes innovants dans les domaines de la santé, de la migration et de l'accès à la justice, conçus pour avoir un impact positif et durable.

**Contexte :**

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), fondée en 1960, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant. Tdh se consacre à apporter des changements significatifs et durables dans la vie des enfants et des jeunes, en particulier ceux et celles qui sont le plus en danger. Tdh est active dans une trentaine de pays, dans des contextes humanitaires et de développement.

En Afrique subsaharienne, Tdh intervient directement dans 8 pays (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinée-Conakry, Kenya Mali, Mauritanie, Nigeria et Sénégal,) et via des partenariats dans 6 autres pays (Benin, Cameroun, Madagascar, Niger, Togo et Ouganda).

Dans le cadre de la décentralisation de son modèle d'organisation, Tdh à ouvert un bureau régional à Dakar au Sénégal pour lequel un poste de Chargé.e des Opérations est ouvert.

**Responsabilités :**

Sous la supervision de la Conseillère Régionale en recherche de fonds, le.la Chargé.e des Opérations appuie le bureau régional et les équipes pays dans la mise en œuvre des activités liées aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds dans la région Afrique.

Ce poste contribue aux processus relatifs aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds — du suivi des opportunités à l'élaboration des propositions et au reporting auprès des bailleurs — tout en soutenant les efforts en matière d'engagement des bailleurs et de partenariats à l'échelle de la région.

Grant Acquisition Process

- Contribue à l'identification et au suivi des opportunités de financement pertinentes pour les programmes de Tdh dans la région Afrique.
- Appuie le développement et la soumission de propositions de projet régionales, multipays et pays : appui ou coordination du processus d’écriture, respect des procédures bailleurs, développement de plans d’action, écriture, traduction, enregistrement sur les plateformes de soumission.
- Contribue au contrôle qualité et à la finalisation des rapports pour des financements institutionnels tout en s’assurant de la soumission en temps voulu (suivi du calendrier et des échéances, relances lorsque nécessaire auprès des contributeurs, consolidation des données, etc.), conformément aux exigences contractuelles et aux normes de Tdh.
- Assure le suivi des besoins en cofinancement avec la CR Finance, appui l'élaboration de propositions et rapports de projets à destination de fondations en coordination avec le secteur philanthropie.
- Veille à ce que les informations relatives aux subventions et aux financements dans Engage360 et les GFU pays et région (système interne de Tdh) soient exactes et régulièrement mises à jour, et assure le suivi auprès des équipes concernées pour garantir l'exhaustivité des données. En cas d’absence de Chargé.e de Grant dans une délégation, assure directement la mise à jour des données pour le pays concerné.
- Appuie le développement des contrats de partenariats opérationnels (contenu, signature, archivage, etc.).
- Contribue à l’analyse des réponses aux demandes de financements institutionnels et philanthropiques.
- S’assure de la collecte et de l’archivage des documents institutionnels nécessaires à la signature des contrats en collaboration avec le siège, la région, les délégations et les partenaires.

Communication

- Appuie la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds et les partenaires, y compris la préparation de supports de recherche de fonds (ex. : témoignages, récits de réussite).
- Appuie le rapportage annuel à travers la vérification et la consolidation des données et informations projets, en coordination avec les équipes PREX, Q&A et Grants, ainsi qu’avec les autres parties prenantes concernées aux niveaux des délégations et de la région.
- Contribue à la communication interne liée aux projets (newsletter mensuelle, supports spécifiques, etc.) et consolide les éléments proposés par les délégations et la région, en veillant à la cohérence, à l’exactitude et à la qualité des informations rapportées.

*La description complète du poste sera communiquée aux candidats sélectionnés pour lancer le processus de recrutement.*

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

Etude supérieure (Master ou autre diplôme équivalant en relations internationales, développement ou autre domaine pertinent)

**Langues :**

Excellentes compétences linguistiques en Français et Anglais.

**Compétences :**

- Bonne compréhension de la gestion du cycle de projet dans les environnements de développement, d'urgence et de crises prolongées, notamment en Afrique
- Bonne compréhension du processus d’aquisition de financements.

**IT :** Maitrise des outils et applications usuels (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

**Conditions :**

Contrat suisse

Salaire mensuel brut CHF 2450- x13,36 mois

Assurances : maladie, accident, rapatriement

Congés annuels : 25 jours/an

Vols aller-retour vers le lieu d'affectation

**Code Global de Conduite et Politiques Ethiques de Tdh :**

S'engage à promouvoir et à respecter le Code de Conduite Global, à rapporter systématiquement toute violation du Code à travers les mécanismes formels de rapport de Tdh et à traiter toute violation des procédures et des processus de manière appropriée.

Sensibilise la Fondation aux risques de non-respect des politiques, de violence et d'abus, et aux droits qui en découlent, à l'égard des enfants, des membres de la communauté et de nos propres employé.e.s.

S'engage à respecter les principales politiques et directives éthiques, notamment la politique de sauvegarde, la politique de lutte contre la fraude et la corruption, la politique relative aux conflits d'intérêts et d'autres politiques liées à la prévention du financement du terrorisme et des activités criminelles, ainsi qu’au comportement sur le lieu de travail.

S'engage à mettre en pratique les valeurs et les principes en adoptant un comportement exemplaire, en parfaite adéquation avec le code de conduite, et en respectant toujours les procédures et les processus établis.

S'engage à développer une culture de management conforme et éclairée au sein de l'organisation et dans notre travail avec les enfants et les communautés dans lesquelles nous opérons.

jobs.title: Digital Fundraising and Communications Officer

jobs.description:
**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

**Medecins du Monde Turkey (MDM-T) /** **Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**Hierarchical & Functional links**

Based in Istanbul, Digital Fundraising and Communications Officer will be directly supervised by the Deputy Operations Director

**Status**:Fixed-term contract

**Expected Starting Date:** 23/11/2026

**EXPECTED PROFILE**

**Knowledge & Qualification**

Bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing, Digital Marketing, Fundraising, Business Administration, Journalism, International Relations, or a related field.

**Experience**

· Minimum 3 years of professional experience in digital fundraising, digital marketing, communications, e-commerce, or donor acquisition.

· Demonstrated experience managing websites, social media platforms, and digital engagement tools.

· Experience developing content for fundraising, marketing, or public engagement purposes.

· Experience using digital performance data and audience insights to improve results.

· Experience working with email marketing, newsletters, CRM systems, SMS outreach tools, or online fundraising platforms is an asset.

· Experience within the non-profit, humanitarian, or development sector is desirable

**Languages**

· Excellent written and spoken Turkish. · Arabic and/or English are considered strong assets.

**IT & Equipment**

· Good proficiency with Microsoft package

**Skills and Qualities required:**

· Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook);

· Strong attention to detail, ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and effective time management;

· Capacity to handle confidential and sensitive information with a high degree of professional integrity;

· Good interpersonal and communication skills; ability to work effectively in a multicultural team environment;

· Commitment to DDD Code of Conduct and humanitarian principles;

**Essential Duties**

· Develop and implement DDD's digital acquisition strategy.

· Increase fundraising revenue through the acquisition and retention of new donors and supporters via digital channels.

· Expand DDD's digital reach, donor base, and supporter engagement.

· Identify and test innovative approaches, tools, and channels that contribute to donor and revenue growth.

· Lead content development for DDD digital channels.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Main Responsibilities**

**Function details**

**Digital Fundraising and Donor Acquisition**

· Contribute to the development and implementation of DDD's individual giving and digital fundraising strategies.

· Generate new donor leads and convert supporters into donors through digital engagement activities.

· Design and optimize donor acquisition offers, donation journeys, and online giving experiences.

· Monitor fundraising performance and make recommendations to improve results based on data and audience insights.

· Maintain an understanding of emerging digital fundraising trends, tools, and best practices.

**Website and Digital Platforms**

· Manage and develop DDD's website as a key fundraising and donor engagement platform.

· Maintain and update website content, donation pages, and landing pages.

· Develop new online fundraising initiatives and giving opportunities through DDD's digital platforms.

· Optimize website user experience.

· Coordinate with external providers and developers as required.

**Communications and Content Development**

· Develop content that supports donor acquisition, fundraising, visibility, and supporter engagement objectives.

· Produce and coordinate written, graphic, photographic, and video content for digital and print publications.

· Maintain an annual calendar of international and health-related days relevant to DDD's mission and develop timely content and fundraising hooks around them in coordination with program teams.

· Work with program teams to collect field stories, photos, videos, and impact data for donor communications, newsletters, promotional materials, and fundraising content.

· Ensure compliance with DDD branding, messaging, and visibility guidelines, including consent and data protection.

· Manage the archiving and structuring of the DDD communications Sharepoint.

**Social Media and Digital Visibility**

· Manage DDD's social media presence, including Instagram, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Facebook, and other relevant platforms for newsletters and SMS campaigns.

· Develop and implement visibility initiatives that increase audience reach and supporter engagement.

· Create, schedule, publish, and monitor content across digital channels, and recommend improvements.

**Monitoring and Reporting**

· Track and report on donor acquisition, fundraising revenue, audience growth, website performance, and digital engagement.

· Analyse fundraising and digital performance data to support decision-making and continuous improvement.

· Produce regular reports and recommendations for management.

**Reporting**

· Provide regular reporting on your activities to your Line-Manager upon his/her solicitation;

· Provide your line-manager with a Handover Report at the end of your contract

**Compliance & Ethics**
Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**
Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.

**NB:** Considering the purpose and values of the organisation, DDD requests to its employee complete flexibility in term of duties and commitment, as their job description and job title can be adjusted throughout the year according to needs and priorities.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Please be advised that female candidates are highly encouraged.

*Dünya Doktorları Derneği is an equal opportunity employer whereby we ensure all hiring and employment decisions, and operates all programs, services, and functions without the practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information or any other status or characteristic protected under applicable law.*

**How to Apply:**

Please apply with your **CV and motivation letter in ENGLISH** through our website

**Closure Date: 30.11.2026**

Due to the urgency to fill this post, DDD reserves the right to review the CVs on a rolling basis and selected candidates may be interviewed prior to the closing dates listed, therefore early applications are encouraged.
DDD is not in a position to respond to every applicant individually due to the anticipated high number of applications.
Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the first interview.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

**General Information**
DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.

jobs.description:
We are currently recruiting a **Global Awards & Donor Compliance Manager** to join our **Awards Management** team.

This is a **remote, 12-month position** open to candidates based in the following Relief International countries of operation: **Kenya, Türkiye, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Palestine and Pakistan.**

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring standard pre-employment checks.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. We work in countries across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, providing Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

**About the Opportunity**

The Global Awards and Donor Compliance Manager is a senior technical leadership role within Relief International's Awards Management Unit, responsible for strengthening award management, donor compliance and partnership management across a portfolio of complex humanitarian and development programmes.

This role serves as a key focal point between Relief International's country offices, programme teams and global support functions, ensuring that donor-funded projects are managed effectively throughout the entire award lifecycle. From proposal development and award negotiation through implementation, modification, reporting and close-out, you will provide strategic guidance that helps country teams navigate donor requirements while maintaining programme quality and operational effectiveness.

You will work closely with Country Directors, Awards Leads, Programme Teams, Finance, Partnerships and senior leadership to strengthen systems, improve compliance standards and build organizational capacity. The role also acts as a key advisor on donor regulations, partnership management, audit readiness, risk mitigation and award performance across Relief International's global portfolio.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced awards and compliance professional who enjoys solving complex challenges, building organizational capability and influencing programme performance at a global level.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- **Lead and support the management of donor-funded awards and contracts** throughout the full award lifecycle, from proposal review and award negotiations through implementation, modifications and close-out.
- **Provide strategic guidance on donor compliance requirements**, award risks, donor regulations and organizational policies across Relief International's country programmes.
- **Participate in Go/No-Go reviews**, proposal development processes and donor agreement reviews, ensuring strong compliance, risk mitigation and quality assurance.
- **Monitor country office performance** against awards management standards and KPIs, identifying risks and supporting corrective actions where required.
- **Strengthen donor reporting quality** by reviewing reporting frameworks, supporting compliance reviews and contributing to donor communication processes.
- **Provide technical oversight on partnership management processes**, including due diligence, partnership agreements, sub-awards and localization approaches.
- **Support audit readiness**, award close-out processes and implementation of lessons learned to strengthen organizational performance and compliance.
- **Lead the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives**, training and guidance for Country Office teams on awards management, donor compliance and partnership management.
- **Maintain and strengthen awards tracking systems**, dashboards, compliance matrices and knowledge management tools to support decision-making and portfolio oversight.
- **Act as a senior representative for Awards Management**, engaging with donors, partners and external stakeholders on compliance, partnership management and awards-related best practices.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- Master's degree or equivalent advanced qualification in a relevant field.
- Significant manager level experience in awards management, grants management, donor compliance and partnership management within an international NGO or similar international organization.
- Strong knowledge of major institutional donors, including US Government donors, European donors, foundations and other international funding agencies.
- Demonstrated experience managing complex donor-funded portfolios and ensuring compliance throughout the award lifecycle.
- Experience reviewing proposal budgets, donor agreements, reporting requirements and compliance frameworks.
- Strong understanding of partnership management, due diligence processes, sub-awards and donor requirements related to localization and partnerships.
- Proven experience using grants management systems, databases and reporting tools. Experience with NetSuite is highly desirable.
- Excellent English writing, editing and communication skills, with the ability to produce and review high-quality donor-facing documentation.
- Strong analytical, organizational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience working in developing countries and knowledge of internal controls, fraud prevention, investigations and safeguarding principles would be an advantage. Arabic or French language skills are also desirable.

jobs.description:
**Job title: Individual Consultant – Needs Assessment, Coordination and Implementation Support System Transformation Grant (STG)**

Type of contract: Consultant Contract

Level: Level 2 - Middle

Hiring Unit: Education Sector (ED)

Duty Station: Project Antenna Office in Yangon, Myanmar
Work location: On-site

Duration of contract: 11 months

Hiring open to: External candidates

Application deadline: 04 November 2026 17:00 Hours Yangon time (UTC+6:30 Time)

**UNESCO Core Values: Commitment to the Organization, Integrity, Respect for Diversity, Professionalism**

## OVERVIEW OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THE POST

1. ## BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE

Under the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) System Transformation Grant (STG), UNESCO Project Antenna Office in Yangon (hereafter called UNESCO) is implementing activities aimed at ensuring that children across Myanmar, including those facing barriers to learning, have access to quality, inclusive education in safe and protective learning spaces, supported by strong community and partner engagement, as well as targeted evidence generation and dissemination. The programme aligns closely with the current Joint Response Framework for Education in Myanmar II (JRF II), ensuring a coordinated and strategic approach to addressing the educational needs of children aged 3–18 years across basic and secondary education. STG is organized around three key drivers of learning:

1. Access: Ensuring safe and equitable access to learning for all children and youth
2. Quality: Strengthening quality teaching and learning through improved resources and capacity building
3. System Strengthening: Enhancing education system management, coordination, and monitoring

## 1. PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The programme prioritizes reaching out-of-learning children and youth (OOLCY), standardizing education data, and ensuring safe, inclusive learning environments. To ensure efficient, optimal, and timely delivery of activities on the ground, UNESCO is seeking an Individual Consultant to provide technical and analytical support for engagement and coordination with current and future implementation partners. This will involve needs assessments, close programme coordination and monitoring, and technical and institutional support to smoothen programme implementation. Based on information and knowledge collected from the ground, the consultant will also contribute to UNESCO’s resource mobilization and proposal development efforts, including support to funding proposals, concept notes, and technical documentation being developed by the education team. The consultant should have demonstrated experience in education programme coordination, partnership engagement and dialogues, and education systems strengthening.

## 2. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

### Supervisory arrangements:

Under the overall authority of the Director of the UNESCO Regional Office in Bangkok and Office for UN Coordination in Asia and the Pacific, the direct supervision of the Head of the UNESCO Project Antenna Office in Yangon and in close collaboration with the Education programme team, the individual consultant will provide technical guidance and analytical support, under UNESCO’s direction, to carry out the following tasks:

- **Planning and Integrating UNESCO frameworks:** Ensure that the implementing partners understand and apply UNESCO frameworks, standards, and tools in the most impactful, impactful and sustainable ways in their implementation of STG activities on the grounds. This involves efficient planning, preparation, and regular check-ins and monitoring of the implementing partners’ efficiency and compliance, while anticipating risks and challenges of implementation across access, quality and systems strengthening.
- **Partner engagement and coordination:** Liaise with UNESCO’s implementing partners, to ensure effective coordination and communication throughout programme implementation, including developing the annual work plan, updating the implementation plan, performing quality control, document review and translation. This includes organizing coordination and technical meetings, preparing meeting notes or minutes, supporting joint planning and review sessions, and coordination and communication with the STG programmes’ focal points of other Grant Agents, school management committees, youth networks, and community representatives, to gather and check information.
- **Need Assessments and Systems Strengthening:** Undertake targeted assessments, mapping and analysis, as appropriate, to strengthen UNESCO’s independent understanding of context, capacities, risks and emerging needs, complementing and triangulating information provided by implementing partners and other sources. Provide technical input to education system strengthening interventions under the STG and future education programmes, including partner capacity strengthening, disaster risk reduction, preparedness and contingency planning, and knowledge management.
- **Facilitation:** Facilitate consultations, learning events and review meetings with implementing partners to strengthen coordination, promote learning and knowledge sharing, review implementation progress, and identify opportunities to improve programme quality and effectiveness.
- **Resource Mobilization and Proposal Development:** Support the development of new education programme proposals and resource mobilization efforts, including coordinating stakeholder consultations, conducting situation analyses and rapid assessments, preparing technical inputs, drafting and reviewing concept notes and proposals, and compiling supporting evidence and documentation.
- **Translation and interpretation:** Provide Myanmar-English-Myanmar technical translation and interpretation for meetings and reporting as needed.

In line with UNESCO’s overall gender mainstreaming strategy, the Individual Specialist is expected to integrate a gender perspective in all activities and apply gender mainstreaming concepts whenever feasible.

### Location and Travel:

The Individual Specialist will be based in UNESCO Project Antenna Office in Yangon, Myanmar during the contract period. No travel outside of Yangon is anticipated.

## 3. TIMETABLE AND DELIVERABLES

### Deliverables

The individual specialist will submit the following deliverables within the designated timeline. All deliverables must be submitted with original, editable files, as well as high-resolution versions of final products (if applicable) to UNESCO. The assigned tasks must be submitted by the following deadlines.

**Assignment period:** From 1 December 2026 to 30 October 2027.

1. Inception Report and Partner Engagement Plan, including: (i) understanding of the assignment; (ii) detailed methodology and work plan; (iii) mapping of implementing partners and other relevant education stakeholders; (iv) proposed consultation and information-validation arrangements; (v) preliminary implementation risks and assumptions; and (vi) schedule of consultations, assessments, learning events and technical outputs by 31 December 2026.
2. Mid-year Learning and Partner Review Workshop Package, including: (i) concept note and detailed agenda; (ii) stakeholder and participant mapping; (iii) facilitation methodology; (iv) key discussion and review questions; (v) presentation and working materials; (vi) framework for documenting lessons learned, good practices and recommendations; and (vii) expected outputs and follow-up actions by 29 January 2027.
3. Implementing-Partner Needs and Capacity Assessment, covering Rakhine, Sagaing or other state/region to be identified, including: (i) assessment methodology and tools; (ii) stakeholder consultations; (iii) beneficiaries to be engaged (iv) analysis of implementation capacities, priority needs, operational constraints and risks; (v) triangulation of information from relevant sources; and (vi) practical recommendations for partner support and programme implementation. Education System-Strengthening Technical Note assessing key challenges, practical recommendations and partner’s potential approaches to strengthening school-level governance, partner capacity, education-data management, disaster risk reduction and preparedness, and safe, inclusive and continuous learning in targeted programme areas, informed by and reviewed against the outcomes of the joint UNESCO and UNESCO-IIEP workshopby 26 February 2027.
4. Technical Review of Partner Implementation Arrangements, including an evidence-based analysis of: (i) alignment with relevant UNESCO frameworks, standards and tools; (ii) implementation progress and bottlenecks; (iii) quality and completeness of selected partner planning and reporting documents; (iv) emerging compliance and delivery risks; and (v) prioritized corrective and follow-up recommendations for UNESCO’s consideration by 31 March 2027.
5. Implementation Quality and Risk Review, including: (i) consolidated analysis of progress against agreed activities and milestones; (ii) review of selected partner deliverables; (iii) updated risk-and-mitigation register; (iv) unresolved issues and required decisions; (v) sustainability and transition considerations; and (vi) prioritized recommendations for the remaining implementation period by 30 April 2027.
6. Situation Analysis and Resource-Mobilization Package, including: (i) an updated situation analysis based on available programme evidence and stakeholder consultations; (ii) identification of priority education needs and potential programme responses; (iii) technical inputs to at least one concept note, funding proposal or resource-mobilization opportunity identified by UNESCO; and (iv) a supporting evidence and document package by 31 May 2027.
7. Partner Capacity-Strengthening and Knowledge-Sharing Package, including: (i) capacity-strengthening priorities derived from the needs assessment and implementation review; (ii) session plans or technical guidance materials; (iii) materials delivered or shared with implementing partners; (iv) anonymized feedback from beneficiaries on project interventions, where collected; and (v) recommended follow-up support by 30 June 2027.
8. Partner Coordination and Implementation Monitoring Report, including: (i) summary of coordination meetings and technical consultations with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders; (ii) consolidated tracking of implementation progress against agreed work plans and milestones; (iii) documentation of remote monitoring, observations and implementation challenges, where undertaken; (iv) follow-up actions and status of outstanding issues; (v) updates on emerging operational risks and mitigation measures; and (vi) prioritized recommendations to support timely, coordinated and quality closure of STG activities by 30 July 2027.
9. End-of-Project Learning and Partner Review Workshop Package, including: (i) concept note and detailed agenda; (ii) stakeholder and participant mapping; (iii) facilitation methodology; (iv) key discussion and review questions; (v) presentation and working materials; (vi) framework for documenting lessons learned, good practices and recommendations; and (vii) expected outputs and follow-up actions by 31 August 2027.
10. Future Programming and Resource-Mobilization Package, including: (i) synthesis of evidence and lessons relevant to future programming; (ii) priority interventions and indicative results; (iii) sustainability considerations; (iv) technical inputs to a concept note, proposal or other programme-development document identified by UNESCO; and (v) recommendations for future partnerships and resource-mobilization opportunities by 30 September 2027.
11. Final Technical Synthesis and Transition Package, including: (i) consolidated analysis of UNESCO’s achievements against the STG Joint Results Framework, including relevant data visualizations; (ii) status of partner deliverables and agreed follow-up actions; (iii) final risk-and-outstanding-issues register; (iv) synthesis of lessons learned and good practices; (v) project close-out, sustainability and transition considerations; (vi) recommendations for future programming and partner engagement; and (vii) an organized handover package containing final editable versions of the tools, analyses, technical notes and materials developed under the assignment by 30 October 2027.

### COMPETENCIES (Core / Managerial)

### Accountability (C)

### Communication (C)

### Innovation (C)

### Knowledge sharing and continuous improvement (C)

### Planning and organizing (C)

### Teamwork (C)

### Results focus (C)

For detailed information, please consult the [UNESCO Competency Framework](https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000245056?posInSet=9&queryId=bcd2a5ea-9a90-4938-88c1-3f56099f4201)

## 5. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

**Education**

- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in education, public policy, international development, economics, social sciences or a related field.

A first-level university degree in one of the above or a related field, combined with at least seven (7) additional years of relevant professional experience beyond the minimum experience requirement, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

**Work Experience**

- Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in education programme management, implementation monitoring, need assessment, education-system strengthening and/or programme development, partner engagement and/or programme coordination, preferably in crisis-affected or conflict contexts.
- Familiarity with the education development context in Myanmar including working with community, monastic or ethnic education providers.
- Demonstrated experience conducting qualitative and/or quantitative assessments, analysing information from multiple sources and translating findings into practical recommendations, implementation plans or technical proposals.
- Demonstrated experience providing technical advice, guidance or analytical support to education stakeholders, implementing partners, civil society organizations, United Nations entities or international development organizations.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Strong understanding of the roles, needs and perspectives of diverse education stakeholders, including teachers, parents and implementing partners.
- Strong analytical and research skills, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, and risks analysis in a context of conflicts.

**Languages**

- Excellent written and spoken English and Myanmar-language skills, including the ability to prepare technical documents in English and provide accurate Myanmar-English-Myanmar interpretation and translation.

## **6. DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS**

**Work Experience**

- Experience in education programming in Myanmar, including engagement with community-based, monastic and/or ethnic education providers.
- Experience working with Civil Society Organizations (CSO) and /or other United Nations entities and International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) or education-development partners.
- Experience contributing to concept notes, funding proposals or resource-mobilization documentation.
- Experience working in crisis-affected, conflict-sensitive or emergency education contexts.

**Skills and Competencies**
- Experience using software packages such as Kobo Toolbox, Power BI or Excel
