jobs.title: Business Development Director
jobs.description:
CARE International in Papua New Guinea is seeking a Business Development Director to lead and strengthen our business development and resource mobilisation function.

CARE is an international development and humanitarian organisation working to fight poverty and support lasting change, with a strong focus on women and girls. In Papua New Guinea, CARE works across areas including gender equality, disaster risk reduction, climate change adaption, agriculture and health.

**About the Role**

The Business Development Director will provide strategic and operational leadership to grow CARE PNG’s funding portfolio, strengthen donor and partner engagement, and improve systems for identifying, shaping and securing high-quality funding opportunities. The role will also support the transfer of business development skills and knowledge to national staff.

This is an opportunity to contribute to lasting change in Papua New Guinea through a locally recruited role based in Port Moresby. The remuneration package does not include housing or additional expatriate benefits

**Key Responsibilities**

- Lead CARE PNG’s business development and resource mobilisation strategy.
- Manage a live funding pipeline and provide strategic advice to senior management.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, partners and key stakeholders.
- Lead proposal development processes, including concept notes, technical proposals, budgets and compliance reviews.
- Strengthen business development systems, tools, workflows and knowledge management.
- Coach and mentor staff to build long-term business development capability within CARE PNG.
- Promote CARE’s values, safeguarding commitments and ethical partnership principles.

**About You**

The successful candidate will have senior-level experience in business development, resource mobilisation and institutional fundraising, with a strong record of leading successful donor proposals. You will be a strategic thinker, a strong communicator and a collaborative leader who can work effectively across teams and cultures.

**Essential Requirements**

- Advanced university degree in International Development, Humanitarian Studies, Public Policy, Business, International Relations or a related field.
- At least 10 years of relevant experience in international development and/or humanitarian programs.
- Significant experience in business development, donor engagement, proposal writing and compliance.
- Experience working with institutional donors such as DFAT, EU, UN agencies, ADB, World Bank, USAID or similar donors.
- Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
- Experience in mentoring and couching

**Location**

This position is expected to be based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, with travel within PNG and occasional international travel as required.

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, + Learning (MEL) Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Reports to:** MEL + Data Quality Manager
**Department:** Compassionate Carbon Tanzania - Monitoring, Evaluation + Learning
**Position classification:** Full-time
**Location:** Lumuma, Kilosa District / Mbuga, Mpwapwa District
**Employment type:** Full-time **(note: visa sponsorship not available for this position)**

**COMPANY INFORMATION**
Compassionate Carbon Tanzania Ltd is a mission-driven organization launched by Compassionate Carbon LLC and Eden: People+Planet (Eden). Specializing in developing and implementing landscape-scale forest carbon projects through Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+), we collaborate with local communities to restore landscapes, create jobs, protect ecosystems, and mitigate climate change.

Our projects integrate nature-based solutions to help meet global emissions targets while ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability. The Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project, a significant initiative in Tanzania, focuses on native forest restoration and community-based conservation efforts.

**POSITION SUMMARY**
The Monitoring, Evaluation + Learning (MEL) Coordinator connects field implementation with the information needed to understand progress, learn, and improve. Working across Compassionate Carbon Tanzania’s Forest Protection, Livelihoods, Forst Restoration and Community/Stakeholder Engagement workstreams, the Coordinator strengthens practical monitoring systems, builds the capacity of field teams and community-based data collectors, and ensures that monitoring information is collected consistently and maintained to appropriate quality standards. The role works closely with the MEL + Data Quality Manager and Program Managers to identify trends and gaps, inform program decisions, strengthen implementation, and contribute to reliable reporting and carbon-standard verification.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITES**

- **Data Collection Tools + Systems:** Develop, adapt, and maintain practical monitoring tools, forms, guidelines, and SOPs across Forest Protection, Livelihoods, Forest Restoration, and Community/Stakeholder Engagement functions. Maintain organized, secure, traceable, and audit-ready monitoring records and support effective use of EarthRanger and other data collection systems.
- **Program Data Coordination:** Coordinate monthly and quarterly data collection with Program Managers, field teams, and community-based data collectors. Ensure monitoring data across programs, including surveys and field monitoring activities, are collected completely, consistently, on time, and in alignment with standards.
- **Data Quality Assurance:** Conduct routine QA/QC, including completeness and validation checks, spot checks, and field verification to ensure that data meets Equitable Earth standards. Identify and resolve data gaps or inconsistencies with Program Managers and data collectors and ensure established data standards and procedures are consistently followed.
- **Data Analysis + Reporting:** Clean, compile, summarize, and conduct routine analysis of monitoring data to identify progress, trends, gaps, and data-quality concerns. Prepare clear monitoring summaries and contribute verified data and documentation to project reporting, learning reviews, and carbon-standard verification.
- **Training + Capacity Building:** Develop practical training materials appropriate to field and community contexts. Train and coach field staff, enumerators, community-based data collectors, and other relevant stakeholders on monitoring procedures, tools, data-quality expectations, and ethical data collection. Revise training materials as needed to address training gaps or quality issues.
- **Collaboration + Stakeholder Coordination:** Work closely with the MRV + Data Quality Manager, Program Managers, field teams, communities, and relevant government stakeholders to integrate monitoring into field activities, coordinate data collection, address monitoring gaps, and communicate relevant findings.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- A Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Forestry, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, or a related field
- At least 3 years of relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation, field data collection, or data management.
- Prior experience working in natural resources, conservation, forestry, agriculture, or other rural development projects is preferred.
- Demonstrated experience with field-based monitoring and data collection, including coordinating or supervising enumerators, data clerks, community-based data collectors, or field teams.
- Experience training and supporting community members and field teams in data collection methods, tools, and data-quality requirements.
- Hands-on experience developing and using digital data collection tools, such as KoBoToolbox, ODK, Survey123, or similar platforms.
- Experience with data management and quality assurance, including data cleaning, validation, routine analysis, and preparation of monitoring summaries or reports.
- Additional professional training or certification in Monitoring + Evaluation is an advantage.
- Familiarity with EarthRanger, SMART, GIS tools such as QGIS, forest carbon projects, or carbon standards such as Equitable Earth or Verra is an advantage but not required..

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Monitoring + Evaluation:** Good understanding of monitoring and evaluation concepts, including indicators, baselines, data quality, results tracking, data collection methodologies, and learning from monitoring information.
- **Data Management + Analysis:** Strong analytical and data-management skills, including the ability to clean, organize, summarize, interpret, and present monitoring data and identify trends, gaps, and data-quality issues.
- **Data Collection Systems:** Ability to develop practical, user-friendly data collection tools and explain their use clearly to people with different levels of technical experience or formal education.
- **Quality Assurance:** Strong attention to detail and ability to apply defined QA/QC procedures consistently, identify errors and inconsistencies, and work constructively with teams to resolve data-quality issues.
- **Training + Facilitation:** Strong training and facilitation skills, with patience, humility, and respect when working with rural communities and community-based data collectors.
- **Communication + Writing:** Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare monitoring summaries, guidelines, SOPs, training materials, and supporting documentation for internal and external reporting.
- **Organization + Coordination:** Strong organizational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage monitoring activities across several programs, field teams, and locations while meeting competing deadlines.
- **Collaboration:** Ability to work independently in field settings while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary project teams, community stakeholders, and government counterparts.
- **Technology:** Proficient in Microsoft Office, including Excel for organizing, checking, summarizing, and analyzing monitoring data, and comfort using smartphones, tablets, GPS devices, and digital data collection systems.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** Combination of office and field settings, including regular visits to forested and rural project sites under varied weather and terrain conditions. Frequent interaction with local communities and multi-stakeholder teams may involve basic field accommodations and extended time in remote areas.
- **Work Schedule:** Full-time, with standard office hours, requiring occasional flexibility (e.g. early mornings, evenings, or weekends).
- **Physical Requirements:** Moderate physical fitness is required for fieldwork in rustic environments, including walking long distances on uneven terrain, standing for extended periods, Must be comfortable in challenging field conditions. Work also involves typical office tasks (computer use, meetings) when not in the field.
- **Travel:** Regular domestic travel within Tanzania to remote project sites for monitoring and community consultation, sometimes involving difficult travel conditions and overnight stays.
- **Safety + Special Conditions:** Adherence to all applicable safety protocols and alignment of activities with established environmental and social safeguards. **Visa sponsorship is not available for this position; only Tanzanian nationals will be considered.**

The Field Extension Officer brings Compassionate Carbon Tanzania’s sustainable livelihood activities directly to farmers and communities, translating approved technical approaches into practical, farm-level support. Reporting to the Sustainable Livelihood Program Coordinator, the Officer provides farmer training, demonstrations, regular farm visits, and follow-up to support adoption of Climate-Smart Agriculture practices, with an initial focus on Conservation Agriculture. As a frontline representative of the program, the Officer works closely with farmers, Lead Farmers, community stakeholders, and government extension personnel while monitoring field progress, maintaining accurate records, and communicating implementation challenges and feedback.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

Conduct regular farm visits, support farmers and Lead Farmers throughout the production cycle, and assist with approved Agroforestry, Quality Declared Seed, seed security, and other livelihood activities as introduced.
- **Farmer Training + Demonstration:** Mobilize participating farmers and support Farmer Groups and program learning structures. Facilitate Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, practical training sessions, farmer exchanges, field days, and other community learning activities. Work with Lead Farmers to strengthen farmer-to-farmer learning and translate approved technical recommendations into clear, practical guidance.

Coordinate local field activities, promote meaningful participation, document community feedback, and promptly report technical, operational, environmental, safeguarding, or community-level concerns through established channels.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Diploma or bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agroforestry, Agricultural Extension, Rural Development, or a closely related field.

- Experience using KoboCollect, ODK, or similar digital data-collection platforms is an advantage.

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Agricultural Extension:** Able to explain and demonstrate approved agricultural practices clearly and practically to farmers and provide reliable follow-up in the field.
- **Farmer Training + Facilitation:** Strong participatory training, facilitation, and community-mobilization skills, with the ability to work respectfully with farmers and community-based groups.
- **Field Monitoring + Documentation:** Strong attention to detail and the ability to collect accurate information, maintain organized records, document observations and feedback, and submit timely reports.

- **Language:** Able to communicate effectively in Kiswahili; knowledge of languages commonly used within the project area is an advantage.
- **Field Readiness:** Able to work independently within approved plans, travel regularly, and spend substantial time in rural communities and farmers’ fields.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** The position is primarily field-based, with regular work in rural communities, farms, Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, and other project sites. Work may involve basic facilities and exposure to heat, rain, dust, and varied terrain.

Our projects integrate nature-based solutions to help meet global emissions targets while ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability. The Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project, a significant initiative in Tanzania, focuses on native forest restoration and community-based conservation efforts.

**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Sustainable Livelihood Programme Coordinator is the key operational link between program plans and effective delivery in the field, ensuring that livelihood activities translate into well-coordinated, high-quality support for participating farmers and communities. Reporting to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager, the Coordinator oversees day-to-day field implementation, supervises Field Extension Officers, and coordinates farmer mobilization, training, demonstrations, and follow-up across project communities. The role monitors progress and implementation quality, identifies and helps resolve field-level challenges, and brings forward practical insights and recommendations to strengthen delivery. Working closely with field teams, communities, government extension personnel, and other local stakeholders, the Coordinator helps ensure approved livelihood approaches are implemented consistently, responsively, and in line with program targets, technical guidance, and available resources.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Program Implementation + Coordination**: Translate approved workplans into weekly and monthly field schedules and coordinate farmer mobilization, training, demonstrations, farm follow-up, and other livelihood activities. Track delivery against targets, timelines, technical guidance, and approved budgets; coordinate field logistics and support agreed program adaptations.
- **Field Team Supervision**: Provide day-to-day supervision and coordination of Field Extension Officers, review field plans, conduct regular supervision visits, and provide practical support in resolving implementation challenges. Ensure field staff maintain accurate records and submit complete reports on time, escalating significant capacity, performance, technical, or operational concerns to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager.
- **Implementation Monitoring + Reporting:** Track implementation progress, verify field records, consolidate weekly and monthly reports, and provide timely updates to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager. Identify delays, emerging risks, operational constraints, and areas requiring corrective action. Support assessments, evaluations, learning activities, and partner or donor field visits.
**Stakeholder + Community Coordination:** Coordinate field-level engagement with village governments, government agricultural extension personnel, Lead Farmers, service providers, participating communities, and other relevant stakeholders in support of program implementation. Maintain effective communication among program management, field teams, and communities and ensure concerns, feedback, and implementation issues are documented and escalated appropriately.
- **Program Quality + Continuous Improvement:** Ensure field activities follow approved program approaches and technical guidance, including Climate-Smart Agriculture, Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, and participatory farmer training. Use field observations, monitoring information, and stakeholder feedback to identify implementation issues and recommend practical improvements to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager, supporting agreed corrective actions and program adaptations.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agroforestry, Rural Development, Agricultural Extension, Project Management, or another relevant field.
- Relevant experience coordinating agricultural, livelihood, rural development, or smallholder farmer programs, including translating workplans into field implementation.
- Demonstrated experience supervising or coordinating field-based teams and supporting staff to plan, deliver, document, and report on activities.
- Practical knowledge of Climate-Smart Agriculture, particularly Conservation Agriculture and Agroforestry, and an understanding of smallholder farming systems, agricultural extension approaches, farmer organization, and participatory farmer training.
- Experience coordinating activities with rural communities, local government, agricultural extension personnel, service providers, or similar stakeholders.
- Experience tracking implementation progress, coordinating multiple field activities, and preparing clear, timely reports.
- Familiarity with Quality Declared Seed, community seed systems, seed security interventions, or digital field-data systems such as KoboCollect or ODK is an advantage.
- Experience coordinating programs across multiple villages or geographically dispersed communities is an advantage.

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Program Coordination:** Strong ability to organize field implementation, coordinate multiple activities, manage competing priorities, and maintain progress against workplans, targets, and timelines.
- **Team Supervision:** Able to provide clear direction, practical coaching, and effective day-to-day supervision to field-based staff.
- **Technical Knowledge:** Good understanding of smallholder agriculture, Climate-Smart Agriculture, Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, agricultural extension, and participatory farmer training, with the ability to support consistent field implementation of approved approaches.
- **Monitoring + Reporting:** Able to track implementation, verify field records, identify delivery gaps or risks, and prepare clear and accurate program updates and reports.
- **Stakeholder Engagement:** Strong facilitation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work respectfully with farmers, communities, government representatives, service providers, and project colleagues.
- **Problem Solving + Adaptability:** Practical and solution-oriented, with the ability to respond constructively to field constraints and support appropriate program adaptations.
- **Communication:** Strong spoken and written Kiswahili and working proficiency in English.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** Combination of office and field settings, including regular visits to forested and rural project sites under varied weather and terrain conditions. Frequent interaction with local communities and multi-stakeholder teams may involve basic field accommodations and extended time in remote areas.
- **Work schedule:** Full-time, with standard office hours, requiring occasional flexibility (e.g. early mornings, evenings, or weekends) to accommodate field requirements.
- **Physical Requirements:** Moderate physical fitness is required for fieldwork in rustic environments, including walking long distances on uneven terrain, standing for extended periods, Must be comfortable in challenging field conditions. Work also involves typical office tasks (computer use, meetings) when not in the field.
- **Travel:** Regular domestic travel within Tanzania to remote project sites for monitoring and community consultation, sometimes involving difficult travel conditions and overnight stays.
- **Safety + Special Conditions:** Adherence to all applicable safety protocols and alignment of activities with established environmental and social safeguards. **Visa sponsorship is not available for this position; only Tanzanian nationals will be considered.**

**Disclaimer:** This document outlines primary duties but may not cover all responsibilities or conditions. Compassionate Carbon may assign extra tasks or modify roles for business needs or employee accommodation, per applicable law.

Compassionate Carbon is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team representing a variety of backgrounds, viewpoints, and skills. Candidate selection is based on technical qualifications and position requirements; employment will not commence until applicable background and reference checks are completed.

**Safeguarding:** Compassionate Carbon holds strict safeguarding principles and does not tolerate behaviors that harm others, including sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, and other injustices. Employees are expected to abide by company policies.

**Compensation:** Compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. Compassionate Carbon provides a competitive benefits package including annual leave, health insurance, and contributions to statutory funds.

jobs.title: Regional Logistician & Administrative Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Mennonite Central Committee (MCC)** is a worldwide ministry of Anabaptist churches, that shares God’s love and compassion for all in the name of Christ by responding to basic human needs and working for peace and justice. MCC envisions communities worldwide in right relationship with God, one another and creation.

**Position Title:** Regional Logistician & Administrative Coordinator
**Reporting to:** Area Directors for East Africa & Sahel
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya
**Employment Type:** One-year renewable contract

**Annual Gross Salary:** KES 1,861,524 - 2,047,676, commensurate with experience and within the established salary band
**Start Date:** Tentatively 15 January 2026

**Job Synopsis:**

The Regional Logistician & Administrative Coordinator manages the logistical, administrative, and communication operations of the Area Directors' office, working closely with the six country program offices in the East Africa & Sahel region. The role coordinates travel, accommodation, transportation, medical support, and other logistics for regional staff visiting Kenya for meetings, medical care, training, or site visits, and oversees the regional apartment, including guest bookings and hospitality arrangements.

The position serves as a key coordination point for the Area Directors by supporting correspondence management, procurement of goods and services, and the organization of regional meetings and events. The role also supports regional finance operations by assisting with invoice processing, payment tracking, maintaining financial records and supporting documentation, contributing to budget monitoring and reconciliations, and preparing finance-related reports and audit documentation in collaboration with the Regional Finance Coordinator.

**Responsibilities:**

**Regional Coordination**

- Plan and organize the logistics for the annual YAMEN Orientation for all global YAMENers; identify the venue, serve as the main point of contact, ensure all participants arrive and depart well, and work with CPCs to ensure participants' needs are met.
- Organize and coordinate regional events such as orientations, Rep Gatherings, and meetings, including logistical arrangements and venue bookings.
- Manage Regional Board meetings, ensuring the board meets as required, bringing items to the agenda, tracking action items and outcomes, and coordinating any required follow-up.
- Accompany donors on country visits when Area Directors are unavailable, ensuring the country office is prepared and all details are handled.
- Represent the Area Directors in-country when needed, especially during times of office transition, serving as a listening ear, observing operations, and providing feedback to the Area Directors on how systems can be improved.

**Logistics & Communication**

- Facilitate the scheduling of travel and meetings for the Area Directors, identifying important upcoming events and overseeing necessary preparations.
- Arrange transportation, accommodation, and other travel logistics for the Area Directors, ensuring smooth and efficient travel experiences and maintaining regular communication throughout.
- Manage the Regional Apartment, maintaining a schedule of visitors and coordinating cooking and cleaning arrangements for guests as needed.
- Communicate with hotels and other service providers to confirm reservations and address any concerns or challenges that may arise.
- Maintain smooth communication between the Area Directors and relevant stakeholders.
- Organize meetings (in person and virtually) as required by the Area Directors, including coordinating logistics, preparing and distributing meeting materials, and recording and distributing minutes.
- Work with the Area Directors to connect and resource MCC's Africa program offices, including maintaining current program resource materials, procedural manuals, and related documentation.
- Collaborate with planning committees to ensure the successful execution of events while adhering to timelines and budgets.
- Support the preparation of reports, presentations, and other documents through formatting, proofreading, and translation between English and French.
- Assist in managing databases and information systems, ensuring data integrity and accessibility for relevant stakeholders.
- Monitor incoming communications and prioritize urgent messages or requests requiring the Area Directors' attention.
- Relay important information promptly and accurately to ensure timely response and action.
- Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Area Directors and diverse stakeholders, including government officials, public entities, and community members.
- Provide cultural insights and guidance to enhance interactions and relationships in multicultural settings.
- Identify areas for process improvement in logistical and communication support services and propose innovative solutions to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.
- Seek feedback from stakeholders and incorporate suggestions for optimizing support mechanisms.
- Uphold professional standards in all communications and interactions, representing MCC in a positive and professional manner.
- Represent the region on various committees and working groups.

**Planning, Learning, and Disaster Response (PLDR) Collaboration**

- Assist with reporting requirements for the Planning, Learning, and Disaster Response (PLDR) Department, Communications, and other parts of the MCC system.
- Obtain quotations from consultants conducting country program reviews and work with HR to maintain and update the consultant pool.
- Compile Annual Plans and Annual Reports for review by the Area Directors.
- Track projects across the East Africa & Sahel region, maintaining a database of ongoing projects and working closely with the Area Directors to identify projects nearing completion and support renewal planning.

**Regional Connecting People's Coordination**

- Communicate logistics for YAMEN Orientation and Re-entry, ensuring participants have the required visas, are aware of travel requirements, and receive the necessary logistical support.
- Identify the needs of different YAMEN cohorts while in service, including follow-up training sessions, and coordinate such trainings with MCC staff and external service providers or counsellors. Review qualifications and rates and share recommendations with the Area Directors for approval.
- Handle confidential information with discretion and ensure compliance with data protection regulations and organizational policies.
- Support CPCs and Representatives in ensuring policies are implemented fairly and consistently. Assist with policy interpretation for workers in consultation with Representatives, Human Resources, and relevant program coordinators.
- Connect with alumni to generate interest for GSL applicants, especially in countries where there is no MCC office.

**Administrative Support**

- Manage administrative tasks, including Microsoft Office administration, filing, invoice processing, expense claims, report preparation, and financial documentation related to the Area Directors' activities.
- Support communication and information sharing with English- and French-speaking stakeholders through interpretation, translation, or coordination of language support as needed.
- Assist with managing shared regional documents and ensure they are readily accessible when needed.
- Maintain organized filing systems for documents, reports, and other administrative records, both electronically and in hard copy.
- Assist the EAS HR Coordinator and Country Representatives with talent acquisition activities as needed.

**Finance Support**

- Support finance and accounting activities under the guidance of the Regional Finance Coordinator.
- Assist with invoice processing, payment tracking, and maintaining supporting documentation.
- Maintain accurate financial records, filing systems, and document retention processes.
- Support budget monitoring, expenditure tracking, and account reconciliations as assigned.
- Assist with finance-related reporting, audit preparation, and compliance documentation.
- Coordinate with vendors, staff, and finance personnel to ensure timely processing of payments and resolution of finance-related queries.
- Perform any other duties and responsibilities as may be assigned from time to time within the scope of the role.

**Qualifications:**

All MCC workers are expected to exhibit a commitment to a personal Christian faith and discipleship; active church membership; and nonviolent peacemaking.

An invitation to an assignment is contingent on the successful completion of a criminal background check.

**Required Qualifications**

- Legally eligible to work in Kenya
- Bachelor's degree or diploma in Project Management, Business Administration, Education, Commerce, Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
- Minimum of three (3) years' experience in administration, logistics, office operations, finance support, or a related role, preferably within an international non-governmental organization (INGO).
- Fluent in English, with excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to foster positive relationships and open communication both in person and electronically.
- Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact confidently and effectively with diverse stakeholders, including international individuals, government officials, vendors, and members of the public.
- Ability to represent MCC in a professional and welcoming manner.
- Highly organized, with proficiency in narrative documentation, data entry, spreadsheets, Microsoft Office applications, and PowerPoint presentations.
- Ability to work independently, proactively resolve issues, and handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion.
- Open to feedback, adaptable, and committed to continuous learning.
- Willing and available to work overtime, particularly before and during meetings and events.
- Willing and able to travel locally and internationally as required.
- Strong relational skills, including the ability to build and maintain positive working relationships, collaborate effectively with MCC teams and partners, and mentor young adults.
- Demonstrated cross-cultural awareness and competence, with the ability to support cross-cultural adaptation and engagement.
- Ability to provide worker care by demonstrating empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and encouraging healthy self-care practices among participants.
- Ability to work effectively in diverse and changing situations and to respond appropriately to participant emergencies with support from the Area Directors.
- Strong planning, coordination, and organizational skills, ensuring efficient use of resources and timely achievement of objectives.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- French language skills, including the ability to communicate, translate, and interpret in professional settings.
- CPA Part I-III or equivalent accounting training.
- Experience supporting regional or multi-country operations.
- Experience coordinating regional events, travel arrangements, and international logistics.

jobs.title: Consultancy: Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (Protection, Education, MHPSS)
jobs.description:
## 1. Background and rationale

Educo is a Spanish child rights organisation working in education and child protection. It has been present in Lebanon since 2025, most recently with a remedial education and psychosocial support project in Bar Elias (West Bekaa), implemented with a local partner and moved online during the 2026 escalation.

Educo intends to apply to DG ECHO under the forthcoming Humanitarian Implementation Plan (HIP) for Lebanon. ECHO requires applicants to justify every action with a recent, evidence-based needs assessment, a clear response analysis and a credible targeting strategy. Existing sources (MSNA, sector dashboards, response plan documents) are national in scope and do not capture the situation of Educo's specific target areas and groups. These sources serve as the baseline (secondary review); this assessment adds education in emergencies and child protection depth, local granularity and response analysis. Educo therefore seeks a consultant to generate and analyse this evidence in time for the submission deadline.

## 2. Objectives

**General objective:** to provide an evidence base on humanitarian needs in the target areas that underpins the problem analysis, targeting and logical framework of Educo's ECHO HIP application.

**Specific objectives:**

1. Identify and prioritise the needs of children, adolescents and youth (up to 24) and caregivers in education in emergencies, child protection (including gender-based violence risks affecting children and adolescents, particularly adolescent girls) and MHPSS, as well as basic needs, WASH and other multi-sectoral needs insofar as they affect children's access to education and protection, disaggregated by gender, age, disability and population group.
2. Analyse barriers to access, quality of existing services and the capacity of schools, local partners and authorities.
3. Map who is doing what, where, based mainly on sector 5W data and coordination fora, to identify gaps, avoid duplication and position Educo's added value.
4. Assess risks (protection, conflict, access, security) and the conflict sensitivity of possible interventions.
5. Recommend a response strategy, indicative target numbers and priority locations, explicitly justified by the primary and secondary evidence collected, aligned with the HIP priorities and the ECHO Technical Annex.

## 3. Scope and key questions

- **Geography:** Bekaa and Baalbek-Hermel (including West Bekaa), Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Saida. within these areas, priority goes to localities hosting displaced people; final selection to be agreed at inception.
- **Population groups:** Lebanese (host communities, internally displaced and returnees), displaced Syrian, Palestine refugee and migrant children and families, with attention to out-of-school children, children with disabilities, adolescent girls and households with specific vulnerabilities.
- **Sectors:** education in emergencies, child protection (including GBV risks for children and adolescents) and MHPSS; basic needs, WASH, shelter and other sectors analysed as they affect children's access to education and protection, mainly through secondary data. Basic needs and WASH are treated as a lens, not an additional sector: MSNA microdata is cross-tabulated with education and child protection indicators, with a few primary questions on the links (cost of schooling, WASH in learning spaces including menstrual hygiene management, schools used as collective shelters, child labour to cover basic needs). GBV is covered through a child and adolescent lens (risks, barriers and access to services), not incident or prevalence data, which would require GBV specialists.

The assessment will answer the questions below.

**Needs and severity:** What are the most severe unmet needs of children and caregivers? Who is most affected, and where? How have needs changed since the 2026 escalation?

**Access and barriers:** How many children are out of school or at risk of dropping out, and why (cost, safety, documentation, displacement, disability, gender norms)?

**Quality and capacity:** What is the state of schools, teachers and learning outcomes (from secondary data), of protection and PSS services, and of local partner capacity?

**Coping and risks:** How do families cope? Which negative coping mechanisms (such as child labour and early marriage) are present? What are the main protection, conflict and security risks?

**Response gaps:** Who is responding, and with what coverage and funding? What gaps and overlaps exist?

**Feasibility:** Which interventions are most relevant and feasible? What efficiency considerations apply? Which modalities and partners are best placed to deliver them?

## 4. Methodology

The consultant proposes the detailed design at inception. A mixed-methods, participatory approach is expected, with the following minimum components:

1. **Secondary data review:** HIP and Technical Annex, Lebanon Response Plan, MSNA, CPIMS, sector working group data, 5W mapping, and Educo and partner project data from Bar Elias.
2. **Primary qualitative data:** key informant interviews (school directors, teachers, municipalities, local NGOs, sector coordinators, UN focal points) and separate focus group discussions with caregivers, adolescents and children, by gender and age group.
3. **Primary quantitative data:** a quantitative component is required, scaled to the timeline, e.g. a short household or school-level survey in priority locations, with a sampling approach, sample size and limitations stated in the proposal, complemented by re-analysis of existing datasets (e.g. MSNA microdata). The quantitative component is mandatory, but a fully representative household survey is not expected within the available field days. Data collection costs are included in the consultant's fee (see section 7).
4. **Triangulation and analysis:** cross-checking of sources, severity and priority analysis, and disaggregation by sex, age, disability and population group.
5. **Validation:** a workshop with Educo and partners to test findings and recommendations before the report is final.

**Standards the consultant must apply:**

- Child safeguarding and ethical participation of children, with informed consent and referral pathways for disclosures.
- Do no harm, conflict sensitivity and humanitarian principles.
- ECHO Gender-Age Marker, protection mainstreaming, disability inclusion and the ECHO education in emergencies policy.
- Data protection, anonymisation and secure storage; data handed over to Educo at the end.
- Contingency: if access or security deteriorates, data collection switches to remote or phone methods, agreed in advance with Educo, without changing the deliverables or deadlines.

## 5. Tasks, deliverables and timeline

Estimated level of effort is 25 working days for the lead consultant, plus the days of the data collection team (enumerators and facilitators), included in the fee, between 1 November 2026 and 15 December 2026.

**Phase 1 – Inception (3 days, Week 1)**
Tasks: kick-off meeting with Educo, desk review, mapping of actors, and definition of methodology and sampling.
Deliverable: Inception note (max. 8 pages) including data collection tools, work plan and ethics protocol.

**Phase 2 – Preparation (2 days, Week 2)**
Tasks: tool design, piloting, enumerator briefing, and arrangements for access and consent.
Deliverable: Final data collection tools.

**Phase 3 – Fieldwork (10 days, Weeks 2 to 4)**
Tasks: key informant interviews, focus group discussions and household survey in the target areas.
Deliverables: a proposal-ready data pack (key figures, priority locations, indicative caseload) by the end of Week 3, so that Single Form drafting can start in parallel; and a debrief to Educo on preliminary findings.

**Phase 4 – Analysis and drafting (6 days, Week 5)**
Deliverable: Draft report.

**Phase 5 – Validation (2 days, Week 5)**
Tasks: validation workshop and incorporation of Educo feedback.
Deliverables: Workshop presentation and consolidated feedback matrix.

**Phase 6 – Finalisation (2 days, Week 6)**
Deliverables: Final report, executive brief, summary in Arabic, and cleaned, anonymised datasets with codebooks.

**Total level of effort: 25 working days over 6 weeks.**

**The final report** (max 25 pages plus annexes, in English) must include:

- Context and needs analysis, with disaggregated data and maps of priority locations.
- Barriers to access, risks and conflict sensitivity analysis.
- Response analysis: gaps, actors, Educo's added value and feasibility of options.
- Recommendations on targeting, indicative caseload, modalities and partners, structured so that Educo can transfer them directly into the ECHO Single Form and logical framework.
- Limitations, annexes (tools, sample, list of sources and interviewees).

An executive brief of 4 pages is also required. A short summary of findings in Arabic (max 2 pages) is also required, to share back with partners and communities. Draft products are reviewed by Educo within 3 working days.

## 6. Consultant profile

**Required**

- Advanced degree in social sciences, education, development or a related field.
- At least 7 years of experience designing and leading humanitarian needs assessments, ideally in Lebanon.
- Demonstrated expertise in \[education in emergencies and/or child protection\].
- Strong qualitative and quantitative skills, including sampling and analysis software.
- Experience working ethically with children, and in gender, age and disability analysis.
- Fluency in English and Arabic.
- Applications from individual consultants, firms or teams are welcome; teams must include Arabic-speaking members, including female facilitators for work with women, girls and adolescents.
- Experience with GBV-sensitive and child-friendly data collection, including referral pathways.
- Three references for similar assignments, preferably with INGOs.

**Desirable:** experience with DG ECHO proposals and the Single Form; knowledge of the Lebanon coordination system and sector working groups; French or Spanish.

## 7. Management and conditions

- The consultant reports to the Country Representative, Educo Lebanon, with weekly check-ins during fieldwork.
- Educo provides existing documents, introductions to partners and logistical support for access; data collection costs are included in the fee.
- The consultant and all team members, including enumerators, sign Educo's child safeguarding and PSEAH commitments before fieldwork starts.
- Educo owns all data and products; use by the consultant requires written approval.
- Payment: 30% on approval of the inception note, 40% on the draft report, 30% on the final report.
- The consultant manages their own insurance, security and travel, and complies with Educo's security guidelines.

jobs.title: [Re-Ad] Developing a Handbook for Working Groups for Strengthening Disaster- Resilient Local Governance in Kerala
jobs.description:
The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and diversified its expertise across social and physical sciences, envisioning safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction. Being an autonomous international organization governed by the Board of Trustees. It supports sustainable solutions for disaster risk reduction across a broad range of specialist areas, with a wide range of professional expertise from atmospheric scientists to social scientists with experience at all levels of engagement typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) effectively.

ADPC’s Strategy 2030 guides the organization in providing comprehensive risk reduction support to countries and communities in Asia and the Pacific, with various programs being implemented under 15 strategic themes by three departments, namely the Preparedness and Climate Actions, Risk Analytics and Climate Services, and Risk Governance and Financing. In addition to these, ADPC also works on three cross-cutting themes: Gender and Diversity, Innovation, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation through permanent working committees. These activities are supported by proactive individual departments of Finance, Human Resources, and Administration. ADPC recognizes the importance of examining the linkages between disaster risk management, poverty reduction, gender equality, sustainability, rights-based approaches, climate change, and regional cooperation. For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**B. Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC advances ADPC Strategy 2030 by strengthening disaster preparedness, anticipatory action, emergency response, resilient recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. The department works with governments, national and local institutions, civil society organizations, volunteer networks, the private sector, communities, and other traditional and non-traditional actors to promote inclusive, locally led, and whole-of-society approaches to disaster risk management. In line with ADPC’s strategic priorities, PCA supports countries and communities in developing and operationalizing preparedness, response, recovery, and climate action frameworks, plans, systems, and capacities before, during, and after disasters. It also promotes localization, gender equality and social inclusion, innovation, regional cooperation, knowledge exchange, and partnerships to ensure that disaster preparedness and climate action are practical, evidence-informed, sustainable, and responsive to the needs of at-risk communities.

**C. Statement of Intent**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC), under the INSPIRE Program, is providing technical assistance to the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA), in collaboration with the Kerala Institute of Local Administration (KILA), to strengthen disaster risk governance and institutional capacities in Kerala, with particular emphasis on risk-informed local governance and strengthening the capacity of Local Self Governments (LSGs). Kerala's decentralized governance system provides a strong institutional platform for integrating disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate change adaptation (CCA) and resilience into local development planning. Working Groups within LSGs play an important role in participatory planning, situation analysis, identification of development needs, project formulation, prioritization, and monitoring. However, LSGs-Working Groups are not equipped with adequate practical tools for mainstreaming DRR, CCA and resilience into local development planning and implementation.

Based on the findings of the Learning Needs Assessment undertaken under the INSPIRE program, the State Steering Committee recommended that a Handbook for Working Groups LSGs should be developed to facilitate effective integration of disaster and climate risks into local development processes. In this context, it is proposed to develop a handbook for LSG Working Groups to facilitate mainstreaming DRR, CCA and resilience into local development planning.

**D. Purpose of the Assignment**

The purpose of the assignment is to develop a practical handbook for LSG Working Groups with a special focus on the LSG DM Working Group (13th Working Group) to enhance their technical capacity, provide operational clarity, and facilitate mainstreaming of DRR, CCA, and resilience into development planning across developmental sectors, thus promoting disaster-resilient local governance.

The objectives of developing the Handbook are to:

- clarify the mandate, roles and functions of the Disaster Management Working Group at different LSG levels.
- provide practical guidance and define mechanisms for integrating DRR and CCA into local development plans, budgets, projects and monitoring systems.
- provide practical tools, templates, checklists and frameworks for use by Working Groups to integrate DRR and CCA into local development planning and implementation.
- support Working Group members to translate identified risks into DRR/CCA interventions and project concepts, including linkage with relevant planning and financing opportunities across development sectors.
- strengthen the technical competency of Working Group members on disaster risk, vulnerability, climate risk and resilience.
- strengthen coordination and convergence between the Disaster Management Working Group and other sectoral Working Groups.
- promote inclusive, gender-responsive and participatory approaches to local disaster risk governance.
- strengthen monitoring of preparedness, disaster management plan actions, and priority interventions.
- establish a roadmap for strengthening and institutionalizing the LSG DM Working Group.

**E. Expected OutputsOutputs/Deliverables**

1. Inception Report and Detailed Work Plan, including understanding of assignment, methodology, stakeholder engagement approach and work schedule
Timeline: Within 2 weeks
2. Desk Review and Gap & Need Assessment Report
Timeline: Within 1 month
3. Draft Note for the Handbook Conception Workshop, including presentation of findings and proposed handbook framework
Timeline: Within 2 months
4. Detailed Handbook Framework and Finalised Chapter Structure, including proposed tools
Timeline: Within 3 months
5. Zero Draft of Handbook along with Tools-Templates, Checklists
Timeline: Within 4 months
6. Revised Draft incorporating Expert Panel Review Recommendations
Timeline: Within 5 months
7. Pilot Testing and Validation Report, including documentation of user feedback and recommendations
Timeline: Within 6 months
8. Final Handbook and Practical Tools, incorporating all agreed comments and pilot-testing findings
Timeline: Within 7 months
9. Final Consultancy/Completion Report and Presentation summarising the assignment, consultations, key findings, revisions and recommendations
Timeline: Within 8 months

**Note**

1. The sequence may be adjusted with the agreement between ADPC and KSDMA.
2. The final handbook should be submitted in editable source format and final publication-ready PDF format, along with editable versions of all tools and templates.

**F. Scope of Work**

The scope of work will include, but will not necessarily be limited to, the following:

**1. Desk Review and Needs Assessment**

The consultant shall:

- Review relevant national and state policies, guidelines, frameworks, and institutional arrangements related to:
- Local governance and decentralized planning;
- Disaster management;
- Disaster Risk Reduction;
- Climate Change Adaptation;
- Local Disaster Management Plans;
- GPDPs and other local development planning processes;
- Working Group functioning; and
- Social inclusion and gender-responsive planning.
- Review relevant existing manuals, guidelines, tools and training materials.
- Review relevant national and international good practices on strengthening local disaster governance and Working Groups.
- Identify institutional, operational, technical, knowledge and capacity gaps affecting the functioning of LSG Disaster Management Working Groups.
- Identify opportunities for convergence between DRR, climate action and local development planning.

Output: Baseline and Gap Assessment inputs/report.

**2. Stakeholder Consultation and Handbook Conception**

The consultant shall support ADPC and KSDMA in conducting a stakeholder consultation/workshop for handbook conception. The consultant shall:

- Present key findings from the desk review and needs assessment.
- Facilitate technical discussions on the proposed handbook scope and structure.
- Consult relevant LSG representatives, government departments, technical institutions, experts, and other stakeholders.
- Identify practical requirements and user needs.
- Facilitate co-design and co-creation of the handbook framework and chapterization.
- Finalize the proposed chapter structure and thematic areas in consultation with ADPC and KSDMA.
- Identify the practical tools required under each thematic area.

Output: Agreed handbook framework and chapter structure.

**3. Content Development and Draft Handbook Preparation**

The consultant shall develop the chapter-wise contents and draft the Handbook as per the agreed framework and chapter structure. The consultant shall:

- Develop chapter-wise contents as per agreed structure.
- Draft templates, checklists and other such tools as agreed.
- Draft the Handbook along with all Annexures in consultation with ADPC and KSDMA.

Output: Draft Handbook (zero draft) with all Annexures

**4. Expert Panel Review**

The consultant shall facilitate Expert Panel Review of the draft Handbook. The consultant shall:

- Share the draft Handbook with the Expert Panel to be set up by ADPC/KSDMA comprising select subject matter experts, LSG representatives, technical institutions, and others as deemed appropriate.
- Obtain feedback and suggestions of the of th on improving the Draft.
- Incorporate the suggestions/feedback and revise the draft Handbook.
- Share the draft Handbook with ADPC and KSDMA for review and feedback.
- Revise draft Handbook and share with ADPC and KSDMA.

Output: Revised Draft Handbook (version1.0) with all Annexures

**5. Pilot Testing and Validation Workshop**

The consultant shall support ADPC and KSDMA in pilot testing with a selected LSG Disaster Management Group through a consultation workshop with LSG representatives, government departments, technical institutions, experts, and other stakeholders for validation of the Handbook. The consultant shall:

- Support in pilot testing of the handbook and tools with selected LSG Disaster Management Working Groups
- Make chapter-wise presentation.
- Facilitate technical discussions on each Chapter and Annexures.
- Facilitate consensus development on contents of the Handbook including templates, checklists and other such tools.
- Incorporate suggestions/feedback received in the Workshop.
- Finalize the Handbook in consultation with ADPC and KSDMA.

Output: Final Version of Handbook with all Annexures

**G. Responsibilities and Tasks**

The Consultant Shall:

- Prepare an Inception Report and detailed work plan for completing the Assignment.
- Undertake the desk review and needs assessment.
- Conduct consultations with relevant stakeholders.
- Facilitate in organizing the Workshop for the conception of the handbook structure, content and chapterisation.
- Develop the handbook framework and detailed content in close consultation with ADPC and KSDMA.
- Draft the handbook in close consultation with ADPC and KSDMA.
- Develop guidance notes, assessment tools, templates, and checklists, etc.
- Ensure that the handbook is technically rigorous while remaining simple and user-friendly for LSG Working Groups.
- Ensure alignment with existing Kerala LSG planning and disaster management systems.
- Integrate gender, social inclusion and differentiated vulnerability considerations throughout the handbook.
- Incorporate multi-sectoral convergence and inter-Working Group coordination mechanisms.
- Participate in expert review processes as agreed with ADPC and KSDMA.
- Revise the handbook based on expert feedback and comments.
- Support pilot testing of the handbook and tools with selected LSG Disaster Management Working Groups.
- Facilitate/participate in validation workshops.
- Incorporate field-level feedback and recommendations.
- Undertake final technical and editorial refinement.
- Submit the final handbook and all associated tools in editable and final formats.
- Prepare a brief completion report documenting the consultancy process, key findings, consultations undertaken, revisions made, and recommendations for future application.

**H. Reporting Arrangement**

The consultant will report to the Unit Head, RBL, PCA, working closely with the Program Coordinator, State Consultant, and other relevant ADPC staff as required.

- The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of ADPC and in close coordination with KSDMA and KILA.
- Development of the Handbook will be guided by KSDMA, with technical and institutional inputs from KILA and other relevant Government stakeholders.
- Overall strategic oversight will be provided through the INSPIRE Program Steering Committee (PSC) at the State level.
- Progress will be reported to NDMA, as Chair of the INSPIRE Program Steering Committee, through quarterly progress updates and meetings of the PSC.
- The Technology Partner shall participate in consultations, demonstrations, review meetings, and validation exercises as required.

**I. Required Qualifications and Experience1. Minimum Academic Qualifications**

The consultant should possess:

- A Master's degree or equivalent in Disaster Management, Disaster Risk Reduction, Climate Change/Climate Adaptation, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Urban/Regional Planning, Rural Development, Environmental Studies, Earth Sciences or a related discipline.
- A doctoral degree or additional specialised qualification in a relevant field will be an advantage.

**2. Professional Experience**

The consultant should have:

- At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, local governance, development planning, institutional strengthening or related fields.
- Demonstrated experience in developing technical manuals, handbooks, guidelines, frameworks, toolkits or similar knowledge products.
- Demonstrated understanding of Local Self Government systems and decentralized planning in Kerala.
- Experience in integrating DRR and/or climate resilience into local development planning and governance.
- Experience working with government institutions, LSGs, development agencies or international organisations.
- Experience in conducting stakeholder consultations, participatory processes, workshops and validation exercises.
- Demonstrated experience in developing practical tools, templates, assessment frameworks or SOPs.

**3. Technical Expertise**

The consultant should have demonstrated expertise in the following areas:

- Disaster Risk Reduction and disaster management
- Climate change adaptation and resilience
- Local governance and decentralized planning
- Risk-informed development planning
- Hazard, vulnerability, and risk assessment
- Community-based and inclusive disaster risk management
- Gender-responsive and socially inclusive planning
- Institutional capacity development
- Multi-sectoral coordination and scheme convergence
- Monitoring and performance assessment
- Knowledge management and development of user-oriented technical guidance.

**4. Language Proficiency**

The consultant must have language proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English and Malayalam.

**5. Desirable Experience**

Preference may be given to candidates with:

- Prior experience working with Kerala LSGs/KSDMA/KILA or other relevant state institutions
- Experience in developing guidelines or handbooks for government institutions
- Experience in disaster-resilient local governance
- Experience in integrating DRR into GPDPs, Ward Development Plans or equivalent local planning processes
- Experience in facilitating multi-stakeholder and co-creation processes
- Publications or demonstrated technical writing experience in relevant areas.

**J. Duty Station**

The assignment will be primarily home-based, with regular virtual coordination with ADPC and KSDMA. The consultant will be required to travel to Thiruvananthapuram and other locations within Kerala, as necessary for stakeholder consultations, workshops, meetings with KSDMA/ADPC/others, pilot testing, state-level dissemination/launch, etc. Travel and associated expenses, where applicable, shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the contract and relevant ADPC policies.

**K. Duration**

The assignment is expected to be completed within 8 months of contract commencement. The detailed work plan will be finalised during the inception phase.
