jobs.title: Provincial Health Extender
jobs.description:
Overview of position

- In 2021 an L3 emergency was announced in Afghanistan following change in power in the country. our client Health programme worked with partners to provide essential health services for children and women in need across the country. Services are provided through health facilities and mobile teams for remote, hard-to-reach and in-need areas. Monitoring and technical support are key functions to verify programme implementation and improve the quality of service, including MNCAH, EPI, and especially health in emergency activities in all provinces of the country, as well as at the regional and national levels.
- In addition, in September 2021, the world bank suspended the Sehatmandi project in Afghanistan, this threatens to collapse the health system in the country, our client and WHO have worked to sustain the services through CERF fund until a new mechanism is created. A monitoring framework of this modality is being created including monitoring field visits to health facilities receiving support through our client.
- Also, in 2021, vaccination against COVID 19 started in the country, adding more burden to the already overwhelmed health system, the introduction of new vaccine targeting different population groups, required another additional monitoring framework and tools to track the progress and ensue quality and equity.
- Objective: Extenders are expected to carry out a range of duties, as outlined below, to support monitoring functions, demand generation, accountability to affected population mechanisms, technical facilitation and programme implementation.
- Those duties, which are described in detail below, do not include neither programmatic nor financial authority. Extenders are identified among Afghani citizens with specific expertise and a thorough knowledge of the territory in which they operate, based on their residency and/or work experience.
- Due to the current emergency situation in the county and the growing needs in all areas (total health PiN in 2022 is 18.4 M) which led to a quick increase of emergency activities supported by our client, and due to the difficult geographical nature of Afghanistan and the lack of transportation infrastructure and the remoteness of many communities, which make access and monitoring a challenge in many areas. The need of our client extenders network to complement our client efforts in such areas (difficult to access by staff) is critical to achieve the programme goals. Extenders are engaged through a third-party Service Provider that is directly responsible for the administrative and security related aspects of the Extenders deployment, while our client is responsible for financial support, technical guidance and supervision.
- Accordingly, the Extenders will be contracted by a Service Provider and will be considered a staff of the contracting company for all purposes and in all circumstances. The Extenders will not be considered a our client staff member or consultant. As such, our client will not be directly or indirectly responsible for the Extenders while implementing this Terms of Reference (TOR).
- Based on the approved RWP, our client is supporting MNCAH and EPI services in the country and working to improve coordination, develop policies, strategies, and guidelines, support implementation and monitoring of activities. extenders are tasked to facilitate and support our client programme activities implementation and monitoring tasks that cannot be done by our client staff due to accessibility, security, and scale. Which make extenders modality the most reliable and efficient way to support those tasks.
- Extender will be based at their area of responsibility, and usually selected from communities in same area for easy mobility and to reduce security risks, and transportation time and cost. These extenders are not given task that is supposed to be done normally by our client staff.

Role objectives

TASK TO BE PERFORMED

- Conduct regular situation monitoring in specific areas based on requests by the programme or Zonal Office, to assess the overall humanitarian situation and document the needs of affected populations, in particular women and children health needs.
- Provide technical services to our client projects primarily in hard-to-reach areas, through ensuring regular and systematic technical advice, quality assurance and technical guidance to implementing partners and counterparts, for the efficient implementation of our client programmes and effective achievement of results for the benefit of Afghani children and women.
- Identify capacity and technical gaps of implementing partners and counterparts and provide technical support to ensure capacity building and on job training as needed.
- Support the implementation of Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT) supported by our client through technical support and capacity building, and monitor the service implementation and quality. and work with partners at the provincial level to improve MHNT programme results.
- Monitor the work of health facilities supported through our client CERF and other funds using the common checklists and tools.
- Support EPI programme routine immunization activities including -but not limited to- service delivery, cold chain system, vaccine and non-vaccine supplies, information system.
- Support emergency preparedness and response activities implementation and monitoring.
- Report any suspected PSEA case directly to the responsible our client focal point and inform the programme specialist.
- Report any suspected fraud case to the Zonal programme specialist or relevant our client staff.
- Coordinate the monthly working\\monitoring plan with the regional extender, and share the progress and visits repots on timely manner.
- Participating in PHCC, Staff meeting with SP, EPI sub comettee and relvent meetings.

Conduct regular visits to monitor Health programme activities supported by our client, and facilitate our client staff programmatic visits, with a focus on:

- Assessing programme implementation by Implementing Partners through PCAs (Programme Cooperation Agreements) and SSFAs (Small-Scale Funding Agreements) as well as programme implementation by partners and agencies according to the our client Afghanistan Country Office Work Plans.
- Checking EPI supplies chain systems and equipment in place and their functionality status, including following SOPs in vaccine storage and utilization.
- Supporting Health information system and data registration reviews and assessments, and the implementation of Data Quality Improvement plans and microplanning activities.
- Verifying health supplies are delivered to target beneficiaries in line with relevant programme documents and flag any delays and bottlenecks.
- Conducting post-distribution monitoring (PDM) of supplies to assess beneficiaries’ feedback in terms of the quality, timeliness and relevance of supplies delivered. Other end-user monitoring of specific programmes will be conducted as required by the Zonal Office.
- Collecting direct feedback form beneficiaries and affected population about the situation and needs, and the suitability of the services provided and how to improve.

DELIVERABLE(s)

- Provincial need assessment for implementation of mobile health teams completed
- Monthly monitoring of mobile health and nutrition teams service delivery points conducted.
- Monthly report of availability of ORS/Zinc stock with CHWs submitted
- Coordination, and monitoring of community mobilization/engagement activities facilitated
- Need assessment of CHWs training for target provinces completed
- Training of CHWs supported by our client monitored
- Routine EPI monitoring checklists completed and reported (this checklist includes all components of Routine EPI).
- Oriented on new RI activities e.g., accelerated immunization, Measles interventions, awareness raising activities (IEC, media broadcast, etc.).
- Percentage of HFs equipped with SDDs reported.
- Emergency need assessment of emergency affected areas completed
- Our client supported emergency activities monitored including HF under the Sahatmandi CERF support.
- Field visits implemented and reported timely with the required quality.
- Situation monitoring reports and needs assessment data is provided.
- Programme monitoring reports are developed and shared with zonal office programme officers\\specialists and reginal health extender including progress information, gaps and challenges, supplies monitoring, and beneficiaries’ feedback.
- Partner’s capacity in area of extender technical expertise is built.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Minimum Qualification and Experience:

- Having certificate in health, medicine, public health, nursing, midwife or related field.
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in in health, medicine, public health, nurse, midwife or related field.
- Proficiency in data analysis and interpretation.
- Excellent communication skills for effective collaboration with healthcare professionals and stakeholders.
- Proven ability to contribute to the enhancement of health programs through data-driven insights.
- Reporting skills

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

jobs.title: Protection Coordinator
jobs.description:
**About the job**

**Overall purpose of the role:** Based in the DRC Türkiye country office, the role provides technical oversight to DRC Protection programme, including to strategy and proposal development, reporting, technical guidance and guidelines, technical support for DRC and partner staff, as well as advising on protection research, needs assessment(s), and advocacy efforts.

**Geographic Scope: Country (Türkiye)**

The role is based in the DRC Türkiye Country Office in Gaziantep.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

***Protection Sectoral Technical Responsibility***

- Technically responsible for the overall protection portfolio, with a strong focus on protection analysis, partnerships, and multi-partner coordination
- With the support of the Partnerships Coordinator, Head of Programme, and Senior Management Team, continue shaping and operationalising DRC’s localisation approach to protection programming and identifying innovative ways to collaborate with CSOs, national and grassroots organisations including refugee-led organisations beyond formal partnership agreements. This will include capacity development and technical support to existing and new partners
- Lead multi-partner protection monitoring analysis efforts in line with the Protection Analysis Framework (PAF) tailored to the Türkiye context
- Lead the development and implementation of the country level protection strategy
- Oversee and lead the in-country development, harmonisation, adaptation and rollout of internal policies, guidelines, tools, Standard Operating Procedures, related to DRC’s protection interventions
- Act as a reference point for Economic Recovery colleagues for Protection Mainstreaming & integrated programming

***Technical Supervision***
- Technically supervise, provide technical advice and guidance to protection staff at Country Office level, including a Protection Programme Officer and a Protection Analysis Officer
- Participate in human resource processes, including the recruitment of protection technical staff in country, establishing minimum technical requirements for protection positions, and supporting performance objectives and performance appraisals
- Responsible for identifying protection sectoral technical gaps and establishing & delivering capacity building plans for protection staff

***Protection Programme Development and Oversight***
- Lead and contribute to the design and finalisation of all protection sectoral interventions in proposals and projects
- Provide technical review of all proposals that include protection interventions and/or mainstreaming
- Maintain oversight of overall protection programme implementation, including budgets and indicators, in close collaboration with HoP, MEAL, Grants & Partnerships, and Finance colleagues
- Participate in protection programme / project review meetings, including grant opening, grant review and close out meetings

***Quality Assurance***
- Lead, in collaboration with MEAL team, on the development of quality assurance systems and ensure they are applied throughout the programme cycle
- Follow technical oversight mechanisms to ensure protection interventions are provided according to established policies, guidance, and Standard Operating Procedures
- Lead the self-assessment based on the Protection Programme Quality Framework once a year and contribute to the annual Protection Survey

***Coordination and Representation***
- Represent DRC and actively contribute to protection sector coordination fora at the country level
- Lead DRC’s protection sector coordination and collaboration efforts with relevant stakeholders including government, civil society, NGOs, and UN
- Actively engage and contribute to DRC protection-related advocacy efforts, nationally as well as regionally
- Promote integrated programming and ensure internal coordination and harmonisation of DRC protection interventions across sites and with other core sectors, as relevant

***Other***
- Any other duties as requested by the line manager

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have university degree in law, social science, political science, international development, or any other related field.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Minimum 5 years of demonstrated technical experience in the international protection sector preferably with an (I)NGO and/or UN agencies
- Minimum 3 years of experience leading, managing or providing technical advice/support to a protection programme that preferably includes legal counselling and assistance, case management and protection monitoring programming
- Very strong technical writing skills
- Documented skills in project development and design for protection programmes, preferably in a multisectoral setting
- Experience in protection strategy development including the development of SOPs, training materials and action plans
- Strategic thinker with the ability to quickly develop good insight and understanding of humanitarian, political and human rights situation in the relevant context
- Proven strong analytical thinker and problem solver
- Experience with technical supervision of teams
- Experience in providing technical guidance and developing and providing learning activities
- Experience working with key institutional donors such as ECHO, DANIDA and SIDA on protection
- Experience in driving protection partnerships including with refugee-led organisations, national partners, local/government authorities, UN organizations and coordination networks
- Full professional proficiency in written and spoken English
- Turkish and/or Arabic proficiency an added value

*Desired*

- Experience in advocacy for protection a strong asset
- Experience working on mixed migration programming a strong asset

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Initially until 31.12.2027 (with possible extension based on fund availability and performance)

Band: G1 – Non-Manager

Designation of Duty Station: Country Office (Gaziantep)

Start date: 01.12.2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for nationals or expatriates and depends on the successful candidate’s profile. For questions regarding the vacancy please reach out to us by sending email to TUR-Recruitment@drc.ngo

jobs.title: Sudan - Head of Programmes
Country Director – Lebanon (International)
jobs.description:
**Department:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Beirut – Lebanon

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Contract duration:** 1 year (renewable)

**Direct report:** Director of Operations

**Grade:** Country Director

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups, De Facto Authorities (AGDAs) and Provisional Governments for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Role**

The Country Director (CD) provides strategic leadership and representation for Geneva Call in Lebanon. As the most senior representative of Geneva Call in the field, the CD is responsible for the overall planning, coordination, implementation, and development of country operations. This includes the qualitative implementation of Geneva Call’s humanitarian engagement and diplomacy (humanitarian dialogue, research, community-based approach), advocacy, fundraising, representation, and the management of financial and human resources.

The CD reports administratively and technically to the Director of Operations and directly manages the country team.

## **Work Relations**

**Internal:**

• Collaborates with regional and HQ units, including Programme, Policy Research and Legal, MEAL, Safety and Security, Global Engagement, Donor Relations, Finance, Logistics, and HR teams.

• Manages the country mission; coordinates with and thematic/technical advisors and functional leads at HQ.

**External:**

• Represents Geneva Call to national and local authorities, donors, UN agencies, INGOs, civil society actors, AGDAs and Provisional Governments where applicable.

• Represents Geneva Call in national and international forums and builds strategic partnerships.

## **Duties and Responsibilities**

**Strategy and programme implementation**

•Analyses the humanitarian and security situation in Iraq to identify key areas of work for Geneva Call.

• Ensures the fulfillment of Geneva Call’s core mission to promote IHL with AGDAs and Provisional Governments with focus on addressing protection threats to vulnerable populations.

• Provides leadership, quality delivery and management, and streamlines monitoring, evaluation, and learning for the country programme, in alignment with Geneva Call’s strategy. Ensures programmes are monitored and evaluated effectively.

• Manages, supervises, and coordinates all activities in-country related to the implementation of Geneva Call’s projects in the country, adhering to proposal guidelines, indicators, budgets, and work plans. Promotes the sharing of learning internally and externally, using results to inform programme decisions and enhance institutional knowledge.

**Safety and security management**

• Oversees safety and security protocols and risk management plans for staff and operations.

• Conducts regular context and risk analyses to ensure safety and operational viability.

• Manages security in line with Geneva Call’s policies and standards.

**Mission management and coordination**

• Manages the country mission team, and has on average 2 to 4 direct reports, depending on the size of the mission. Is accountable for all leadership processes in-country such as performance management, duty of care, attendance.

• Ensures transparent financial management and compliance with internal procedures, policies, code of conduct and local laws.

**Fundraising and resource mobilisation**

• Develops and implements a country fundraising strategy to secure necessary resources.

• Leads the preparation of project proposals and donor submissions, ensuring contextual relevance.

• Fosters relationships with donors and identifies new funding opportunities.

**Advocacy and communication**

• Represents Geneva Call’s interests with government bodies, donors, and key stakeholders.

• Actively participates in clusters and working groups relevant to Geneva Call’s mission.

• Advocates for Geneva Call’s initiatives to enhance civilian protection and adherence to IHL.

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

• A Master’s degree (preferred) or a bachelor’s degree in political or social sciences, International Humanitarian Law (IHL), Human Rights, or a related field relevant to the role.

**Experience (Essential)**

• A minimum of 12 years of experience in humanitarian organisations, with a strong preference for at least 15 years, including at least 2 years in a Country Director role.

• Out of total required experience, minimum 7 years’ experience of working in conflict affected contexts.

• Proven experience in managing multi-donor programmes, teams (including expatriates), and complex operations.

• Strong background in financial and donor management, capacity building, and security management.

**Experience (Desirable)**

• Experience in working with armed groups, De Facto Authorities and Provisional Governments is a strong plus.

• Proposal writing and donor reporting skills.

• Experience working on programmes related to civilian infrastructure and/or rule of law.

**Job related competencies**

• Strong organisational and analytical skills with an entrepreneurial mindset.

• Solid diplomatic skills with the ability to communicate with high-level interlocutors.

• Knowledgeable and passionate about political and security affairs. Extensive knowledge of security management.

• Fundraising, project cycle management, and budget management.

• Strong risk-planning and problem-solving skills.

• Capacity to meet deadlines under time pressure.

• Negotiation and interpersonal skills.

• Knowledge of International Humanitarian Law (IHL) or International Human Rights Law is a strong asset.

**Organisational competencies**

• Understanding and respect for humanitarian principles and the organisation’s vision, mission, and confidentiality.

• Flexibility and adaptability.

• Collaborative, team-oriented, and solutions-oriented approach.

• Upholds and promotes the highest ethical and professional standards in alignment with organisational values.

• Understands how to navigate in a matrix organisation.

**Languages**

• Fluency in English and Arabic is required.

• Proficiency in French, Spanish, or other languages is a strong advantage.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

This is a unique opportunity to lead impactful humanitarian engagement in complex conflict environments while contributing to the protection of vulnerable communities. It is also a unique chance to combine strategic leadership, diplomacy, and operational management within an organization recognized for its principled engagement with armed actors and commitment to humanitarian norms. If you are motivated by combining operational impact, strategic leadership, and humanitarian purpose, this position offers you the possibility to make a tangible and lasting contribution where it matters most. We look forward to your application.

Geneva Call consists of many diverse nationalities, cultures, languages, and opinions. Geneva Call is an inclusive working environment for all staff. Applications are particularly encouraged from all qualified candidates without distinction on the grounds of race, color, sex, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, and gender identity.

jobs.title: Responsable Environnement et Énergies renouvelables
jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a l’objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociales les plus vulnérables.

## **Termes de référence**

**Intitulé du poste** : Responsable Environnement et Énergies renouvelables

**Code :** SR-31-10315

**Pays :** Tchad

**Lieu d’affectation** : Koukou, Est du Tchad

**Date de prise de fonction** :16/11/2026

**Durée du contrat** : 6 mois

**Sous la supervision de :** Coordinateur Programme

**Supervision de :** 1 superviseur Environnement

**Lieu d'affectation:** sans famille

## **Contexte général du projet**

INTERSOS est présent au Tchad depuis 2004 avec des projets dans les secteurs de la Sécurité alimentaire, de la protection, de la santé-nutrition et aussi de l'EHA (WASH) au profit des personnes déplacées internes dans la région du Lac et pour les réfugiés soudanais à l'Est du Tchad. Après une interruption des activités en 2016, INTERSOS a repris ses activités en 2017. Les domaines sur lesquels INTERSOS Tchad focalise ses interventions sont principalement les suivants : la Protection à travers le renforcement d'un environnement favorisant la promotion et la protection des droits humains et plus spécifiquement ceux des enfants et des femmes à travers la mise en place des Espaces Amis d'Enfants, la gestion de cas VBG, la restauration de la cohésion sociale, la réhabilitation communautaire, mais aussi de l'accès à l'eau, l'hygiène et l'assainissement, à la sécurité alimentaire et à la santé/nutrition.

## **Objectif général de la position**

Le/la Responsable Environnement et Énergies renouvelables sera responsable de l’accompagnement et de la facilitation des activités de construction de biodigesteurs familiaux, de renforcement des capacités des bénéficiaires et des autres parties prenantes, en cohérence avec les objectifs et la stratégie du projet RésiSila, et conformément aux politiques de sauvegarde et de durabilité environnementale d'INTERSOS et du bailleur de fonds SRF.

## **Principales responsabilités et tâches**

**Planification et conception**

- Assurer/Réviser la conception technique des ouvrages (biodigesteurs communautaires et familiaux à cas de besoin), incluant la conduite des études de faisabilité du projet, le CCTP (Cahier des Clauses Techniques Particulières), les BoQ, s’assurant de leur alignement avec les normes réglementaires existantes.
- Garantir l’efficacité des activités de protection de l’environnement prévues dans le projet: agroforesterie (particulièrement la culture de Moringa), promotion des pesticides biologiques à base de Moringa, engrais organiques (compost/fumier) et protection du sol.

**Suivi des travaux**

- Appuyer le processus de sélection du/des prestataire(s) pour la réalisation des ouvrages, puis assurer la supervision des travaux, garantissant leur qualité et conformité au cahier des charges ; identifier les adaptations nécessaires aux plans initiaux le cas échéant, et faire des recommandations au Chef de projet et au Coordinateur des programmes ;
- Appui/suivi de la sécurisation des biogaz produits.

**Gestion des risques**

- Identifier, évaluer et proposer des mesures pérennes afin d’atténuer les risques potentiels liés au projet, y compris les retards, l’impact environnemental et les dangers pour la sécurité, et proposer des mesures de mitigation appropriées.

**Sensibilisation et engagement des bénéficiaires parties prenantes :**

- Appuyer les activités de sensibilisation menées auprès des bénéficiaires et des autres parties prenantes autour des biodigesteurs ; soumettre des rapports mensuels sur l’avancement de l’activité au Chef de projet, pour l’information des autorités locales et des autres parties prenantes ; Veiller à l’appui-conseil, au réseautage et au plaidoyer dans la mise en œuvre du programme.

**Renforcement des capacités**

- Appuyer les bénéficiaires et les autres parties prenantes par des formations techniques en lien avec le biodigesteur et sa chaîne de valeur (production de compost, aliments dérivés et pesticides).

**Capitalisation**

- Contribuer à la documentation des résultats de l’activité en relation avec le responsable de capitalisation du projet, veillant à mettre en exergue les leçons apprises, et les bonnes pratiques tirées de la mise en œuvre de l’activité ; contribuer à l’élaboration de nouvelles propositions de projet.

## **Profil requis**

**Education**

- BAC +4/5 dans le domaine du développement rural, de l’environnement, de l’ingénierie (agronomie, énergie renouvelable, production animale, agro économie) ou tout domaine équivalent ;

**Expérience Professionnelle**

- Minimum 4 ans d'expérience pertinente dans la mise en œuvre de projets similaires ;
- Expérience du contexte des zones sahéliennes, et de l’Est du Tchad en particulier ;
- Une expérience avec une ONG internationale est un atout majeur.

**Exigences Professionnelles**

- Bonne connaissance du fonctionnement, de l’installation et de l’entretien des biodigesteurs ;
- Compétences en mobilisation communautaire et en formation ;
- Maîtrise des outils de suivi-évaluation et de reporting ;
- Bonnes capacités rédactionnelles.

**Langues**

- Français courant (écrit et oral exigés)
- Anglais et Arabe (atouts)

**Exigences personnelles**

- Travail d'équipe et coopération
- Flexibilité et orientation résultats/qualité
- Bonne gestion du stress
- Engagement envers les principes d'INTERSOS

## **Conditions générales et avantages :**

- **Fourchette de salaire :** 06 - 2.258€ - 2.447€ monthly gross
- **Rémunération**: La rémunération mensuelle pour chaque poste est définie conformément à la grille salariale et à la grille de fonctions standard internationales d'INTERSOS, en tenant compte de l'expérience du candidat sélectionné. Elle est communiquée lors de l'entretien avec les ressources humaines, ou en tout état de cause lors de la première étape du processus de sélection.
- **Hébergement :** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R :** Le personnel d'INTERSOS tenu de travailler pendant des périodes prolongées dans des lieux d'affectation soumis à des conditions périlleuses, stressantes et difficiles bénéficie d'une période régulière et obligatoire de repos et de récupération (R&R). Cette mesure vise à protéger sa santé et son bien-être et à garantir une performance de travail optimale lors de la reprise de ses fonctions, tout en préservant la capacité opérationnelle de l'Organisation. Les avantages liés au R&R ne constituent pas une compensation financière pour le degré de pénibilité et d'insécurité d'un lieu d'affectation. Admissibilité : les membres du personnel recrutés en tant que personnel international de terrain dont le contrat indique un lieu d'affectation R&R comme lieu d'affectation principal et dont la durée du contrat est égale ou supérieure à 4 mois civils. R&R : il consiste en 7 jours de récupération psychophysique toutes les 8/10/12 semaines, selon le lieu d'affectation. Une indemnité de 1 000 € y est associée.
- **Congés annuels :** 2,5 jours par mois
- **Assurance médicale:** Assurance accidents et décès ; assurance responsabilité civile ; remboursement des vaccins, du certificat médical et du test PCR pour le déploiement ; soutien psychosocial sur demande pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Transport:** Vols A/R pour l'humanitaire. Pour toute mission d'une durée d'au moins 9 mois, un billet d'avion supplémentaire vers le pays de résidence et le retour sur le lieu de mission est pris en charge par l'Organisation pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS prend en charge les frais et l'assistance pour l'obtention du visa pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Formation d’intégration :** Cours d'orientation en ligne : chaque nouveau membre du personnel reçoit une formation préparatoire avant le départ, adéquate pour fournir les informations nécessaires relatives à la structure d'INTERSOS et aux principaux processus décisionnels et outils de travail, afin de faciliter son intégration au sein de l'Organisation.
- **Remarque 1 :** INTERSOS applique une « politique d'apprentissage et de développement » (Learning & Development Policy) qui inclut la possibilité de bénéficier de formations et de participer à des formations internes et externes. La priorité sera accordée au personnel travaillant pour INTERSOS depuis plus de deux ans.
- **Remarque 2 :** La classification des lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, R&R et sans accompagnement est soumise à des critères de sécurité, d'accès aux services de santé et d'éducation, et n'est pas négociable.

jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:
1\. **International knowledge hub for health** – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.
2\. **Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health** – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.
3\. **Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats** – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.
4\. **Driver of health system transformation** – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.
5\. **Voice for health equity** – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

1\. Provide input to and manage the implementation of the country level OSL strategy, annual workplan, business-continuity arrangements and emergency logistics plans, ensuring alignment with WHO rules, policies, technical standards, programme priorities and available resources.
2\. Coordinate supply-chain planning for health commodities, medical equipment and operational supplies, including demand forecasting, supply planning, prioritization, requisition follow-up, shipment tracking and coordination with procurement, finance and technical teams.
3\. Oversee importation, customs clearance, reception, transportation, warehousing and distribution, resolving complex constraints and holding freight forwarders, transporters and other service providers accountable for contractual performance and service quality.
4\. Ensure effective warehouse and inventory operations, including stock controls, traceability, storage conditions, cold-chain requirements, shelf-life monitoring, physical inventories, loss prevention, incident management and timely disposal of unserviceable or expired items.
5\. Coordinate national and subnational distribution plans, including rapid deliveries to priority, hard-to-reach and emergency-affected locations, and support inter-agency convoys and common logistics arrangements where appropriate.
6\. Lead emergency logistics readiness and surge capacity through risk-based contingency stocks, framework arrangements, scenario planning, field assessments and rapid identification of logistics capacity, needs, risks and gaps; recommend timely corrective and preparedness measures to management.
7\. Liaise with national authorities, UN agencies, the Health and Logistics Clusters, partners and service providers; represent WHO in relevant logistics coordination mechanisms and negotiations within delegated authority.
8\. Support the establishment, update and enforcement of OSL standard operating procedures, internal controls, quality-assurance arrangements and risk-mitigation measures. Ensure compliance with WHO requirements, donor conditions, good storage and distribution practices, contractual obligations and audit recommendations, and lead corrective action where gaps are identified.
9\. Monitor OSL performance, financial and risk-monitoring mechanisms, including relevant KPIs, dashboards, service-provider performance measures and BMS records; analyze trends and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior management and emergency coordination structures.
10\. Supervise and guide OSL personnel as assigned, including workforce planning, delegation, coaching, staff development and performance management promote teamwork, knowledge sharing and compliance with established procedures.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** A first-level university degree (Bachelor's level) in supply chain management, logistics, business or public administration, engineering, pharmacy, health sciences or another field relevant to the functions of the position from an accredited/recognized institution.
**Desirable:** An advanced university degree (Master's level) in one of the above fields. Professional certification in humanitarian logistics, supply-chain management, transport, warehousing Training in information management systems and their application to supply-chain monitoring.

### Experience

**Essential**: At least five years of progressively responsible professional experience, at the national and/or international level, in logistics or supply-chain operations, including experience supporting emergency or humanitarian operations, coordinating multiple supply-chain functions, previous experience in team management

**Desirable**:

- Experience providing strategic advice to senior management and leading logistics or supply-chain operations across multiple locations in a complex field setting.
- Relevant experience with WHO, the United Nations system, Health or Logistics Cluster partners, a recognized humanitarian organization or an international nongovernmental organization.
- Experience in health logistics, import/export and customs administration, warehouse and inventory management, cold chain, last-mile distribution, emergency preparedness, service-provider or contract management, and performance, financial or risk monitoring.
- Proven experience in managing a team

### Functional Skills

• Advanced knowledge of end-to-end supply-chain and logistics management in emergency and humanitarian settings, including strategic planning, forecasting, transport, customs clearance, warehousing, inventory control, cold chain and distribution.
• Strong strategic, analytical, planning and organizational skills, with the ability to translate programme priorities into supply-chain strategies, governance arrangements, SOPs, KPIs and practical risk-based solutions in complex and rapidly changing operating environments.
• Demonstrated ability to lead and develop a multidisciplinary team, manage resources and performance, establish priorities, make sound decisions under pressure and maintain business continuity in high-risk operations.
• Excellent interpersonal, advisory, coordination and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence decisions, build consensus and engage senior national authorities, UN entities, humanitarian partners and service providers with tact and diplomacy.

### **Other Skills (e.g. IT)**

• Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and demonstrated ability to use ERP and supply-chain information systems, including BMS or comparable platforms.
• Advanced skills in database and dashboard use for demand forecasting, shipment tracking, inventory management, distribution monitoring, KPI reporting and data-quality assurance.
• Working knowledge of communications and emergency logistics equipment, including radios and satellite telephones, is desirable.

### WHO Competencies

Teamwork
Respecting & promoting individual and cultural differences
Communication
Producing results
Creating an empowering and motivating environment
Ensuring the effective use of resources

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

Link to apply: [Job Description - Operations Support and Logistics (OSL) Officer (2604566)](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2604566&tz=GMT%2B03%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: Project Officer, Ethiopia (Maternity Cover)
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Project Officer, Ethiopia (Maternity Leave Cover)

**Location:** Jigjiga, Ethiopia

**Reporting to:** Project Manager, Ethiopia

**Duration:** Fixed-term contract, 11 months

**Salary:** Annual Gross salary £18,626, including employer pension contribution

**Deadline:** 17:00 UK time, Monday 26th October 2026

## Conciliation Resources

Conflict is difficult, complex and political. The world urgently needs to find different ways to respond. Conciliation Resources (CR) is an international organisation committed to stopping violent conflict and creating more peaceful societies. We work with people impacted by war and violence, bringing diverse voices together to make change that lasts. For over 25 years, we have been making peace possible. We currently have over 70 full and part-time staff members, working mainly out of the London and Australian offices. We work with over 70 locally-based and international partners worldwide.

Conciliation Resources has been active in the Horn of Africa since 2012. Our work predominantly focuses on Ethiopia and Kenya and to a lesser extent Somalia. We have locally-based staff-consultants in Kenya and Ethiopia as well as a local office in Jigjiga in the Somali regional state of Ethiopia. CR is registered as an international NGO in Ethiopia and Kenya. The Horn of Africa programme is committed to long term presence and supporting peacebuilding and conflict transformation in the region in collaboration with national, sub-national and local governments, civil society and communities. We would also like to develop the programme to meet new demands working with new partners in new areas.

## Job purpose

The Project Officer provides programmatic and logistical support necessary for the implementation of the Horn of Africa programme’s work in Ethiopia. The post holder will play a key role in liaising with partners across the areas in which we work, and in supporting the team in Jigjiga, Nairobi, and London on activity implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), and donor reporting requirements. The Project Officer is based in Jigjiga and may undertake travel within the Somali region. The Project Officer reports to a Project Manager, and works closely with our teams based in London, Nairobi and Jigjiga. The role will also work with a local implementation partner and a number of community-based organisations and networks directly supported by the programme or through the local partner including accompanying and training support to these local organisations and networks.

## Person specification

### Essential knowledge, skills and experience

- Experience of working in an administrative and team support position.
- Strong organisational skills including planning, developing, implementing and maintaining administrative systems.
- Understanding of and interest in peacebuilding and conflict transformation processes.
- Initiative, proactiveness, enthusiasm and a problem-solving approach to new challenges.
- Willingness to work irregular hours occasionally and to undertake some international travel to areas affected by conflict.
- Excellent numeracy and accuracy skills with a high level of attention to detail.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Somali and/or Amharic.
- Excellent working knowledge of Microsoft Office software packages, databases, email, internet in a Mac environment.
- Appreciation of issues of confidentiality, and cross-cultural and political sensitivity.

### Desirable knowledge, skills and experience

- Experience supporting partners on the successful joint delivery of work and accompanying local community-based organisations with limited organisational (financial and management) capacities.
- Experience of supporting monitoring, evaluation and reporting of projects.
- Experience of working with databases and handling diverse sources of information.
- Hostile environment training, or willingness to undertake hostile environment training.
- Living and working experience in Ethiopia and/or Somalia.

**Please note: applicants need to have the right to live and work in Ethiopia.**

**Qualified female applicants are highly encouraged to apply.**

jobs.title: HEAD Of Middle East Durable Solutions Platform
jobs.description:
The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956, and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced.

All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation.

DRC hosts the Middle East Durable Solutions Platform (ME DSP), a membership-based NGO platform established by DRC, NRC and IRC and later joined by Oxfam, ACF and Save the Children to strengthen evidence, programming and advocacy on solutions to displacement in and from Syria. In 2022 its scope was widened to Iraq and Yemen. Following a period of hibernation since 2023, ME DSP has secured core donor funding and is in the process of re-establishing its membership, reviewing its governance and operating model, and diversify its partnerships. ME DSP is one of three DRC-hosted solutions platforms, alongside ReDSS (East Africa and Great Lakes) and ADSP (Asia), and sits within the DRC Middle East, Asia and Europe Hub under the leadership of the Hub’s Executive Director.

The **Head of ME DSP** provides overall leadership, strategic direction and management of the Platform, a membership-based, consensus-driven platform of NGOs working on solutions to displacement across the Middle East. As the Platform’s principal convener, s/he leads engagement with members and governance structures, builds consensus around shared priorities and ensures delivery of agreed commitments; leads the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy agenda so that research is translated into programming and policy guidance; represents the Platform at senior level with members, governments and donors, UN agencies and policy makers at country regional and global levels; manages ME DSP grants, staff and consultants; and works in close collaboration with DRC’s sister platforms, ReDSS and ADSP.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership, Governance and Management**

- Facilitate the implementation of the ME DSP Strategy 2026-2028, lead the regular review of the Platform’s work plans, and ensure ME DSP maintains a strategic, neutral and member-driven role that complements existing coordination mechanisms
- Lead the re-establishment of the Platform’s membership and the review of its governance and operating model, in line with Steering Committee decisions
- Lead annual planning and budgeting and report to the Steering Committee and members on progress, risks and results; maintain the risk matrix, commission periodic evaluation of ME DSP and integrate lessons learned
- Work in close collaboration with ReDSS and ADSP to share learning, align approaches and tools, and contribute to joint NGO engagement in global solutions fora
- Accountable for people management of direct reports, including recruitment, objective setting, performance management and staff development, and for the management of ME DSP consultants

**Membership Convening and Coordination**

- Act as the Platform’s principal convener. Design and facilitate member meetings, technical working groups and consultations in an inclusive and transparent manner that builds collective ownership of the Platform’s agenda and outputs
- Facilitate consensus-building among members, managing differing priorities and resolving issues that may affect Platform decisions and delivery
- Ensure effective coordination and information sharing among members and the Steering Committee, and support members’ engagement with the Platform at country, regional and global levels
- Lead a membership engagement strategy, including the onboarding of new members and clarity on members’ roles and contributions.

**Research, Evidence and Learning**

- Define and oversee the Platform’s research and knowledge management agenda with members, initiating and commissioning studies, managing researchers and research institutions, and ensuring methodologically rigorous, research ethics and relevance to programming and policy
- Lead the analysis of regional displacement and solutions data, strategies, policies and legislation; translate evidence into programming and policy guidance, briefing papers and policy briefs; and ensure quality control of all ME DSP publications and monitoring of their uptake
- Facilitate regular technical workshops and learning events and the roll-out of learning tools and training packages, ensuring cross-learning across countries and with global developments in solutions policy and practice
- Promote the meaningful engagement of displacement-affected communities and local civil society in the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy work

**Policy Engagement and External Representation**

- Represent the Platform at senior level with governments and national authorities, donors, UN agencies, international financial institutions, regional bodies and policy makers, building trusted relationships and navigating politically sensitive contexts with discretion and in line with humanitarian principles
- Oversee the development and implementation of the Platform’s policy and advocacy strategy with members, ensuring positions are evidence-based, agreed by members and coordinated with NGO fora and durable solutions working groups in the region
- Support members’ advocacy with governmental and inter-governmental actors and engage proactively in regional and global policy processes on solutions for displacement-affected populations
- Engage research institutions, think tanks and academia, and oversee high-quality external communications reflecting members’ agreed positions

**Business Development and Project Management**

- Manage existing and future grants, including budgets, work plans, monitoring and donor reporting, ensuring timely delivery and compliance with DRC and donor policies, including safeguarding
- Develop and implement a fundraising strategy to ensure financial sustainability, including donor engagement and partnerships, in coordination with the Steering Committee

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have **Experience and technical competencies** :

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in political science, international relations, humanitarian law, migration, Middle East studies, or related field
- Understanding of the regional displacement dynamics. Excellent understanding of
- At least 8 years' relevant experience, including 5 in people management and substantial experience leading, facilitating or coordinating a membership-based, consensus-driven consortium, network, NGO forum or inter-agency platform
- Expert knowledge of durable solutions to displacement and the relevant international frameworks, with demonstrated experience in complex and contested return and reintegration contexts
- In-depth knowledge of the displacement context of the Middle East, displacement in and from Syria, Iraq and Yemen, and of the political complexities, policy landscape and coordination architecture of the region
- Demonstrated strategic leadership, ability to manage competing priorities, and ensure accountability for results
- Proven experience in grant management, budget oversight and resource mobilization
- Proven experience in leading, conducting or commissioning research, or in working in close collaboration with researchers, and in translating evidence into programming and policy guidance
- Excellent convening, facilitation and networking skills, with the ability to build trust and broker consensus among diverse organizations; outstanding interpersonal and diplomatic skills, political and cultural sensitivity, tact and impartiality
- Excellent analytical and writing skills, with proven experience producing high quality research and policy briefs and presenting complex information in an accessible manner
- Demonstrated commitment to collaborative working across organizations and with sister platforms, ability to work in a multicultural environment, and flexibility, proactive engagement and high tolerance for change, complexity and unpredictability

**In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:**

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with DRC’s vision and values.

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.* “

**Location:** Jordan/Amman with potential travel in the region

**Contract length**: 1 year contract

**Start date;** 1 Jan 2027

**Closing date for applications:** 16-11-2026.

If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit [drc.ngo/jobsupport](https://forms-hr.drc.dk/view.php?id=348161).

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

jobs.title: Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator !**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

We are looking for a Climate, Environment & Health (CEH) Coordinator to join MSF OCG.

Reporting to the Deputy General Director, the CEH Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating OCG’s strategic approach to reducing the environmental impact of its activities, while strengthening the integration of the health and humanitarian consequences of climate change into operational planning.The position works closely with the Logistics, Medical, Communication and Operations departments, supporting field missions and contributing to more relevant, responsible and effective humanitarian operations.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

- Develop and implement OCG’s strategy to address climate change and environmental issues across its activities.
- Support the integration of climate risks and evolving patterns of climate-sensitive diseases into operational planning to strengthen the relevance of operational responses.
- Promote the reduction of environmental impacts across OCG’s activities to enhance the environmental responsibility of MSF operations.
- Coordinate cross-functional initiatives on climate and environmental issues to ensure alignment and consistency across OCG.
- Develop frameworks, guidelines, and tools to support teams in effectively addressing climate risks and environmental impacts.
- Monitor progress towards climate and environmental objectives to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including overseeing the organisation’s annual carbon accounting process.
- Represent OCG in intersectional and external meetings on climate, environment, and health.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Essential: Advanced university degree in environmental health, climate change, sustainability, environmental engineering, or a related field.
- Desired: Certification in carbon accounting.

*Experience*

- Essential: Experience in a similar role or in leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders without direct hierarchical authority.
- Field experience with MSF or another humanitarian organization is an asset.

*Languages*

- English and French are mandatory.
- Additional languages are an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Carbon accounting.
- Environmental sustainability and climate change.
- Health and humanitarian impacts of climate change.
- Strategic planning and change management.
- Data analytics, monitoring, reporting, and performance tracking.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Strategic thinking.
- Influencing and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Coordination and facilitation skills.
- Communication and presentation skills.
- Project and change management skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment to diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviours and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Geneva
- Ideal start date: 1st of December 2026
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 119’964.- to CHF 137’640.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: GERENTE DE PROYECTO - CARABOBO
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. La misión de Acted es aportar asistencia humanitaria inmediata a aquellos que se encuentren en situación de necesidad al mismo tiempo que genera oportunidades a largo plazo para un crecimiento durable. Acted opera en contextos de catástrofe natural, conflicto armado y crisis socioeconómica.

Actualmente, Acted está buscando un/a gerente de proyecto para integrar nuestro equipo en la misión de Venezuela.

El/la Gerente de Proyecto, se encargará de liderar integralmente el ciclo de vida de las intervenciones en respuesta a la emergencia humanitaria post-terremoto del 24-06-2026, concentrando las acciones en la zona impactada de Morón, Estado Carabobo. Entre sus principales responsabilidades, se encargará de planificar las actividades estratégicas, realizar el seguimiento operativo en terreno para mitigar riesgos y gestionar los recursos humanos, logísticos y financieros (FLATS). Asimismo, asumirá la representación institucional de la organización ante clústeres y autoridades locales, asegurando el estricto cumplimiento de los estándares de calidad y normativas del donante.

**Funciones**

**Gestión y Ciclo de Proyecto**

- Planificar las actividades mediante la elaboración de estrategias de ejecución y planes de trabajo alineados con las normas del donante.
- Realizar el seguimiento diario de las actividades para anticipar riesgos y aplicar medidas correctivas oportunas.
- Asegurar la documentación y conformidad de cada actividad, compilando los registros que prueben su finalización.
- Preparar informes narrativos periódicos y actualizar las herramientas de seguimiento para el departamento de Desarrollo de Proyectos.

**Coordinación y Relacionamiento Externo**

- Organizar y participar en plataformas sectoriales (clústeres) y reuniones bilaterales con socios humanitarios.
- Liderar la comunicación con las autoridades locales y asegurar el compromiso y responsabilidad ante los beneficiarios.
- Apoyar la gestión de la seguridad mediante el análisis del contexto y la negociación del acceso a comunidades.

**Gestión de Recursos (FLATS)**

- **Recursos Humanos:** Estructurar el equipo, asignar responsabilidades, gestionar planes de trabajo y evaluar el desempeño del personal a cargo.
- **Logística:** Coordinar adquisiciones, verificar la calidad de los artículos adquiridos y supervisar el inventario y transporte del proyecto.
- **Finanzas:** Realizar el control de gastos mediante la previsión periódica y apoyar en la preparación de solicitudes de efectivo.

**Calidad y Desarrollo Estratégico**

- Colaborar con el departamento MEAL en el monitoreo de indicadores y alimentar la base de datos de lecciones aprendidas.
- Participar en el diseño de nuevas propuestas, aportando insumos sobre costos, personal y opciones programáticas estratégicas.

**Prevención de la explotación y el abuso sexuales**

- Crear y mantener un entorno que prevenga la explotación y el abuso sexuales y promueva la aplicación de la política de tolerancia cero y el código de conducta de ACTED.

**Perfil deseado**

**Requisitos**

Obligatorios:

- Profesional graduado (a) en: Ingeniería, Sociología, Trabajo Social, Economía, Educación, Ciencias Políticas, Estudios Internacionales, Ciencias de la Salud, Protección humanitaria, o carrera afín.
- Al menos tres (3) años de experiencia como Gerente de proyecto. Preferiblemente de proyectos de emergencia, desarrollo o dentro del sector de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (ASH/WASH).
- Experiencia en el trato con socios implementadores y autoridades locales / gubernamentales
- Experiencia en habilidades organizativas comprobadas.
- Experiencia trabajando en entornos de trabajo multicultural.
- Dominio de Paquete Microsoft Office.
- Disponibilidad total para desplazamientos frecuentes a comunidades remotas dentro del estado.
- Habilidades blandas:
- Capacidad probada para dirigir equipos multidisciplinarios y multiculturales en contextos de difícil acceso.
- Habilidades organizativas excepcionales, con capacidad para gestionar cronogramas, presupuestos y reportes técnicos de alta calidad.
- Capacidad para mantener el enfoque en la entrega de impacto humanitario con alta atención al detalle.
- Capacitad para trabajar con transparencia y flexibilidad para ajustar la estrategia ante cambios en el contexto.
- Comunicación asertiva y diplomacia para la representación institucional.

Deseables (no obligatorios):

- Experiencia en formación y capacitación.

**Condiciones**

- Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de honorarios profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de Acted en Carabobo.
- Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.
- Prestación de Servicios de forma presencia y traslados frecuentes a zonas afectadas por el doblete sísmico.
**Moron - Carabobo**

Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. - Experiencia previa en formación, facilitación de talleres y desarrollo de capacidades técnicas.

**Condiciones**

jobs.title: Project Evaluation Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23684**
Position Title: **Project Evaluation Consultant (Type B)**
Duty Station City: **Port Vila**
Duty Station Country: **Vanuatu**
Contract Type: **Consultant B**
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**
Initial duration: **2 months**
Closing date: **03 November 2026**

**Context:**

Since 2015, more than 30 per cent of Ni-Vanuatu citizens have experienced temporary or protracted displacement due to disasters. Vanuatu's approximately 300,000 people (Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, 2020) spread across 83 islands are exposed to cyclones, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, ashfalls, earthquakes, mudslides, flooding and drought. As the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events increases due to climate change, disasters pose a primary threat to Vanuatu's national security and human development.

Tropical Cyclones (TC) Judy and Kevin (both of Category 4 intensity) made landfall over Vanuatu on 1 and 3 March 2023. TC Judy and Kevin affected an estimated 24,657 households (123,288 people) with 90 per cent of houses in Shefa and Tafea provinces destroyed or severely damaged. The cumulative impact of compounding events such as previous cyclones (TC Harold), high La Nina rainfall and COVID-19, has had a devastating impact on basic living conditions, access to basic services, livelihoods, and coping capacities. While traditional resilience in Vanuatu is strong, emergency preparedness needs strengthening at all levels - national, provincial, area council and community – particularly in light of intensifying climate change impacts in the Pacific.

In response, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing a project to support the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) in strengthening the capacity of national and provincial government institutions, Community Disaster and Climate Change Committees (CDCCCs), Area Councils, faith-based organizations, and community leaders — particularly women leaders — to develop and maintain safe and dignified evacuation arrangements during emergencies.

This builds on the existing work being undertaken by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster which brings together key partners to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities. It will strengthen and extend the work of the DECM Cluster to provincial and community level, moving towards improved localization of emergency response measures in Vanuatu.

Specifically, the Sef Ples Blong Yumi Phase 2 project funded by the Government of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), implemented by the National Disaster Management Office, Vanuatu in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration, supports the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness, coordination, and evacuation centre management across multiple hazards. The project focuses on strengthening the DECM Cluster’s coordination capacity, updating and rolling out the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and Evacuation Toolbox / Training Materials, improving information management systems, and supporting preparedness at national, provincial, and Area Council levels.

**The Objective of the project is:**

To contribute to the protection and resilience of people at risk of displacement in Vanuatu by supporting the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness and evacuation procedures.

The project will update and finalize the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and developing the Evacuations Toolbox / Training Materials for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to strengthen:

1. National, provincial and area council-level coordination of evacuations.
2. Capacity of communities, CDCCCs, faith-based groups to manage and lead their own community-based evacuations in ways that both draws on traditional knowledge about evacuations and increases protections for vulnerable groups, especially women, children, older people and people with disability.

The Outcomes and Outputs of this project are the following:

Outcome 1: Government, faith-based groups and communities have enhanced capacity to coordinate, develop, maintain and monitor safe, dignified evacuation accommodation in emergencies.

Output 1.1: Improved information management at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in sudden-onset emergencies.

Output 1.2: Improved coordination at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in emergencies.

Output 1.3: Updated National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines and Evacuations Toolbox for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

Output 1.4: Roll out of Evacuations Toolbox training for national trainers, Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Disaster Risk Reduction - Humanitarian

Project code: CC0083

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**The Final Evaluation Report shall include the following sections:**

- Executive Summary
- Introduction, objectives, methodology, and limitations
- Findings (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability and cross-cutting issues)
- Discussions of outcomes and results
- Lessons learned and good practices (success factors and/or those which challenged performance)
- Conclusions
- Recommendations
- Annexes (i.e. TOR, Data Sources, Evaluation Matrix, etc.)
- Further details of the deliverables are:

**Other general tasks to be undertaken as part of this assignment will include**
- Providing advice and input to project direction and methods.
- Reporting to and keeping up good communication with National Programme Officer and Project Manager.
- Attendance at project meetings online or in person.
- Meetings, where requested, with IOM Chief of Mission, IOM Project Staff, or Government of Vanuatu representatives.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Performance should be assessed according to the tangible and measurable deliverables of the work assignment as stated in Section 7 above.
- Payment instalments to be made upon the satisfactory completion of each of the deliverables and approval by the project manager.
- Performance will be assessed against the outputs as provided above.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- The evaluator should preferably have a master's degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 2 years of relevant professional experience.
- Or the evaluator should have a bachelors degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 4 years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in carrying out similar evaluation assignments for projects related to humanitarian preparedness, response, recovery, disaster resilience, climate change, evacuation center management, or displacement and evacuation center management coordination.
- Demonstrated capacity to coordinate with and secure key informants (including government actors, community networks, other key stakeholders, and community participants) is required.
- Minimum 4 years of experience working with research, policy development, analysis, monitoring and evaluation, and program evaluation preferably in the field of climate change, disaster risk reduction, emergency response, and / or environment.
- Understanding of Vanuatu displacement, emergency response, evacuation centres, and climate change context are an advantage
- Experience of working in the Pacific region is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Computer skills required (MS Word and basic MS Excel) for reporting.
- Strong facilitation, mentoring, and stakeholder coordination skills.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, Fluency in Bislama and English language is required. Working knowledge of French is an advantage.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

One trip to Port Vila will be required as part of this ToR:
Trip 1: Approximately 10 days (estimated early - December 2026 or early January 2027) – this travel is required to coordinate evaluation activities, attend meetings, and conduct key informant interviews. Exact dates of the trip to be coordinated between IOM Project Management Team and the selected evaluator(s).
If budget allows a second trip can be considered in mid or late January 2027.
IOM will cover costs relating to round trip airfares, accommodation, and a consultant / evaluator daily subsistence allowance. Travel and health insurance will not be covered by IOM and is the responsibility of the consultant / selected evaluator(s).

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
