jobs.title: Senior Crafts and Artisan Development Manager
jobs.description:
Turquoise Mountain exists to support artisans and communities and revitalize their heritage. The Senior Manager - Crafts and Artisan Development will uphold the exceptional crafts heritage of Afghanistan and enable and develop the ecosystem of support provided to artisans and communities across a range of crafts traditions. Reporting to the Head of Programs, this role will lead Turquoise Mountain Afghanistan’s work to strengthen traditional crafts and develop skilled artisans. It will support and improve continuity of artisan skills, production and product quality across Calligraphy, Miniature Painting, Jewellery-Making, Gem-Cutting, Woodwork, Embroidery, and Carpets. The role will provide technical leadership to the training faculties and support master artisans and trainers to pass their knowledge to new generations.

The role will connect craft training - delivered through targeted short and medium-term courses - with professional workshop practice, production improvement, business development and market needs – supporting throughout all areas the preservation and continuity of Afghanistan’s craft heritage. Working with master artisans, trainers, production colleagues, and creative / commercial teams, the postholder will strengthen apprenticeship and skills-transfer systems, support high-quality and culturally authentic production, identify and support existing master artisans, and help develop master artisans for the future. Training will respond to artisan development needs as well as production and market requirements.

The postholder will directly supervise the training faculties and training administration function in accordance with the approved organisational structure. They will support master artisans and trainers through mentoring, curriculum oversight, and practical quality assurance, and promote an inclusive learning environment. Planning, budgeting, grant compliance, monitoring, reporting, and coordination will support the delivery and sustainability of these craft and artisan development outcomes. The role will work across the country programme and with the Institute, monitoring and evaluation, operations, finance, production, business development, and creative and commercial teams; it will not line-manage production, commercial, or central creative teams unless specifically delegated through the approved organisational structure.

**Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

**Craft & Artisan Development, Training & Quality**

- Lead and develop the direction for TM Afghanistan’s crafts, artisan development, and training functions, in coordination with the Head of Programs, to ensure traditional craft skills preservation and continuity, artisan progression, and product quality, and in line with organisational objectives.
- Provide technical and management oversight to the training faculties for Calligraphy, Miniature Painting, Woodwork, Jewellery-Making, Gem-Cutting, Embroidery, and Carpet Design & Graphing courses.
- Ensure craft learning promotes, preserves, and celebrates Afghanistan’s heritage, identifying master artisans and technical specialists, ensuring high-quality knowledge of traditional techniques, materials, design, and cultural context is upheld at all stages.
- Lead regular reviews of training scope and curriculum components, workshop quality and fit-out, production standards, and artisan performance, implementing practical improvement plans with master artisans, technical trainers, and production teams.
- Implement and oversee TM’s foundational business training for new artisan enterprises and connect it with practical production, quality, pricing, and market-readiness needs.
- Work directly with TM global creative team to develop representative ranges in each craft type, that both directly relate to technical components and milestones during training and enable onward production and market opportunities for individual artisans and business.
- Conduct regular review of curriculum content, assessment and attainment, and update based on market opportunities, developing trends and demand, and upholding the authentic crafts heritage of Afghanistan.
- Contribute specialist advice to TM’s craft-sector direction and lead research and documentation of traditional techniques, materials, cultural narratives, workshop practices, product quality, and market opportunities. Use findings to inform curricula, product improvement, heritage preservation, and practical progression routes for artisans.
- Strengthen apprenticeship and skills-transfer systems, including trainer observation and support, learner assessment, practical workshop quality assurance, curriculum review, and certification or accreditation where appropriate, in coordination with relevant authorities and technical experts.
- Follow up with graduates and apprentices to understand their craft progression, work and enterprise opportunities, continued use of traditional skills, and views on the quality and relevance of training.

**Promotion & Partnerships**

- Participate in regular alignment sessions with TM creative / commercial teams, to ensure a holistic approach that ensures full TM ecosystem supports artisans and local and global promotion for artisan products, commercial opportunities and creative partnerships connection.
- Identify and build partnerships that support master artisans, strengthen local craft production, improve quality and innovation, and create sustainable opportunities for artisans.
- Work with the local and global teams to create an annual schedule of exhibitions and promotional events to present Afghan craft, share artisans’ work, and learn from client and market feedback.
- Support connecting commercial viability with fair opportunities for artisans and the preservation of traditional craft skills.

**Representation & Stakeholder Coordination**

- Engage with Afghanistan authorities, including the Technical & Vocational Education and Training Authority and the Ministry of Industry & Commerce, on craft skills, apprenticeships, training quality, and sector development.
- Engage and work with international accreditation authority of City & Guilds to further develop certification options for trainees.
- Represent TM in relevant craft, training, and artisan development networks and coordination forums.
- Provide craft and artisan development inputs to donor proposals, budgets, engagement, and reporting, in coordination with the Country Director, Head of Programs, and relevant in-country and global teams, including global Creative and Commercial teams.

**Team Management**

- Manage and develop a team of course trainers, technical experts, consultants and education administrators, to deliver the programmes as described.
- Oversee day-to-day team operations, including attendance, leave, and travel approvals, so teams can deliver consistent training and technical support.
- Maintain clear working relationships and feedback processes with in-country and global creative, commercial, production, and business development teams, connecting craft development priorities with organisational objectives.
- Recruit, induct, supervise, and develop trainers and training staff, in coordination with Human Resources and relevant line managers; encourage strong craft practice, effective teaching, and knowledge-sharing.
- Promote fair and transparent access to training and apprenticeships, and support participation, attendance, completion, and progression for women and other underrepresented artisans.
- Promote equal opportunity and inclusion for staff, artisans, trainers, and learners, including practical steps that enable women and underrepresented groups to participate and progress.
- Promote Turquoise Mountain’s values and a respectful, collaborative working environment, with shared accountability for craft quality and artisan development.

This list is not exhaustive, and other duties may be required as determined by the needs of the organisation.

**Key working relationships / cross-working**

**Internal:** Turquoise Mountain Institute of Afghan Arts and Architecture; in-country craft, training, monitoring and evaluation, operations, finance, production, business development, and sales teams; and central creative and commercial teams.

**External:** Master artisans, craft producers, training partners, clients, donors, partners, and Afghanistan authorities.

**Professional approach:**

A committed and practical crafts professional who respects artisans’ knowledge and helps teams strengthen their technical practice. Able to guide trainers and master artisans, work across training and production, and ensure craft development reflects heritage, learner needs, quality standards, and market realities. Brings sound organisation and accountability to support these outcomes.

**Experience:**

- Substantial practical experience in one or more traditional crafts, craft production, or artisan development, including direct work with master artisans or craft enterprises.
- Experience developing artisans’ technical skills, supporting apprenticeship or skills-transfer systems, and mentoring trainers or master artisans.
- Experience improving product quality and workshop practice, including quality assurance, production processes, or translating design and market requirements into production.
- Experience overseeing technical curricula or training programmes for traditional crafts; relevant vocational training or education experience is an asset.
- Demonstrated ability to apply creative or technical knowledge in practical workshop settings and contribute to the preservation of craft heritage.
- Experience managing or contributing to programmes, workplans, budgets, or donor requirements is an asset; strong crafts and artisan-development expertise is the priority.
- Experience liaising with authorities, training partners, or external craft-sector stakeholders is an asset.
- Experience working in Afghanistan is an asset.

**Personal Attributes & Skills:**

- Committed to preserving and promoting Afghanistan’s traditional crafts and heritage.
- Able to understand the links between craft disciplines, artisan needs, training, workshop production, and product quality.
- Collaborative and respectful, with the ability to build trust and accountability with artisans, master artisans, trainers, and colleagues.
- Clear verbal and written communication, facilitation, mentoring, and technical reporting skills.
- Able to support team development, give and receive constructive feedback, and address problems or conflict appropriately.
- Strong practical planning, prioritisation, problem-solving, and analytical skills, with sound budget-management ability to support craft activities.
- Able to turn artisan, learner, production, and market needs into relevant training and craft-development plans.
- Able to provide technical leadership, make timely decisions, and help teams meet agreed craft-quality and artisan-development outcomes.
- Willingness to live and work in Afghanistan

**Digital skills and experience:**

Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint), with experience using digital tools for training records, craft quality, production planning, and programme tracking.

**Language skills:**

Fluency in international-standard spoken and written English is essential. Professional working proficiency in Dari and Pashto is strongly desirable. The ability to work effectively in multilingual environments and through interpretation is required.

jobs.title: Training on Practical Business Skills, Market Systems and Cross-Cutting Capacity Building Training for Livelihoods Groups
jobs.description:
## 1. Background and Context

Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO), in partnership with the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) and with funding from the IKEA Foundation, implements a Livelihoods Programme in the Dadaab Refugee Complex, Garissa County. The programme supports refugee and host-community households to build sustainable, market-oriented livelihoods, with a particular focus on agriculture and allied sectors such as poultry, honey value chain, livestock (meat and milk), and textiles.

Through a rigorous identification process, the programme has organized 350 participants into 10 livelihoods groups of 35 members each (aggregate unit), distributed equally between refugee and host communities (50% / 50%), and drawn from Ifo1, and Dagahaley camps and neighbouring host-community villages including Bulla Kheir and Dadaab Host. Members have self-selected livelihoods sectors and are now ready to move from basic registration into structured capacity building that equips them to run their enterprises profitably and sustainably.

SOLO/NRC now seeks to engage a qualified training consultant or firm to design and deliver a practical, hands-on training package covering two complementary thematic areas: (a) core business skills, and (b) market participation and cross-cutting skills including gender and social inclusion, leadership, life skills, legal awareness, and quality and branding.

## 2. Rationale

Many group members currently operate small-scale production activities with limited exposure to formal business practice: informal or absent record keeping, ad hoc pricing that does not reliably cover costs, weak customer care and marketing practice, and limited experience negotiating with buyers or honouring contracts. Refugee members in particular face additional barriers to market participation, including restricted movement, limited legal and regulatory awareness, and constrained access to formal markets, while women across both communities often face compounded barriers linked to time poverty, decision-making power, and access to leadership roles within groups.

A structured, practical training package is therefore required to convert production-focused groups into viable, market-oriented enterprises; to strengthen group governance and inclusion so that gains are equitably shared; and to build the confidence, negotiation ability, and legal literacy members need to participate safely and profitably in local markets.

## 3. Purpose and Objectives

### 3.1 Overall Objective

To strengthen the business, market participation, governance, and life-skills capacities of 350 members of 10 SOLO/NRC-supported livelihoods groups in Dadaab, enabling them to operate viable, market-oriented, and gender-inclusive enterprises.

### 3.2 Specific Objectives

1. Equip participants with practical entrepreneurship, record keeping, costing and pricing, customer care, and marketing skills applicable to their specific livelihoods sector.
2. Build participants' understanding of local market dynamics and demand, and strengthen their negotiation and contract management skills.
3. Strengthen gender and social inclusion practice, and leadership and governance capacity, within the 10 groups.
4. Build participants' life skills and soft skills to support individual and collective decision-making, resilience, and cooperation.
5. Raise awareness of the legal and regulatory environment relevant to trading and group enterprise in and around Dadaab.
6. Strengthen participants' understanding and practice of product quality and branding to improve market competitiveness.

## 4. Scope of Work

The assignment covers two complementary training components, to be delivered to each of the 10 groups. The consultant/firm is expected to develop a detailed curriculum against the indicative content below, adapt it to the specific sectors and literacy levels of each group, and translate/deliver in Somali and/or Kiswahili as appropriate.

### 4.1 Component A. Practical Business Skills

**Sub-topic, indicative content, and indicative duration**

Entrepreneurship; entrepreneurial mindset; opportunity identification; business planning basics tailored to the participant's sector (poultry, kitchen gardening, crop farming, livestock) for 0.5 day

Record keeping: Simple, low-literacy-friendly tools for recording sales, expenses, stock, and savings; separating business and household finances for 1 day

Costing and pricing: Calculating production/unit costs, setting profitable prices, break-even basics, responding to competitor and seasonal price changes, for 1 day

Customer care: building customer relationships and trust, handling complaints, and repeat-business practices for 0.5 day

Marketing strategies: identifying customers and market channels, low-cost promotion, and group/collective marketing approaches for 1 day

### 4.2 Component B. Market Participation, Governance, and Crosscutting Skills

**Sub-topic, Indicative content and Indicative duration**

Market dynamics and demand: Understanding local/Dadaab market structures, seasonality, demand assessment, and identifying viable market opportunities for 1 day

Negotiation skills: Practical negotiation techniques with buyers, suppliers, and off-takers, including role-play practice for 0.5 day

Contract management: understanding, negotiating, and honoring simple supply/off-take agreements; managing disputes for 0.5 day

Gender and social inclusion, leadership and governance, GESI awareness, equitable participation in group decision-making, group leadership roles, and transparent and accountable group governance structures for 1 day

Life skills and soft skills: communication, teamwork, problem-solving, conflict resolution, stress management, and goal setting for 0.5 day

Legal and regulatory awareness; relevant national and county trading regulations; business registration basics; rights and obligations of refugee and host traders for 0.5 day.

Quality and branding; basic quality control/assurance for produce and simple branding and packaging to strengthen market competitiveness for 1 day.

*Total indicative contact time is 4 days for Component A and 5 days for Component B per group (9 training days), plus follow-up coaching described in Section 7. The consultant/firm may propose an alternative sequencing or balance of days, with justification, in their technical proposal.*

## 5. Target Participants

Livelihoods groups formed under the SOLO/NRC registration exercise - 10

Members per group, standard group size - 35

Total participants: 10 groups × 35 members = 350

Community distribution: Refugee community / Host community (50% / 50%)

Camp locations include Ifo1 and Dagahaley camps (5 groups) and Host-community locations - Bulla Kheir, Dadaab (5 groups)

Participants include both male and female members across a wide age range, with varying levels of literacy. The consultant/firm must design and facilitate sessions that are accessible to low-literacy adult learners and give equal opportunity for participation to women, men, youth and persons with disabilities. SOLO/NRC will share group-level lists (anonymized) confirming exact composition by sex, age, camp/village, and sector at contract signing.

## 6. Training Methodology

The training must be practical and participatory and should draw on adult-learning principles. At minimum, the consultants/firm are expected to:

- Use experiential, hands-on methods: role play, simulations, group work, case studies, and, where feasible, market/field visits rather than lecture-based delivery.
- Adapt materials for low-literacy participants, using pictorial, oral, and demonstration-based tools alongside written materials.
- Deliver in Somali, with facilitators fluent in the languages spoken by participants.
- Apply gender-sensitive facilitation, ensuring equal voice and participation for women and men and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities.
- Conduct a pre-training assessment to establish baseline knowledge/skills and a post-training assessment to measure learning gains.
- Support each group to produce a simple, practical output from the training (e.g., a basic costing sheet, record-keeping template, or group action plan) rather than knowledge alone.
- Provide at least two follow-up coaching/mentoring visits per group after the classroom training to reinforce learning and support application (see Section 7).

## 7. Duration and Indicative Schedule

The assignment is expected to run over approximately 8–10 weeks from contract signing, inclusive of inception, delivery to all 10 groups, follow-up coaching, and reporting. This is an indicative timeframe; the consultants/firm should propose a detailed work plan and team composition (e.g., number of parallel facilitation teams) in their technical proposal, with justification for any variation from the indicative schedule below.

**Phase**

**Activity**

**Indicative duration**

Phase 1

Inception: desk review, curriculum design/adaptation, translation of materials, submission of inception report and training plan - 1 week

Phase 2

Delivery of Component A and Component B classroom training to all 10 groups (9 contact days per group; groups may be trained in parallel by a facilitation team or sequentially) - 4–6 weeks

Phase 3

Follow-up coaching/mentoring visits (minimum two per group) and post-training assessment- 2–3 weeks

Phase 4

Consolidation, final reporting and handover of materials and datasets - 1 week

*Exact start and end dates will be confirmed at contract signing.*

## 8. Deliverables

**Deliverable**

Inception report, including finalized curriculum, session plans, and translated/localized training materials— Within 1 week of contract signing

Pre- and post-training assessment tools and completed assessment data/report

Tools before delivery; report after each group's training

Signed attendance registers for all 10 groups, disaggregated by sex, age, camp/host village, and group—throughout delivery

Group-level practical outputs (e.g., costing sheets, record-keeping templates, group action plans)

By end of classroom training per group; follow-up coaching/mentoring visit reports (minimum 2 per group) throughout Phase 3

Final training report, including methodology, participation data, assessment results, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations within 2 weeks of assignment completion

Provide full set of training materials/manuals and a facilitator's guide handed over to SOLO/NRC for future use with final report.

## 9. Roles and Responsibilities

**SOLO / NRC will**

Mobilize and confirm participants and group schedules

Arrange venues, seating and any required camp access/movement permissions

Provide available baseline/registration data on groups (sector, camp/village, sex, age)

Provide a technical focal point for oversight, quality assurance and approvals

Cover participant transport/refreshments if budgeted separately from this contract

**The Consultant / Firm will**

Design and adapt the curriculum and all training materials

Provide qualified, experienced facilitators for all sessions

Deliver all training, assessments and coaching visits per the agreed schedule

Prepare and submit all deliverables in Section 8 to agreed quality and timelines

Comply with SOLO/NRC and donor safeguarding, PSEA and code-of-conduct requirements

## 10. Duty Station and Reporting

The assignment will be delivered in Dadaab and Bula Kheir, with sessions held in Ifo 1 and Dagahley camps and in the listed host-community villages. The consultants/firm is responsible for its own travel, accommodation and logistics within Dadaab unless otherwise agreed in the contract.

The consultant/firm will report to the SOLO Livelihoods Project Manager, in coordination with the NRC livelihoods focal point, and will provide brief progress updates after each group's training in addition to the formal deliverables listed above.

## 11. Required Qualifications and Experience

The firm (or team) should demonstrate:

- Registration as a training consultant, firm or institution, with a valid business registration and tax compliance certificate.
- A minimum of 3–5 years' experience designing and delivering business/entrepreneurship or market systems development (MSD) training, preferably with refugee, IDP or host-community populations.
- Demonstrated experience working in Dadaab, Garissa County, or comparable arid/semi-arid and displacement-affected contexts.
- A facilitation team with combined expertise across all thematic areas in Section 4, including at least one facilitator experienced in gender and social inclusion (GESI) programming.
- Facilitators fluent in Somali, with experience adapting training for low-literacy adult audiences.
- A track record of participatory, practical training methodology (not purely lecture-based), supported by references or sample materials.
- Familiarity with humanitarian/NGO safeguarding standards, including PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) and child safeguarding.
- Logistical capacity to mobilize a facilitation team to deliver training across 10 groups within the proposed timeframe.

## 12. Safeguarding, Ethics and Data Protection

The consultant/firm and all facilitators must sign and comply with SOLO’s Code of Conduct, Child Safeguarding Policy, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) policy prior to engagement. Any incidents or concerns arising during training must be reported immediately through SOLO's safeguarding reporting channels.

All participant data (names, ID/phone numbers, attendance and assessment records) collected during the assignment is confidential and remains the property of SOLO. The firm may not share, publish or reuse participant data for any purpose outside this assignment without prior written consent, and must securely store and, on request, delete or return all such data at the end of the assignment.

## 13. Budget and Payment Terms

Interested consultants/firms must submit a detailed, itemized financial proposal in Kenya Shillings (KES) covering facilitator fees, training materials, travel/logistics within Dadaab, and any other costs required to deliver the scope of work.

Payment will be made in instalments linked to approved deliverables, indicatively: 30% on submission and approval of the inception report; 40% on completion of training and coaching for all 10 groups; 30% on submission and approval of the final report and materials. Exact terms will be confirmed in the signed contract, subject to applicable taxes.

## 14. Evaluation Criteria

Technical proposals meeting a minimum qualifying score of 70% will have their financial proposals opened and scored. Overall award will be based on the combined technical and financial score below.

**Criteria**

Technical proposal: understanding of the assignment, methodology, work plan, and curriculum outline- 30%

Team composition and qualifications, including thematic coverage and language capacity- 20%

Relevant experience in Dadaab/refugee or comparable contexts, with references- 20%

Financial proposal (cost-effectiveness and value for money)- 30%

**Total - 100%**

jobs.title: P&C Operations Training Specialist
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The P&C Training & Learning Delivery Specialist ensures employees and managers have the knowledge and skills to work effectively as P&C transformation initiatives roll out. This role owns end-to-end training design and delivery for Workday enhancements, process changes, and digital capability rollouts.

Working closely with the Change Management Specialist, Business Analysts, and P&C Partners, this role builds training on a real understanding of stakeholder needs and readiness — turning the Change Management Specialist's impact assessments into practical, audience-appropriate learning experiences, and applying the reusable frameworks, tools, and methodology to deliver consistently at scale.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training Design & Delivery**

- Lead the end-to-end design and delivery of training programs for Workday enhancements, process changes, and digital capability rollouts — developing and executing training in line with the approach and standards set out in the Global Workday Learning Strategy and Rollout Training Methodology.
- Design and conduct training needs assessments ahead of every major rollout, building on the Change Management Specialist's stakeholder impact assessments, with a consistent methodology identifying what each user group needs, in what format, and by when
- Create a range of training assets appropriate to audience and context — job aids, quick reference guides, process guides, facilitator guides, and e-learning content — establishing reusable templates and standards
- Facilitate live and virtual training sessions for P&C and non-P&C users across the organization, adapting delivery style for different audiences and contexts
- Build an evaluation framework to measure training effectiveness through feedback, assessment, and post-training adoption data, iterating on content and delivery based on findings
- Establish and maintain a centralized training library, creating the structure and governance to keep materials current as systems and processes evolve

**Partnership & Knowledge Management**

- Partner closely with the Change Management Specialist to ensure training design is grounded in real stakeholder readiness and impact findings, and coordinate on rollout timing and sequencing
- Track training completion and content-effectiveness metrics, feeding into the team's broader adoption reporting
- Build the team's training capability through reusable templates, toolkits, and standards applied across all P&C transformation projects
- Conduct post-implementation reviews on training effectiveness, using findings to improve future delivery
- Stay current on Workday training approaches and adult learning principles

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience**

- 3–5 years of experience in training/learning & development, ideally including system rollouts or process change contexts
- Experience building training tools, templates, or frameworks
- Solid working knowledge of Workday from an end-user or training perspective is a strong advantage
- Instructional design background or certification is an advantage
- Experience in a complex, matrixed organization preferred
- Experience creating microlearning content for adult learners and/or working with tools like Articulate 360, Adobe Suite, Moodle, or equivalent

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Instructional design capability: able to assess needs, build practical learning materials, and adapt content for different roles, formats, and audiences
- Confident facilitator of live and virtual sessions for diverse groups
- Clear and adaptable communicator across audiences
- Data-aware: able to define training effectiveness metrics, interpret findings, and recommend action
- Well-organized and able to manage multiple concurrent workstreams without losing detail

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week.

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Colombia.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: 22323 Project Officer (Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS))
23438 Finance Officer (Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA))
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director – Management (DRD-M) in Dakar, and the direct supervision of the Project Finance and Budget Officer – Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA) in close coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), the Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in the programmes budget, accounts, and financial reports of all the implementing Country Offices (COs), provide support to the programmatic unit of the MPRR-SSA team in the areas of financial monitoring and reporting. The Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will work closely with the European Commission Compliance Unit in IOM Global Office Brussels, Regional Office, as well as central units at Headquarters (HQ).

The MPRR-SSA is an EU-funded programme that is implemented in 16 countries of sub-Saharan Africa, including Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, Chad, Ethiopia, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, Somalia, and Sudan.

**Responsibilities**

1. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to monitor and oversee the financial management of all activities, including oversight of financial expenditure and accountability, and undertake financial analysis of all activities in the offices implementing the MPRR-SSA programme.
2. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to oversee and coordinate the preparation and review of EU financial reports in accordance with IOM regulations and EU regulations and established procedures.
3. In coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), Project Managers, the Regional Office (RO) Coordination Unit, Global Office Brussels, and Resources Management Officers (RMOs), prepare budget reports, proposals, and revisions in the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA).
4. Contribute to the budget control process and analyse variances between the budget and actual expenditures for MPRR-SSA projects.
5. Contribute to the creation of draft general instructions and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure compliance with the general instructions of IOM and relevant permanent instructions in the areas of general administration, finance, Supply Chain, Information and Communications Technology (ICT), and Human Resources (HR).
6. Contribute to the capacity building initiatives to train local staff on EU and IOM’s administrative/financial policies and procedures.
7. As assigned by the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA), undertake travel to offices in view to building financial management capacity of administrative and finance staff in the field.
8. Provide support to the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in facilitating the financial audit of the MPRR-SSA programme in accordance with the donor agreements.
9. Assess monthly financial reports and advise on resolving anomalies and unusual trends.
10. Provide advice and guidance to Country Offices (COs) in the Region with management of implementing Partners (IP) under the MPRR-SSA programme.
11. Contribute to ensure compliance with all administrative and financial rules, instructions, regulations, and procedures related to the EU-funded project(s).
12. In coordination with the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) and upon approval of the Regional Financial Comptroller, undertake duty travel to the CO to increase capacity building in financial reporting in relation to assigned projects.
13. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Auditing, or related fields from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in accounting, financial management and reporting;
- Experience in preparing clear and concise financial and management reports;
- Experience working in and with international institutions;
- Experience with internal control assessment, internal or external audit;
- Previous work experience in the region is an advantage;
- Previous working experience in emergency operations is an advantage; and,
- Experience with EU budgeting rules is mandatory.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS);
- Knowledge of the IOM/UN accounting system, software, and procedures, Common System regulations, policies, and procedures is a distinct advantage;
- Familiarity with financial oversight and public administration is an advantage; and,
- Knowledge of MS Office products and good computer literacy skills are required.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Global Finance and Compliance Business Partner
jobs.description:
**Location:** United Kingdom (preferred), or other approved locations where HelpAge International is legally able to employ staff (Ethiopia, Italy, Jordan, Kenya, Spain, Tanzania, Türkiye and Zimbabwe)

**Department:** Business Support Team

**Reports to (Line Manager):** Director of Finance & Business Support

**Responsible for (Line managing):** N/A

**Grade:** E- [https://helpage.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/external/HR/Global%20Finance%20%26%20Comp%20BP-Grade%20E%20Salary%20Ranges.xlsx?d=w430eb70dde154b1ea879aac96f47c68f&csf=1&web=1&e=IgX0R7](https://helpage.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/external/HR/Global%20Finance%20%26%20Comp%20BP-Grade%20E%20Salary%20Ranges.xlsx?d=w430eb70dde154b1ea879aac96f47c68f&csf=1&web=1&e=IgX0R7)

**Contract Type:** Open ended

**About HelpAge**

HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives.

Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience.

## **About the Job**

The Global Finance & Compliance Business Partner provides high-quality financial business partnering support and oversight to assigned programmes and organisational initiatives.

The role supports managers in ensuring compliance to policy in areas of budgeting, proposal development, donor compliance, and financial reporting. The post holder will help colleagues make informed financial decisions while ensuring compliance with organisational, donor, and regulatory requirements.

The role also lead the internal audit planning and implementation, compliance, and assurance activities across corporate and partner financial reporting.

## Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities

**Financial Business Partnering**

- Build strong relationships with budget holders and managers, providing proactive financial advice, support and oversight.
- Support managers in understanding financial compliance and managing risks.
- Contribute to financial decision-making through analysis, insight and challenge.

**Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Planning**

- Support the preparation of programme budgets, and financial plans with a view to ensuring compliance with policy.
- Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and provide timely feedback on variances, risks and mitigation
- Contribute to organisational financial planning processes and reporting cycles.
- Support grant managers and programme teams in understanding donor rules and compliance requirements.
- Monitor and advise on cost recovery, co-funding requirements, and financial risks associated with grants.

**Partner Financial Management**

- Support financial oversight of implementing partners in line with HelpAge’s partner-led approach.
- Review partner financial reports and supporting documentation.
- Support partner financial assessments, capacity strengthening initiatives, and compliance reviews.
- Audit selected partner organisations in line with agreed audit plan

**Compliance and Audit**

- Analyse monthly management information prepared for senior management and provide audit and assurance on them
- Support the design of relevant financial reports, dashboards and performance reports needed to manage performance and risk.
- Support the annual external audit preparation and process.
- Develop and propose an annual internal audit plan for review and approval by the Audit & Risk Committee, ensuring appropriate oversight and safeguards to maintain the independence of internal audit activities.
- Develop and maintain Internal Audit Procedures to ensure best practice and that the audits address specific areas of identified risk withing corporate accounts and programmes/partners activities
- Coordinate and implement the approved internal audit plan in accordance with established procedures and appropriate independence safeguards. At the conclusion of each audit, communicate findings to Director of Finance and Business Support Department or partner organisation, document management responses and agree corrective action plans.
- Monitor and report on the implementation of any recommendations;

Skills and experience required

**Essential**

- Professional accounting qualification or equivalent audit certification and experience.
- Significant experience in financial management, budgeting and financial reporting.
- Experience working within an NGO, charity or similar organisation.
- Strong understanding of donor-funded programmes and donor compliance requirements.
- Experience in financial audit, compliance, and investigation.
- Good communication, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.
- Strong Excel and financial systems skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work collaboratively across teams.

**Desirable**

- Experience supporting partner-led programming and partner financial management.
- Experience preparing donor budgets and donor financial reports.
- Knowledge of UK charity finance requirements.
- Knowledge of Charity SORP and auditing standards
- Experience using MS Business Dynamics or similar accounting systems.
- Experience supporting finance process improvements and risk management.

## Key Behavioural Competencies

Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together.

Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further.

Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged.

Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners.

Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Policies and Code of Conduct**

As a HelpAge International employee, you are expected to comply with all organisational policies and standards, and to conduct yourself in a manner consistent with our values at all times.

This includes, but is not limited to:

- Code of Conduct
- Safeguarding Policy and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Anti-Fraud and Bribery Policy
- Anti-Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy
- Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy
- Raising a Concern (Whistleblowing) Policy
- Social Media Policy

All staff are required to familiarise themselves with these policies, complete any mandatory training, and adhere to them throughout their employment with HelpAge International.

**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
- Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
- Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
- Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

jobs.title: MOZAMBIQUE - DEPUTY COUNTRY DIRECTOR FOR PROGRAMS (M/F) - CABO DELGADO
jobs.description:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: ASAP**
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**
**Location: CABO DELGADO**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.

Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.

At the beginning of 2025, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganisation of operations to maintain essential activities. This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement and unpredictable access since mid-2024.

In early 2026, the mission entered a new phase with the confirmation of significant short-term emergency funding, alongside the launch of a major 3-year development-oriented WASH/FSL/Education project in Consortium. This shift requires strengthened programmatic oversight to manage simultaneous emergency and longer-term interventions within a rapidly evolving operational context.

Despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, IFSAN, UNICEF and WFP.

Projects and activities include:

\- Rapid Response Mechanism to shocks (conflict, natural disasters, epidemics): multisectoral WASH / Food / Shelter-NFI assistance through CVA or in-kind distributions

\- WASH: rehabilitation of large water networks, water points construction/rehabilitation, WASH in schools and health facilities, rainwater harvesting systems, sanitation and hygiene promotion

\- FSL: seeds and equipment distributions, support to cooperatives, cash-for-work and income-generating activities

\- Shelter/NFI: mainly emergency shelter and NFI through RRM

Around 50 staff in total across the mission in April 2026, but it will increase in May/June with the new funding.

SI operates 3 bases:

• Pemba (Coordination / Operational Base): 27 staff

• Mueda (Operational Base): 19 staff

• Mocímboa da Praia (Operational Sub-base): 4 staff

• Chiure (Operational Sub-base) to be opened: 6 staff

The DCDP is based in Pemba and covers operations in all bases of SI in Mozambique.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) is responsible for the overall supervision, quality and strategic orientation of Solidarités International programmatic operations and MEAL systems in Cabo Delgado. S/he ensures effective, high-quality and compliant implementation of programmes in line with SI strategy and donor requirements. S/he supervises Program Managers and the MEAL Manager, supports adaptive programming, and works closely with the Area Coordinator and field teams to strengthen coordination, accountability and operational continuity.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

1- Major mission restructuring following BHA funding cuts in early 2025, with reduced staffing and evolving organisational set-up, followed by a rapid increase of funding in 2026, including short-term emergency grants and a multi-year development project
2- Short implementation timelines for emergency projects (6 months) requiring strong planning, monitoring and adaptive management
3- Volatile and unpredictable security context requiring continuous analysis and flexible programming
4- Multi-base programme (Pemba, Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Chiure) with limited resources and high coordination needs
5- High workload linked to simultaneous project closures, scale-up of emergency response and launch of new projects
6- Strengthening and maintaining relationships with local authorities and coordination bodies in a sensitive operational environment

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

1- Ensure structured supervision of ongoing programmes across all bases and also the suppervision of the technicall departments (WASH, FSL, RRM Co, and MEAL)
2- Strengthen MEAL systems and ensure effective use of monitoring data and accountability mechanisms for programmatic decision-making
3- Ensure quality closure of ending projects and structured launch of new projects (Apri-May 2026)
4- Reinforce program compliance with donor requirements and internal procedures
5- Clarify roles, workflows and coordination mechanisms between Program, MEAL and Support departments
6- Lead and coordinate proposal development with Project Managers, Technical Coordinators and the Grants Department
7- Strengthen representation and collaboration with provincial and district authorities, clusters and key partners

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Security level 2 in Pemba with limited constraints.

Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia are security level 3, with more restrictions. Movements and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

The security situation remains volatile, with unpredictable insurgent attacks and evolving dynamics involving armed actors. Close monitoring of the context is required for daily movement validation. Travel to field bases is mainly via UNHAS flights.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
2. Solid background or experience in at least one technical
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making
4. Good knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong information management capacity and ability to coordinate multiple activities across bases
2. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills
3. Ability to represent SI with authorities, partners and coordination bodies
4. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
5. Capacity to supervise and structure teams in a complex operational environment

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Portuguese (strong asset)
3. Spanish or Italian (asset)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a coastal city with good living conditions for expatriates, including stable water and electricity and reliable 4G internet. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day. SI provides comfortable office and guesthouse facilities close to amenities.

The position is based in Pemba, with frequent visits to the bases. Field bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour. Living conditions in field locations are basic but functional.

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - PALESTINE (H/F/X)
jobs.description:
**Working environment:**

The French Red Cross (FRC) has been present in Palestine since November 2022, based in Ramallah and working in close partnership with the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS). Initially established to implement a five-year AFD-funded project supporting the institutional and pedagogical development of Ibn Sina College of Health Professions in Nablus, the Delegation has progressively expanded its portfolio to support PRCS across key health and humanitarian priorities.

The Delegation currently combines longer-term institutional and capacity-strengthening programmes with support to PRCS's response to the evolving humanitarian context, particularly in emergency medical services, first aid, rehabilitation and disability inclusion, and health education. This includes support to PRCS through CDCS-funded EMS/First Aid programmes, rehabilitation activities, and the continued implementation of the AFD-funded Ibn Sina College project. The overall approach is centred on capacity building, technical expertise, knowledge transfer and institutional strengthening, increasingly through delegated implementation by PRCS while maintaining FRC technical, programme, financial and donor oversight.

The programme portfolio is implemented in a highly volatile operational environment, characterised by severe humanitarian needs in Gaza, increasing access and protection constraints in the West Bank, and significant pressures on Palestinian health and emergency-response systems. The Delegation therefore needs to balance longer-term development and capacity-strengthening objectives with the ability to adapt programmes to rapidly changing humanitarian and operational priorities.

**Position**

For a Programme Coordinator position, the role sits at the centre of this portfolio: ensuring strategic coherence across programmes, supporting and overseeing PRCS-led implementation, maintaining strong donor and partner relations, ensuring smooth and proactive coordination between programme and support teams through all steps of the project cycle, supporting positive team coordination including through the supervision of the Project Manager, identifying opportunities for programme development and funding, and ensuring that FRC's support remains relevant, technically sound and adaptable to the changing Palestinian context.

**MISSIONS AND ACTIVITIES**

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Programme Coordinator will :

- contribute to the development and implementation of the operational strategy of the Delegation,
- ensure the monitoring and steering of the implementation and development of programmes,
- and contribute to the representation of the Delegation to partners, humanitarian coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders.

1. Lead on all aspects of programmatic design and projects implementation (working closely with all relevant technical experts and counterparts as well as in constant coordination with PRCS), and actively contribute to the strategic & operational positioning and development of the Delegation in support of the Head of Delegation.
2. Coordinate the development and writing of new quality Project Proposals and Concept Notes, in coordination with the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS) and in line with the Delegation's annual operational programming validated by the FRC.
3. Support the programme team in the planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and quality and timely narrative and financial reporting of projects, in line with FRC's international strategy and MEAL obligations (processes and tools) in the country of intervention.
4. Contribute to the representation of the FRC and the development of partnerships in support of the Head of Delegation.
5. Ensure good coordination and support of project and programme teams for quality project management.
6. Contribute to good partnership relations and the capacity building of the PRCS, as well as to any further support activities that the position may require.

**Reporting relationship**: Head of Delegation

**Managing and Operational links :**

- The incumbent will manage the FRC Delegation’s technical programme/project in the field of health, in coordination with partners, Health and NSD Logistics regional experts, and under the supervision of technical advisors from HQ. At the time of posting, the FRC Delegation is considering ad hoc technical staff support rather than long term in-country technical programme teams. The development of projects and portfolio through the Programme Coordination position will impact the Delegation organigram.
- The incumbent will be the direct line manager of a national Project Manager, focused on the AFD project (see context section above)

**Collaborates internally with :**

- All the delegation & FRC HQ support services (Desk, Finance, Logistics, MEAL, Technical departments, Compliance & Audit, Security Management, etc.)

**Collaborates externally with :**

- PRCS counterparts and management team
- Ibn Sina College Project Manager
- AFD Project Manager
- Counterparts and colleagues within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement
- Technical experts and consultants supporting project development and implementation

**Profile**

**1/ Qualifications and experience**

***Experience :***

- At least five (5) years’ experience in the same type of position - **mandatory**
- Previous experience in programme coordination positions - **mandatory**
- Previous experience in supervising staff and supporting their professional and technical development -
- Experience and/or knowledge in communicating with various partners and donors - **mandatory**
- Experience in developing new projects (concept note, proposal, budget, logframe, etc) - **mandatory**
- Experience in donor reporting and contract management - **mandatory**
- Experience working with local partners and partner-implemented projects / programmes - **mandatory**
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement - **mandatory**
- Previous experience managing projects with AFD and CDCS is a strong asset
- Experience in the MENA region and specifically in Palestinian context is a strong asset
- Background in health or in health projects (including emergency medical services, nurse sciences, pre-hospital care, first aid, etc.) is a strong asset

***Education*** :

- Studies in humanitarian or development studies, or any equivalent field
- Mastery of the project cycle and project management tools
- Knowledge of the different humanitarian sectors
- Mastery of the humanitarian coordination system
- Knowledge of the main donors and rules

**2/ Competencies**

Mandatory job requirements

- Organisational capacity
- Coordination capacity
- Strong writing and synthesis skills (for both proposals and reporting contributions)
- Effective capacity in grant management
- Effective capacity in MEAL procedures and processes
- Strong communication and diplomatic skills in multicultural work environments
- Teamwork skills (active listening, proactivity and consensus building)
- Experience in team management
- Initiative and ability to work efficiently and effectively without close supervision

Valued skills

- Proficiency in Office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (Google-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Expertise in identifying and implementing jointly capacity-improvement plans
- Experience facilitating trainings and accompanying staff to strengthen their expertise
- In-depth knowledge of the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement’s National Society Development approaches, especially through a Programme Coordination and Development lens

Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:

- Flexibility and quick adaptability
- Restraint, patience and diplomacy in institutional relations
- Ability to work within a coordination team and in functional link with the project and field teams
- Ability to work with a multicultural team
- Resilience to stress and high workload
- **International driving licence mandatory**

Languages

- English and French mandatory (oral and written); Arabic would be an asset.

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Ramallah- PALESTINE
- Duration: 12 months (renewable)
- Starting date : December 2026
- Mandatory driving licence

The French Red Cross reserves the right to close a recruitment before the closing date of the advertisement and the application deadline. Thank you for your understanding.

If we do not contact you within 3 weeks, please consider that we will not consider your application.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

**Online training**

To learn more about the Red Cross Movement, we invite you to follow two online training courses, free of charge and accessible to all. W.O.R.C. (World of Red Cross and Red Crescent): this course covers topics such as the origin and history of the Movement, its fundamental principles, the emblem, the International Federation, the ICRC and the national societies. Stay Safe aims to develop a common culture of security management within the Movement. You can find these courses on the International Federation's Learning Platform: [https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx](https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx)
