jobs.title: Director of Quality and Impact Hub [Open to Internal and External Applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

For six decades, UNDP has shaped the progress of human development, working with its partners to lift millions from poverty and increase opportunities for all. Empowered by Member States with a mandate to work across the spectrum of human development, UNDP provides integrated support at scale to improve people’s lives worldwide. UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029 is grounded in the determination of UNDP to eradicate poverty, the greatest global challenge, indispensable to the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Through the Strategic Plan, UNDP will continue to support countries’ progress towards high human development, while protecting the planet. Four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and healthy planet – define its strategic direction, powered by three accelerators: digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance. All are underpinned by a commitment to human rights and to leaving no one behind, and rest on the recognition of UNDP as a trusted and transparent development partner.

Within UNDP, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) unites world-class policy expertise, flagship global programmes, and collaborative innovation and learning networks so UNDP is not only ready for the future— but helps build it with governments and partners. BPPS is where policy meets practice - for impact. From development to crisis contexts, BPPS helps countries navigate complexity, scale what works, and advance a more just, resilient, and sustainable future. The position of Director, Quality and Impact Hub is a member of the BPPS senior leadership team.

The Quality and Impact Hub aim to expand UNDP’s value position as an accountable, transparent and therefore trusted and neutral development partner. The Impact Hub serves as the corporate custodian and strategist driving continual improvement of UNDP’s institutional architecture that guides UNDP programming. The Impact Hub leads changes in UNDP policy instruments and quality assurance approaches to enable UNDP programming - spanning all funding sources, including core, non-core, and Vertical Funds (VFs) - that is risk-informed, agile, results focused and integrates social and environmental risks and opportunities. The Impact Hub brings together two existing units in BPPS: the Vertical Fund Hub (VF Hub), and the Quality Programming Team (QPT - including the Social and Environmental Team (SES) Team) to be the central pillar of trust and transparency in UNDP.

By consolidating policy custodianship, quality assurance, risk management, and results oversight, the Impact Hub will be better able to support UNDP in achieving higher accountability, fostering greater trust with partners, reduce fiduciary risks, be more adaptable, and achieve greater developmental quality and impact. A renewed focus on fit-for-purpose and relevant policies will enable and steer UNDP into new partnerships with the private sector, with IFIs, and with the VFs. The Impact Hub will also institutionalize quality assurance and oversight into UNDP, where risk management, results assurance, and policy coherence operate seamlessly through digital systems, enabling evidence-based decision-making and learning across all UNDP programming. The Impact Hub will drive continuous improvement internally while learning from external engagements with the UNDP Executive Board and Boards of the Vertical Funds amongst others to ensure UNDP remains fit-for purpose, dynamic, agile and relevant in an ever-changing international development landscape. The Quality and Impact Hub will continue to lead UNDP’s accountability and engagement with the VFs and ensure UNDP VF programming complies with VF policies and requirements, as well as continue to provide financial oversight of VF programming to ensure VF funds are used for their intended purpose as required by the VFs and VF fiduciary management, reporting and auditing as mandated by the VFs.

Position Purpose

The Director of the Quality and Impact Hub guides and informs areas within the Hub, drawing on their deep technical expertise, political acumen, and demonstrated leadership and managerial capacities. The Director leads cross-cutting efforts in UNDP programming policy reform, and accountability, thereby contributing to UNDP’s reputation as a trusted and transparent. The Director also provides advice and technical expertise for high level decision makers seeking UNDP’s support. Further, the position engages across multilateral processes and partners to position UNDP as a partner of choice in support of developing countries. The role also interfaces with the broader BPPS (other Hubs, Teams) UNDP’s other Bureaus and Offices, and with UN system and related offices, entities, agencies/programmes/funds. The Director is responsible for creating a culture and enabling systems and processes that motivate, engage, and build a coherent team across multiple geographies. The Director will be supported by a Deputy Director.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead UNDPs engagement with the Vertical Funds including Policy alignment, Project Oversight and Compliance and Financial Oversight

- Develop political, technical, operational and financial strategy for UNDP’s engagement with the Environmental Vertical Funds (Global Environment Facility, Green Climate Fund and Adaptation Fund) and provide the substantive technical and managerial leadership required to implement it;

- Ensure effective collaboration and relationship management with the Secretariats of the Environment Funds.

- Represent UNDP in the Vertical fund partnerships engaging with the Governing Bodies of each Fund; the technical and advisory bodies of each Fund, and the Accredited Entities under each Fund;

- Prepare, implement, and monitor annual VF Fee budgeting and planning in close collaboration with the Director of the Planet Hub and technical teams, as well as Regional Team Leads to ensure organizational alignment;

- Develop and continuously enhance the internal UNDP VF oversight and compliance procedures to ensure VF policies are met in UNDP VF programming;

- Deliver on project and portfolio level VF monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements;

- Provide dedicated financial oversight for each VF project, including nationally implement projects and specific global projects, as well as annual portfolio level Fund specific audits, as required by VF policy and procedures;

- Regularly engage with other UNDP Bureaus to ensure consistent application of oversight and compliance procedures across VF programming, and on policy, legal, risk and other strategic VF issues;

- Proactively monitor project and program level VF specific risks connected with UNDP’s relationship with the Vertical Funds and regularly engages with Planet Hub teams including at regional level to ensure efficient and effective oversight and risk management of VF programming.

2. Lead development of UNDP Programme, Portfolio and Project Management standards, approaches, and prescriptive content (PPM)

- Represent UNDP in relevant UNSDG programming working mechanisms, inter-agency task forces and other UN reform initiatives and provide strategic analysis and advice on emerging issues across the UN related to programme and project management, and programming standards, approaches and modalities (e.g. on QCPR, UNSDCF, UNSDG guidelines and programming principles); help establish programme-related priorities, positions and action;

- Lead and develop new and revised programme, portfolio and project standards, approaches, policies and procedures to improve the quality of UNDP programming, facilitate evidence-based decision making/feedback loops, reduce unnecessary transaction costs, respond to evaluation and audit recommendations, and maintain coherence with operational content;

- Lead on the roll-out, review and revision of programming and portfolio approaches to enhance programme effectiveness for achieving results;

- Lead the review of specific quality assurance tools and standards including Partner Capacity Assessment Tool (PCAT) and Private Sector Due Diligence (PSDD) to facilitate flexible, innovative and impactful programming in UNDP;

- Monitor implementation of policies, methods and tools and compliance by relevant UNDP units, and analyze performance to identify lessons learned and steps needed to incentivize improved organizational performance, compliance, and effectiveness;

- Manage and contribute to development of PPM-related capacity building guidance, training modules and other resources for staff.

3. Provide management leadership on quality country programming, SES, Transparency, and Risk Management to increase value add of UNDP programming

- Develop and update guidance and Standard Operating Procedures for the corporate HQ Programme Appraisal Committee (HQ PAC) for new country and regional programmes (CPDs and RPDs);

- Manage the nomination, appointment and orientation process of HQ PAC members and chairs;

- Oversee the quality assurance processes and oversight of the regional bureau cleared CPDs/RPDs, for onward submission to the Executive Board based on its adherence to the Programme Quality Appraisal recommendations;

- Leads the development of standard operating procedures, guidance and systems (VF and non-VF) to ensure UNDP provides high-quality oversight services and remains compliant with policies and procedures;

- Monitor project-level appraisal and VF pipeline development processes and quality assurance, including the implementation of the Quality Standards for Programming and the Social and Environmental Standards;

- In partnership with other Bureaus, update UNDP tools to embed risk management into UNDP programming and the escalation of implementation risks for enhanced oversight as needed;

- Lead UNDP’s transparency initiative by integrating and implementing the International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI) standard in programme and project management;

- Lead enhancement of and application of UNDP Social and Environmental Standards across all UNDP programming.

4. Promote and lead innovation and substantive knowledge management

jobs.description:
Background

The position is located in the Department of Safety and Security of Ukraine. This position is locally administered by UNDP and is financed by the United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) from the Local Cost Share Security Budget (LCSSB) . The contract may be extended subject to the availability of funds, satisfactory performance, and continuing need for the post.

Under the supervision of the UNDSS Head of Training for training related matters and the Field Security Coordination Officer (FSC)) for security related matters; and overall guidance of the Chief Security Adviser (CSA), the Field Security Associate (Training) assists in the conducti of security training in Ukraine.

Duties and Responsibilities

Within limits of delegated authority and depending on location, Field Security Associate (FSA) - Training at this level may be responsible for the following duties: (These duties are generic and may not be performed by all Field Security Associates).

1. Facilitate knowledge sharing and Provide Security Trainings Coordination and Delivery

• Contributes to the planning, organization and delivery of security training courses including Safe and Secure Approached in Field Environment (SSAFE), Individual First Aid Kit (IFAK), Emergency Trauma Bag (ETB), Women Security Awareness Training (WSAT), and Field Security Associate (FSA) Training.

• Provides administrative and logistic support for all aspect of the training arrangements.

i. Liaises with conference manager for booking of training room and facility.

ii. Communicates in a timely manner with practical training ground manager.

iii. Assists in the preparation of IFAK/ETB/SSAFE training aids.

• Coordinates the co-facilitation of training with other trainer(s) from UN Agencies, Funds, Programmes and Organizations (UNAFPOs).

• Provides support in liaising with INGOs regarding security training assistance as part of Saving Life Together (SLT)_ framework.

• Assists in maintaining/updating training repository and data in SharePoint.

• Prepares and develops training package (including translation) as required.

• Conducts in-person IFAK/ETB/SSAFE training in field locations as required.

• Assists FSCO in preparing monthly training reports.

• Arranges IFAK sessions for the certification of new IFAK instructor candidate.

• Conducts practical and written assessment for IFAK and ETB.

2. Monitor Security Information and Coordination

• Assists the Chief Security Advisor/FSCOs in collecting, updating, and communicating information regarding the security situation in the Area of Responsibility (AoR):

i. Liaises and coordinates, as appropriate, with the host government security organizations and/or personnel, including national and local provincial authorities, military, and police officers, as well as non-governmental organizations in the area of operation;

ii. Helps to assess the security situation at the duty station and ensures adequate gathering and verification of security information that may be required for a proper analysis of the situation;

iii. Communicates information on security issues to the heads of United Nations agencies and provides host country security advice to UNDSS, as required;

iv. Maintains regular contacts with Security Focal Points of UN agencies;

v. May be requested to provide technical assistance at Area/Security Management Team meetings.

3. Assist in Security Planning and Monitoring

• Assists in maintaining the Security Plan, including updating staff lists:

• Helps in the preparation and review of the UN Security Plan;

• Supports actions during the implementation of the Security Plan, as required.

• Assists with the monitoring of the security measures implementation as recommended in the Security Risks Management (SRM) process for the AoR.

• Assists in reporting security incidents affecting UN staff, offices, and assets, and assists in the preparation of security reports, such as the Security Incident Report and other Security Assessments.

4. Monitor the security compliance of UNSMS premises and international staff residences

• Provides support in conducting security evaluations and provides advice on Residential Security Measures of UN staff, as well as on latest trends and threats to staff safety and security;

• Establishes and maintains warden system and keeps update of information related to UN offices and residences;

• Administers a pass and ID system;

• Maintains liaison with commercial companies used for UN security at offices and residences in order to facilitate the effective and efficient use of the guard force.

5 Provide General Administrative Support

• Maintains routine and confidential correspondence files/documents;

• Maintains a database on contact details of host country security authorities;

• Arranges appointments, receives visitors, places, and screens telephone calls with discretion, and takes minutes and/or notes at meetings.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the supervision of the UNDSS Head of Training for training related matters and the Field Security Coordination Officer (FSC)) for security related matters; and overall guidance of the Chief Security Adviser (CSA), the Field Security Associate (Training) assists in the conduction of security training in Ukraine.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Business Management

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy.

requests.

- Applicable security, police and/or military training is desirable.

- Minimum six (6) years (with secondary education) or three (3) years (with bachelor’s degree) of working experience in the field of safety and security management or security training in the public or private security service areas is required.

HR Business Partner Specialist (Open to all Applicants)
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to eradicate poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, and build resilience so countries can sustain progress. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP plays a critical role in helping countries achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Our people are united by a common call to action: building a fairer and more inclusive world for those in need through sustainable development.

The Office of Human Resources (OHR) is part of the UNDP Bureau for Management Services (BMS) of UNDP. It is the anchor of the global HR function for UNDP, providing strategy and policy setting, guidance and oversight. In addition, BMS/OHR provides a broad range of HR advisory and talent management services enabling UNDP to deliver fully integrated development solutions to enable its workforce to deliver more and better results. BMS/OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by developing high quality and innovative human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

Within this innovative, ambitious and dynamic context, BMS/OHR is seeking high calibre HR professionals with a strong HR background, and the capacity, commitment, and attitude needed to drive a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, transformative results, as well as inclusion, respect and trust.

Position Purpose

In this context and under the supervision of the Senior HR Business Partner, the HR Business Partnering Specialist is responsible for the delivery of a full spectrum of strategic HR services to the Regional Bureau for Arab States (RBAS) and its Country Offices aimed to ensure that Bureaus and Offices can attract and effectively manage required talent in the culture of high performance, innovation and informed risk-taking.

In line with the People for 2030 Strategy the successful candidate will endeavor to support and enable effective HR management, workforce analytics, HR performance monitoring and business process reengineering. S/he will collaborate closely with the Talent Management and Organizational Effectiveness teams to provide strategic advice and guidance on all issues of human resources management, as well as in providing client-specific HR solutions that are fair, consistent, objective and consistent with the policies and procedures of UNDP.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Contribute to the Workforce Planning, Analytics and Organization Development

- Generate workforce data, interpret data and statistics. Ensure an intelligent analysis of workforce against the business model. Provide authoritative advice and recommendation based on HR analytics.

- Prepare HR reports, presentations, briefing notes based on the analysis of the workforce data.

- Recommend and implement HR practices and strategic interventions to optimize the use of talent products/guidelines, and policies.

- Analyze and provide advice on selection & recruitment initiatives

- Advocate the best application of HR practices, staffing, development and organizational workforce planning, targeted interventions to achieve business objectives

- Study and analyze the results of global/regional HR surveys and contribute to design interventions, and action plans where necessary.

- Gather data from Performance Reviews to develop reporting of potential career paths and development needs for staff and liaise with other OHR Units to deliver on specific needs.

- Provide advice based on HR analytics, propose enhancements of existing platforms and reports.

Interpretation of HR policies, implementation of corporate HR exercises, and ensure quality assurance

- Provide advice and support to managers and staff on human resources related matters.

- Ensure continuous analysis of corporate HR strategies and policies, assessing the impact of changes and making recommendations on their implementation in UNDP.

- Interpret corporate strategic sourcing and succession planning and ensure accurate projection of vacancies and staffing requirements to the appropriate corporate unit.

- Provide Quality Assurance of UNDP people management standards in the assigned Bureau.

- Ensure monitoring of recruitment processes liaising with the Central Recruitment Unit. Ensure monitoring of transactions performed in the People Transaction Services Unit.

- Liaise with OAI / Legal / Ombudsman’s office as needed.

- Support HR corporate initiatives for bureau, provides inputs to management plans, products, strategies, and tools.

Facilitate Capacity Development and Knowledge Management

- Ensure enhanced capacity of HR staff through delivery of workshops and virtual clinics, synthesis of lessons learned. Disseminate lessons learned, best practices, and sound contributions in knowledge networks and communities of practice.

Contribute to the Organization Development and Change Management Facilitation

- Provide inputs on change management strategies, as required, based on corporate policy but with elements of innovation, using internal consulting models and process consultations.

- Contribute to the development of organizational design solutions, including structural design options.

- Support senior managers on implementation of structural changes through effective information sharing and problem solving.

- Identify risks and liaise with relevant stakeholders.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

- Cross Functional and Technical Competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management - Portfolio Management:

- Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity.

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment.

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Business Management - Communication:

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Partnership Management - Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

HR People Strategy & Planning - Human Resources Strategic Planning: Ability to develop integrated HR strategies, governance structures, policies and procedures.

HR People Strategy & Planning - Workforce Planning: Knowledge of theories, mechanisms and tools to analyse the current workforce, determine future workforce needs, as they align to the needs of the business, identify the gap between the present capabilities in the workforce and the organizations needs, and design and implement talent acquisition and development solutions so that an organization can have the required capacity to accomplish its mission, goals, and strategic plan.

HR Talent Acquisition - Talent Sourcing and Outreach: Knowledge of and ability to develop and implement strategies, mechanisms and platforms to ensure the effective outreach to the relevant segments of the labour market, active and passive candidates internally and externally.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Social Sciences, Business Administration, Public Administration, Organizational Psychology, Psychology, Sociology, Economics, Development Economics, International Relations, Human Resource Management, Organizational Development or any other related field is required. Or

- A first level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of five (5) years (with master’s degree) or seven (7) years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in human resources management or must have held similar positions in other international organizations is required.

- Experience with UN/UNDP HR policies and procedures, rules and regulations’ interpretation and application is desirable.

- Experience in providing strategic HR advisory/business partnering services in complex international organizational settings is desired.

- Experience supporting organizational design/workforce optimization or change management initiatives is desired.

- Experience in advising on talent sourcing/recruitment and selection processes desirable.

- Experience in analyzing HR data, reporting in support of HR strategy development and workforce planning initiatives desirable.

- Experience in the usage of computers, office software packages is required; and experience using Quantum modules related to HR functions is desired.

- Experience working with UNDP country offices set up and context is desirable.

jobs.description:
Descripción del Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de los Decretos federales y Programas de Manejo elaborados con los Insumos técnicos que fortalecen la normatividad ambiental aplicable a las ANP y otros instrumentos jurídicos que contribuyen a mejorar la gestión y operación de la CONANP.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Apoyar en la revisión y validación jurídica de los programas de manejo para la conservación y protección de las ANP.

- Colaborar en la formulación y revisión de estrategias de manejo y conservación de las ANP.

- Asistir en la coordinación de las actividades atribuibles a la Dirección de Asuntos Jurídicos con otras unidades administrativas.

- Dar seguimiento a los procesos de opinión requeridos para los nuevos decretos de ANP de las regiones definidas por la CONANP.

- Contribuir al fortalecimiento de procesos de la CONANP relativos a consulta pública de forma eficiente y transparente.

- Apoyar en la elaboración de documentos técnicos, notas informativas, comunicados que requiera la dirección de área.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la Dirección de Asuntos Jurídicos, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Derecho y/o carreras afines, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 2 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de informes de calidad.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Conocimiento y/o Experiencia en: Atención y seguimiento a Juicios agrarios

- Conocimiento y/o Experiencia en: Atención y seguimiento a Juicios de amparo

- Conocimiento y/o Experiencia en: Atención y seguimiento a juicios de nulidad en materia administrativa.

- Conocimiento y/o Experiencia en: planes de manejo para la conservación y protección de las ANP.

- Conocimiento y/o Experiencia en: estrategias de manejo y conservación. Se dará ventaja si cuenta con experiencia en Áreas Naturales Protegidas.

Tiered Approach

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

Within UNCDF’s thematic are of nature, climate and energy financing, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Sustainable Energy 2 program, a 5 year program funded by the Central African Forestry Initiative (CAFI) and Fonds National de REDD+ (FONAREDD DRC), aims to scale up clean energy solutions to reduce deforestation and emissions, through building a diversified investment portfolio across clean fuels, renewable electrification, and sustainable biomass.

To continue driving these objectives, UNCDF seeks to hire an Administration and Finance Analyst for the Sustainable Energy 2 Program. The Administration and Finance Analyst will support the Energy Investment Program Manager in the day-to-day operations, reporting and activities, to ensure that the program is efficiently executed against donor-committed timelines.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administration and Finance Analyst will provide support in the effective financial management, administrative support, and compliance with UNCDF/UNDP rules and procedures. The incumbent will play a critical role in supporting program operations, managing budgets, overseeing procurement, and ensuring transparent and efficient use of resources.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

Support to Project Planning and Management

- Assist in standardizing finance and accounting systems in accordance with UNDP and UNCDF procedures.

- Support preparation of annual work plans, budgets, budget revisions, procurement plans, and ensure proper system entry.

- Review budget revisions, financial plans, and ensure timely reporting and submission to relevant stakeholders.

Financial Management and Reporting

- Assist in monitoring project expenditure and cash flows to ensure compliance with approved budgets.

- Support quarterly Fund Authorization and Certification of Expenditures (FACE) reviews, cashbook and bank reconciliations.

- Prepare and maintain detailed financial records and reports, ensuring accuracy and completeness.

- Prepare and monitor budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports.

- Ensure support in compliance with UNCDF/UNDP financial regulations and donor requirements.

- Support the consolidation of investee financial reports to inform annual financial reporting and plans, to the donor and to UNCDF.

Procurement and Contract Administration

- Support procurement processes, including preparation of requests for quotations/proposals and contract management in adherence to procurement policies and procedures.

- Maintain accurate records of procurement activities and vendor performance in line with UNCDF standards.

Administrative Support

- Oversee office operations, logistics, and asset management.

- Assist with events management, travel arrangements, and documentation and records management.

- Facilitate communication between project teams and partners.

Audit and Compliance

- Facilitate internal and external audits, ensuring timely submission of required documentation.

- Support the implementation of risk management and compliance measures.

Program Support and Coordination

- Support data collection for companies during due diligence process, when necessary.

- Provide administrative and financial input for program planning and reporting.

- Liaise with partners, government counterparts, and stakeholders on financial and administrative matters.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Finance

Budget Management

Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning, drawing and management of budgets.

Finance

Audit (General)

Understands audit regulations and standards; ability to examine and verify financial accounts and records.

Finance

Finance Business Partnering

Supports business units by providing financial solutions and advice; understands organizational operations and challenges.

Administration & Operations

Documents and Records Management

Manages overall document lifecycle including storage, archiving, and retention policies.

Administration & Operations

Travel Policy and Procedures

Understands travel policies and related administrative rules; able to interpret and apply them appropriately.

Business Management

Operations Management

Ability to effectively plan, organise and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organisation’s assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

Procurement

Procurement Procedures

Knowledge of procurement processes and adherence to UNDP procurement policies.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

• A professional accounting qualification from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy, and/or Advanced (Master´s) University Degree in Finance and/or Accounting is required. Or

• A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

• Candidates with professional accounting qualifications from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.

• Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance must complete the Finance Training and Certification Programme (FTCP), if recruited.

• Candidates satisfying the two above criteria are exempted from undertaking the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT).

• Candidates with MBA or master’s in finance with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

Experience:

• Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience. Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of Finance and Operations in a national or international organization implementing the development projects, and/or leading and managing projects.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

• Experience with UN agencies or international organizations.

• Familiarity with energy, climate, or investment-related programs.

• Knowledge of financial management systems and procurement procedures.

• Experience with UNCDF/UNDP rules and procedures is an advantage.

• Knowledge of Entreprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems (e.g., Atlas, Quantum).

• Strong financial analysis and reporting skills/experience.

• Experience in finance, programme support, management advisory services and managing staff and operational systems.

• Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Required Language(s):

Fluency in French and English is required.

Travel and Reimbursement

The Administration and Finance Associate will be required to report to the office. Travels within the DRC for on-site project monitoring and financial spot check support may be required and will be paid for by UNCDF, in accordance with UNCDF travel policies. A separate TOR with clear deliverables, budget and timelines will be prepared and agreed prior to each field mission.

i. Frequent travel annually for onsite assessments, due diligence and monitoring

ii. Occasional other international travel may be required

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Background

Within the Bureau for Management Services, the Office of Human Resources provides strategic leadership and advisory services to enable UNDP to attract, develop, engage and retain the people required to deliver on its mandate. The People Experience, Performance and Culture Unit (PEPCU) leads UNDP-wide approaches to employee experience and engagement, performance management, culture, respectful workplaces, and duty of care, including mental health and well-being.

The Mental Health and Well-being Team develops and coordinates organization-wide initiatives that prevent and address psychosocial risks, promotes a healthy and inclusive working environment, and enables personnel and managers to access timely information, resources and support. Its work is aligned with UNDP's People for 2030 Strategy, the United Nations System Mental Health and Well-being Strategy, and applicable ethical, confidentiality and data-protection standards.

The UNDP Well-being Coordinator supports two core pillars of the Well-being Function: Psychosocial Risk Management and Early Intervention, and Access to Psychosocial Support Services. The role coordinates psychosocial risk monitoring and follow-up, including analysis of Well-being Index and service-utilization data, identification of emerging risks and service gaps, and support to targeted intervention planning with offices, bureaux, business partnering team and other stakeholders. It also facilitates timely and equitable access to confidential psychosocial consultations, short-term support, referrals, care navigation, manager and HR consultations, and deployment-related psychosocial resources. The role contributes to limited individual or group psychosocial support, as well as the programme’s prevention, communications or learning portfolios.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Coordinate psychosocial risk management and early intervention

- Coordinate collection, validation and analysis of Well-being Index, service-utilization and other relevant data to identify psychosocial risk trends, offices requiring attention and emerging service gaps.

- Maintain a structured risk-monitoring process, including risk flags, office profiles and follow-up records, in line with confidentiality, data-protection and records-management requirements.

- Support consultations with Country Offices, Regional Bureaux, HR Business Partners, managers and staff counsellors to understand identified risks and contextual factors.

- Coordinate the development, documentation and follow-up of targeted psychosocial risk mitigation and early-intervention plans, escalating clinical or organizational concerns to the appropriate technical lead.

- Prepare quarterly psychosocial risk reports, leadership and HR briefings, dashboards and recommendations to support timely organizational decision-making.

2. Coordinate access to psychosocial support services

- Serve as a confidential coordination point for personnel, managers and HR colleagues seeking psychosocial consultation, information or support, and facilitate timely access to the appropriate service.

- Conduct initial psychosocial needs screening within professional competence, identify urgency and appropriate next steps, and escalate high-risk, complex or clinical cases to staff counsellors or emergency services in accordance with established protocols.

- Coordinate short-term psychosocial support pathways, referrals and care navigation to internal and external providers, including follow-up on access barriers and continuity of support.

- Maintain accurate, secure and confidential records of support requests, referrals, utilization and follow-up, ensuring appropriate separation of personal case information from aggregate programme reporting.

- Coordinate pre-deployment psychosocial briefings, resilience resources and referral information for personnel serving in high-risk or challenging operational contexts, in collaboration with the designated service provider and relevant units.

3. Manage service data, monitoring and reporting

- Maintain service-utilization, referral and case-management datasets and apply quality-control procedures to ensure completeness, consistency and confidentiality.

- Develop and maintain indicators, dashboards and reporting processes covering demand, access, response times, utilization, referral outcomes and geographic equity.

- Analyse quantitative and qualitative evidence to identify demand patterns, service gaps and emerging psychosocial risks, while safeguarding anonymity in organizational reporting.

- Prepare concise statistical reports, briefing notes and presentations for management and contribute relevant inputs to corporate well-being reporting.

- Use feedback and evaluation findings to recommend improvements to risk-monitoring processes, referral pathways, resource allocation and service accessibility.

4. Coordinate service delivery arrangements, partnerships and resources

- Coordinate external providers and internal partners supporting counselling, referrals, deployment support and other psychosocial services, and monitor service standards, coverage and follow-up.

- Maintain and periodically update the Referral and Care Navigation Framework, including clear pathways for routine, urgent, specialized and location-specific support, as needed.

- Maintain the Psychosocial Support Resource Hub with approved self-help materials, service information, referral guidance and deployment-related resources.

- Support service administration, including provider coordination, procurement, budget monitoring, documentation for payments and identification of delivery risks requiring management attention.

5. Contribute to prevention, communications, learning and broader programme delivery

- Contribute technical and coordination inputs to organization-wide prevention and mental health literacy initiatives led under other pillars of the Well-being Function.

- Support the development and delivery of awareness campaigns, such as October Mental Health Day, global well-being communications, webinars, learning sessions and practical resources for personnel and managers.

- Provide evidence from psychosocial risk monitoring and service-utilization trends to inform prevention priorities, learning content and targeted communications, while safeguarding confidentiality and anonymity.

- Assist with stakeholder coordination, event logistics, resource development, reporting and other programme responsibilities required to deliver the broader Well-being Function workplan, as needed.

The incumbent performs other duties within the functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Subject to professional qualifications, established protocols and available capacity, this may include brief individual or group psychosocial support, initial assessment and referral. The role does not independently manage emergencies, complex clinical cases or long-term counselling.

6. Institutional Arrangement

The Well-being Coordinator will report to the HR Specialist - Mental Health and Well-being Team Lead BMS/OHR/PEPCU.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking:

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Direction & Strategy - Effective Decision Making:

- Ability to take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one’s authority, area of expertise and resources.

Business Development - Human-centered Design

- Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process.

Business Management - Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Management - Risk Management

- Ability to interact with different levels of management and across different agencies and offices to obtain information, develop legal approaches and resolve issues, this skill includes liaison with counterparts and determining the best sequence in which to pursue an issue, were information, particularly for UNDP, may be across different independent UN agencies.

Legal - Managing Client Relations

- Ability to interact with different levels of management and across different agencies and offices to obtain information, develop legal approaches and resolve issues, this skill includes liaison with counterparts and determining the best sequence in which to pursue an issue, were information, particularly for UNDP, may be across different independent UN agencies.

HR Talent Management - Employee Engagement

- Knowledge of theories and models of human motivation and engagement including the predictors of employee engagement;

- Knowledge of and ability to guide application of tools, techniques, and processes to increase employee engagement;

- Knowledge of tools and methodologies to measure employee engagement and to identify its specific drivers;

- Knowledge of tools and methodologies to ensure regular engagement with personnel on key workplace matters, with a view to identifying the most pressing workplace issues.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Clinical or Organizational Psychology, Counselling, Social Work or Psychiatry required. OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant Work experience

Required skills

- Experience coordinating confidential psychosocial support requests, referrals, care navigation and follow-up across multiple locations or service providers.

- Knowledge of professional ethics, confidentiality, safeguarding, data protection and escalation protocols applicable to psychosocial services.

- Strong analytical, coordination, documentation and reporting skills, including the ability to translate evidence into practical recommendations for offices, managers and HR stakeholders.

Desired Experience, Knowledge, and skills

- Experience with the UN system, international organizations or geographically dispersed workforces.

- Experience using surveys, dashboards or case-management systems to monitor psychosocial risk, service demand, access and outcomes.

- Training or certification in trauma-informed practice, psychological first aid, suicide-risk response, case management or cross-cultural counselling.

- Experience coordinating psychosocial support for personnel in high-risk, crisis or deployment contexts.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy.

UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The focus is on the development of a horizontal network of practitioners across UNDP and the broader development community and working closely with UNDP Regional Hubs.

As part of the Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding Hub, UNDP’s Global Programme for Strengthening the Rule of Law, Human Rights, Justice and Security for Sustainable Peace and Development provides programmatic, policy and financial support to national partners in over 100 countries and territories. The Global Programme is widely recognized for its ability to mobilize funds, provide technical and strategic expertise, and collaborate and coordinate across UN entities to enable more holistic, coherent and comprehensive responses to rule of law, justice, security and human rights challenges. It provides tailored, context-specific technical, financial and strategic support to contexts across the development spectrum.

Phase V of the Global Programme for Strengthening the Rule of Law, Human Rights, Justice and Security for Sustainable Peace and Development, builds on experience, lessons and achievements during Phase IV and is guided by and aligned to UNDP’s 2026-2029 Strategic Plan.

The United Nations Team of Experts on the Rule of Law and Sexual Violence in Conflict (Team of Experts), based at the UN Headquarters in New York, deploys regularly to some of the world’s most challenging contexts. It has a unique “co-lead” structure comprised of the Department of Peace Operations (DPO), the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Sexual Violence in Conflict (SRSG-SVC) and UNDP.

Scope of Work

Under the overall supervision of the Policy Advisor / Deputy Team Leader of the Team of Experts, within UNDP’s Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Team, the IPSA holder will support UNDP and the Team of Experts in advancing the implementation of the Framework of Cooperation on the Prevention and Response to Conflict-Related Sexual Violence (CRSV) between the Government of Ukraine and the United Nations. In addition, the IPSA holder provide support with outreach to Member States and EU institutions.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Provide technical support in the implementation of the Team of Experts' programme in Ukraine, including by:

- Providing strategic and technical advice to the Ukraine team of the Team of Experts on the various workstreams implemented in Ukraine by the Team of Experts.

- Assisting in the full operationalization of Team of Experts’ projects in Ukraine, including the case management system procured for the Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine.

- Supporting the organization of training activities for Ukrainian authorities by drafting training materials and coordinating human resource and logistical.

- Deploying to Ukraine in support of the above-listed tasks.

2. Assist with outreach to Member States, including by:

- Supporting fundraising efforts for the Team of Experts through in-person and virtual engagement with Member States and the private sector.

- Organizing events to raise the profile of the Team of Experts.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP has achieved significant progress in making gender equality and women’s empowerment integral to its work on human development. The new UNDP Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029 complements the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, approved by Executive Board consensus, which defines gender equality as one of three accelerators of human development on a healthy planet. The Strategy acknowledges that success in every area of the Strategic Plan depends on realizing gender equality and the empowerment of women. It retains the ambition of the previous strategy, with a central focus on transforming the systems and power structures that generate gender inequalities. It calls on UNDP to help governments place gender equality at the core of political, economic, and environmental decisions, with the goal of expanding development choices that work for all. The Strategy defines gender equality priorities across each strategic objective and accelerator of the Strategic Plan. It focuses on areas where UNDP has a strong comparative advantage and where solutions can be scaled, building on successful initiatives and partnerships. UNDP also recognizes that mechanical or compliance approaches will not suffice to address the scope of discrimination, and the importance of renewing emphasis on partnerships, including with the private sector. The Strategy proposes institutional transformation inspired by UNDP Gender Equality Seal Certification principles and aligned to the United Nations system-wide Action Plan on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN-SWAP) and Gender Equality Action Plan (GEAP) standards. UNDP recognizes that external impact and delivery mirror internal policies, structures, culture and ways of working.

The Gender Team (BPPS) has the leading role in the implementation of the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029, including through the implementation of Gender Equality Global Programme.

Duties and Responsibilities

Reporting directly to the Head of Gender in New York, the Gender Specialist, Accountability and Reporting will ensure UNDP is accountable for its commitments to gender equality in line with the Strategic Plan 2026-2929 and the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029; lead the implementation of the UN-SWAP and the GEAP to advance UN-System wide commitments on gender equality and interagency coordination; lead UNDP’s efforts to track financial investments for gender equality; and lead and provide reliable gender-related data for decision-making.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Ensure UNDP is accountable for its commitments to gender equality in line with the Strategic Plan 2026-2929 and the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029.

- Coordinate and deliver UNDP’s reporting on gender equality including the Annual Report on the Implementation of the UNDP Gender Equality Strategy (official and glossy version), the GEAP Annual Report, the UN-SWAP Annual Report, and the ECOSOC reports.

- Provide technical and coordination support for the preparation, convening and follow-up of the Gender Steering and Implementation Committee (GSIC), as the main mechanism for monitoring implementation of the GES 2026-2029.

- Provide advice and technical support to ensure performance assessment criteria for all senior and middle managers include implementation of the GES 2026-2029, in close collaboration with key bureaus and teams (OHR/BMS, Gender Equality Seal for Development, among others).

- Act as evaluation and audit focal point for the Gender Team, including by liaising with the UNDP Independent Evaluation Office and the Audit Office; engaging in corporate gender evaluations or audits; preparing management responses; tracking the implementation of evaluation recommendations; and delivering the reports and evaluation of the Gender Equality Global Programme 2023-2025.

- Ensure the gender equality data powerhouse is updated.

Lead the implementation of the UN-SWAP and the GEAP to advance UN-System wide commitments on gender equality and interagency coordination.

- Develop and lead UNDP’s Action Plan for the effective implementation of its commitments in the framework of the UN-SWAP and GEAP.

- Liaise with key teams and units (HQ, RH and CO) to ensure UNDP meets UN SWAP/GEAP standards.

- Engage closely with the UNDP Gender Equality Seal for country offices, as the primary global initiative to operationalize the GES 2026-2029.

- Represent UNDP and the Gender Team in key global UN interagency coordination spaces, such as IANGWE, UN-SWAP and GEAP.

- Support UNDP’s participation in intergovernmental conferences and high-level inter-agency events related to system-wide commitments for gender equality.

Lead UNDP’s efforts to track financial investments for gender equality.

- Lead implementation of UNDP’s gender marker as the main tool to track budgets and expenditures for gender equality at all levels (HQ, RH and CO).

- Ensure UNDP’s gender marker meets UN system wide quality standards; coordinate quality assurance and periodic reviews to ensure accuracy.

- Provide technical support to HQ’s Teams, RH and COs to help them meet UNDP’s gender marker targets (GES 2026-2029); foster learning and knowledge sharing.

- Coordinate the development of financial and narrative annual reports/snapshots for leadership decision-making (i.e., global, by region, by priority), including analysis of progress towards the targets established in the GES 2026-2029.

- Represent UNDP in inter-agency fora on the implementation of gender markers and other mechanisms to track financial investments for gender equality.

Lead and provide reliable gender-related data for decision-making.

- Collect and analyze relevant corporate data from different sources (i.e., Gender Marker, ROAR, Gender Equality Seal, including AI driven analytics) for evidence-based decision-making and programming.

- Develop dashboards and visualizations to communicate complex findings in clear, compelling ways.

- Prepare policy briefs, reports, and presentations that translate data into actionable recommendations for stakeholders.

- Liaise with Regional Hubs’ Gender Teams and Country Offices to identify their data needs and interests; and contribute to strengthening their capacities in data collection and analysis for decision-making and programming.

- Provide content for the activities of the Global Gender Equality Community of Practice (CoP) and the Gender Equality Seal Learning Plan, drawing from data and lessons learned from the different workstreams.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

2030 Agenda People – Gender

- Monitoring and Evaluation on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment.

2030 Agenda People – Gender

- Data and Research on Gender Equality.

2030 Agenda People – Gender

- Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Development - Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches.

- Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management - Working with Evidence and Data

- Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Business Management - Portfolio Management

- Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity.

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment.

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in statistics, feminist economics, data science and analytics, gender studies and/or relevant related fields is required; OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor´s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with two additional years of relevant work experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of five (5) years (with Master’s degree) or seven (7) years (with Bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in accountability, reporting and/or data analysis is required.

- Technical expertise in gender equality is desired, with feminist economics as an added plus.

- Proven knowledge and experience in data science and analytics, including preprocessing, exploration, use and visualization of data for decision-making is desired, with AI driven data analytics as an added plus.

- Proven experience in producing quality reports in English is desired.

- Proven experience in coordination with diverse partners and stakeholders is desired, with experience in coordination with UN-System entities as an added plus.

- Proven knowledge and experience working with UN accountability tools is desired, with experience with UNDP accountability tools as an added plus.

- Proficiency in statistical software and data visualization tools is required.

Language:

- Knowledge of another UN language is an advantage.

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.
