jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Enlace Estratégico y Asuntos Jurídicos de Proyectos de Cooperación
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Vigente desde el año 2013, la historia del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) está ligada al establecimiento del Sistema Mexicano de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, contribuyendo a la implementación del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 17 “Revitalizar la alianza mundial para el Desarrollo Sostenible”, con el propósito de apoyar los esfuerzos de la AMEXCID para transitar hacia un modelo eficaz, que refleje las particularidades de un Cooperante Dual, oferente y receptor de cooperación en sus diversas modalidades, y País de Renta Media Alta, de acuerdo con sus propias prioridades y visión, en el marco de la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible.

En su Tercera Etapa (2019-2025), el Programa de Cooperación promueve que la Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (CID) sea un instrumento para alcanzar las prioridades de desarrollo incluidas en el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2019-2024, alineado particularmente al compromiso de “Conducir la política exterior en apego a los principios constitucionales y articulada con las prioridades de la política interna”, siendo la CID uno de los siete principios de la política exterior de México.

Específicamente, se apoyarán los esfuerzos que realiza la AMEXCID para consolidarse institucionalmente, encaminados a desarrollar sus capacidades nacionales, fortalecer su política de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta, así como establecer alianzas estratégicas con otros actores relevantes (como el sector privado, la academia y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, otras agencias de cooperación multilaterales y bilaterales presentes en México que realizan esfuerzos de naturaleza complementaria), por medio de esquemas innovadores de cooperación al desarrollo. Además, se apoyará la contribución de la Agencia a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Lo anterior está orientado a potenciar los 6 ejes de acción de la AMEXCID (diplomacia deportiva; diplomacia en ciudadanía, diplomacia científica y tecnológica; diplomacia económica empresarial; diplomacia educativa; y diplomacia humanitaria), su nueva estructura (coordinación de la política de cooperación internacional; análisis y evaluación de proyectos; implementación de proyectos), así como las prioridades de México como país receptor y país oferente de CID.

El objetivo general del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) es la consolidación institucional de la AMEXCID para fortalecer la Cooperación Sur-Sur en México, a través de cuatro resultados:

1.Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales para la gestión de la CID;

2.Fortalecimiento de la política mexicana de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta;

3.Promoción de alianzas estratégicas para el desarrollo;

4.Apoyo a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1.Participar en la coordinación de las relaciones estratégicas y la logística de vinculación jurídica con misiones diplomáticas, embajadas y organismos extranjeros, asegurando que los compromisos políticos y de cooperación se traduzcan en acuerdos formales claros y exigibles conforme a derecho.

2.Apoyar en el análisis y redacción de los marcos jurídicos, memorandos de entendimiento, cartas de intención y convenios bilaterales o multilaterales de cooperación internacional que suscribe la AMEXCID, garantizando que se apeguen estrictamente al marco legal mexicano y al derecho internacional.

3.Coadyuvar en la gestión de la agenda de la Agencia en asuntos parlamentarios, comparecencias y armonización de normativas relacionadas con la cooperación internacional para el desarrollo.

4.Aportar elementos para la estrategia de transparencia, rendición de cuentas y combate a la opacidad dentro de la Agencia, asegurando que los procesos internos, la asignación de recursos y la ejecución de programas cumplan con las normativas de fiscalización y acceso a la información pública.

5.Proveer consultoría jurídica a la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID en asuntos contenciosos, administrativos y regulatorios complejos.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El/la Asociado/a de Enlace Estratégico y Asuntos Jurídicos de Proyectos de Cooperación formará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID o de la dirección general en la que se asigne. Bajo la supervisión que determine la unidad correspondiente, brindará análisis y seguimiento técnico a iniciativas vinculadas con cooperación internacional, fortalecimiento institucional y alianzas estratégicas, trabajando de manera coordinada con las áreas de la Agencia, el PNUD y las contrapartes nacionales e internacionales pertinentes.

Competencias Escenciales:

Logro de Resultos: NIVEL 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: NIVEL 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: NIVEL 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: NIVEL 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: NIVEL 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado/a.

Participar y Asociarse: NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: NIVEL 1: Aprecia y respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes y confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de preparatoria (Bachillerato), es requisito.

- Estudios universitarios nivel licenciatura en Derecho o carreras afines, no es requisito, pero se le dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidato/as con certificado de preparatoria: 6 años de experiencia dentro de la administración pública a nivel municipal, estatal o federal.

- Para candidatos/as con título de Licenciatura: 3 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Manejo de paquetería Office (Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook)

- Experiencia en redacción, negociación y revisión de convenios, acuerdos interinstitucionales o tratados.

- Conocimiento de la Ley Orgánica de la Administración Pública Federal, normatividad presupuestaria y leyes de transparencia.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia en resolución de conflictos, diálogo institucional y construcción de consensos con actores políticos.

- Experiencia traduciendo objetivos de política en instrumentos legales viables y seguros.

- Experiencia gestionando agendas, especialmente en temas jurídicos o parlamentarios.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Pathfinder Multisectoral Tools Development Internship
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes.

HIV and Health Approach

UNDP is a founding cosponsor of the Joint UN Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS), a partner of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria, a signatory of the WHO led SDG3 Global Action Plan for Healthy Lives and Well-Being for All, and a co-sponsor of several other international health partnerships. UNDP’s work on HIV, health and development leverages UNDP’s core strengths and mandates in sustainable development, governance, poverty reduction and climate. UNDP delivers support to countries in three areas of HIV and health: reducing the inequalities that drive disease, promoting effective and inclusive governance for health and building resilient and sustainable systems for health. UNDP helps countries to mainstream attention to HIV and health into action on gender, poverty, governance, financing, and the broader effort to achieve and sustain the Sustainable Development Goals. UNDP works with partners to address the interactions between governance, human rights, and health responses, especially for those left behind. UNDP also supports countries in effective implementation of complex, multilateral and multisectoral health projects, while simultaneously investing in capacity development so that national and local partners can assume these responsibilities over time. The UNDP/Global Fund partnership is an important part of this work, facilitating access to resources for action on SDG 3 by countries that face constraints in directly receiving and managing such funding. UNDP partners with countries, WHO and other partners in responding to health emergencies and HIV and health dimensions of crisis/post-crisis situations.

As a long-standing partner of the Global Fund, UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services drawing on policy and technical support from other UNDP business units (e.g. data, digital, environment, climate). Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance to Global Fund grants in 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments.

“The Comprehensive Multisectoral Action Framework – Malaria and Sustainable Development” was launched in 2022. With the ethos of ‘try, learn, share’, the Pathfinder Endeavour paves the way for sustainable development with malaria as tracer. Pathfinder is implemented in partnership with RBM Partnership to End Malaria, UNHabitat, and WHO. Pathfinder embraces UNDP’s portfolio approach in collaboration with the UNDP/SIU Team as well as scaling smart health systems in collaboration with the UNDP/SHS Team.

Pathfinder focuses currently on three countries: Cameroon, Madagascar, and Uganda and within each of these, three districts that are left the furthest behind in both SDG achievement and malaria-burden.

80 promising tools have already been identified and drafted, each addressing one of the malaria-critical SDG indicators. Further, a gamification “Halt the Vicious Cycle” has been prepared and used in the tree countries for strategic prioritization. Finally, a guidance note is currently being piloted in three communes (districts) in Cameroon. During the pilot each commune focuses on three quick-wins, one from each of the Pathways: (A) Indivisible SDGs, (B) Five steps to become malaria-smart, and (C) 360o Accountability. It is envisaged that the final Pathfinder Toolbox will contain 80 tools for Pathway A, 80 tools for B, and 50 tools for C as well as a guide for comprehensive systems-based implementation. The Toolbox is planned to be ready for use in Q2-2027.

Objective

Provide support to the Pathfinder Secretariat on a systems-based multisectoral toolbox: search, develop and prepare for use in districts and communities that are left the furthest behind.

Duties and Responsibilities

The intern will undertake the assignments outlined below:

Expected Outputs:

Support to the UNDP-Health Funds and Health Systems / Pathfinder Secretariat:

- Contribute to the Secretariat’s support to UNDP country office in Cameroon during the piloting in the three communes.

- Contribute to the evaluation of the piloting in Cameroon.

- Search, develop, and prepare draft 80 tools for Pathways B and 50 for C.

- Contribute to the Pathfinder guide for comprehensive systems-based implementation.

- Undertake related tasks as assigned by the team

Competencies

Corporate Competencies:

- Demonstrates integrity by modeling the UN’s values and ethical standards.

- Promotes the vision, mission, and strategic goals of UNDP.

- Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability.

Functional:

- Strong track record of research and writing skills;

- Knowledge of international public health, gender and/or human rights;

- Experience with data visualization;

- Editing skills in both English and French are helpful; and

- Expertise in health and development issues.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Degree programme in public health, international relations/development studies or other relevant fields.

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

- Be enrolled in a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher);

- Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum Bachelor’s level or equivalent);

- Have graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation.

Experience:

- Familiarity with the UN system, and/or other international organisations;

- Background in international development, global health, or other relevant field;

- Experience in public Health is an advantage;

- Ability to work in a multicultural environment;

- Experience with web-based applications, data visualization software, Microsoft Office tools (Word, Excel, Powerpoint, Outlook) is required.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and French (written and spoken) is required;

- Knowledge of additional UN official language is an asset.

Reporting:

The intern will report to the Advisor Pathfinder Endeavour for Multisectoral Action on Malaria • HQ/BERA/RO/Geneva.

Only applicants available for six months be considered. Applicants must state their availability.

Conditions of the Internship:

- As of 1 January 2020, Interns may be given a stipend according to the UNDP Internship Policies, if is not financially supported by any institution or programme, such as a university, government, foundation or scholarship programme,

- Interns are responsible for securing adequate medical insurance for the duration of the internship. UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship;

- The intern is responsible for obtaining necessary visas and arranging travel to and from the duty station where the internship will be performed;

- Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship;

- Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity;

- The purpose of the Internship Programme is not to lead to further employment with UNDP but to complement an intern’s studies. Therefore, there should be no expectation of employment at the end of an internship;

- The intern will be evaluated at the end of the contract and due recognition of work will be issued in writing.

In case an applicant is successfully selected, s/he will be requested to provide electronic versions of the following documents:

- Copy of the applicant’s most recent resume or curriculum vitae;

- Letter from his/her university confirming current enrollment and graduation date;

- Letter of recommendation from a professor;

- Copy of his/her school transcript;

- Copy of passport;

- Completed UNDP internship application form (to be provided upon selection);

- Signed UNDP Internship Agreement (to be provided upon selection);

- Medical Certificate of Good Health (to be provided upon selection);

- Proof of medical insurance (to be provided upon selection).

Application process:

- In your application, please (i) state in one paragraph why you would like to be considered for the internship, and (ii) indicate your preferred start and end date, as well as your availability timeframe in 2026/27 (6 months).

- Please submit your CV/Resume

Please Note that only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Disclaimer

Important information for US Permanent Residents ('Green Card' holders)

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. UNDP advises applicants for all professional level posts that they must relinquish their US Permanent Resident status and accept a G-4 visa, or have submitted a valid application for US citizenship prior to commencement of employment.

UNDP is not in a position to provide advice or assistance on applying for US citizenship and therefore applicants are advised to seek the advice of competent immigration lawyers regarding any applications.

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Procurement & Log Assistant - UNOCHA
jobs.description:
INFORMATION GENERALES

Le Bureau de la coordination des affaires humanitaires des Nations Unies (OCHA) fait partie du Secrétariat de l’Organisation des Nations Unies. Il est chargé de rassembler les acteurs humanitaires afin d’assurer une réponse cohérente aux situations d’urgence. OCHA veille également à l’existence d’un cadre permettant à chaque acteur de contribuer efficacement aux efforts de réponse collective.

La mission d’OCHA est de mobiliser et de coordonner une action humanitaire efficace et fondée sur des principes, en partenariat avec les acteurs nationaux et internationaux, afin d’atténuer les souffrances humaines causées par les catastrophes et les situations d’urgence ; de défendre les droits des personnes dans le besoin ; de promouvoir la préparation et la prévention ; et de faciliter des solutions durables.

Le Bureau régional pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (ROWCA), basé à Dakar, cherche à renforcer ses capacités opérationnelles, notamment sa présence auprès des populations affectées. Conformément à son mandat, OCHA collecte, compile, analyse et diffuse des informations relatives aux situations humanitaires et à l’assistance apportée dans la région.

Pour plus d’informations sur le mandat d’OCHA, veuillez consulter : https://www.unocha.org/ .

RESPONSABILITES/RESULTATS CLES ATTENDUS

Afin de répondre à ses besoins opérationnels, OCHA souhaite renforcer son Bureau régional pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (ROWCA) à travers le recrutement d’un(e) Assistant(e) Logistique et Achats.

Sous la supervision directe du Spécialiste national de l’administration et des achats d’OCHA/ROWCA, l’Assistant(e) Logistique et Achats veille au fonctionnement efficient et efficace du bureau, tout en faisant preuve d’un haut degré de confidentialité dans l’exercice de ses fonctions.

Fournir un appui administratif aux activités d’acquisition de biens et de services, avec les résultats attendus suivants :

- Examiner, enregistrer et hiérarchiser les demandes d’achats, et obtenir toutes les informations et tous les documents complémentaires nécessaires.

- Vérifier la disponibilité des prestataires de services et des fournisseurs.

- Assurer le suivi de l’état d’avancement des demandes en cours.

- Effectuer un suivi auprès des fournisseurs afin de garantir la livraison des biens et services dans les délais prévus.

- Vérifier la clarté des demandes d’achats et solliciter des informations supplémentaires lorsque cela est nécessaire.

- Appuyer la préparation des dossiers d’appel d’offres, notamment les demandes de devis et les demandes de propositions, selon la nature et la valeur de l’acquisition.

- Finaliser les bons de commande et les notes de dossier.

- Assurer la tenue et l’archivage des informations de gestion interne dans les bases de données et les dossiers.

- Rechercher, recueillir et présenter des informations provenant de sources internes et externes concernant les fournisseurs appropriés.

- Rédiger des correspondances administratives, notamment des lettres, des télécopies (fax) et des notes de service (mémorandums).

Identifier les besoins du bureau en matière de matériel, de fournitures, d’équipements, etc., avec les résultats attendus suivants :

- Assurer le suivi des stocks et veiller à leur disponibilité permanente.

- Gérer les fournitures de bureau, les équipements et les véhicules.

- Veiller à l’entretien des locaux et des véhicules conformément aux règles et procédures des Nations Unies.

- Soumettre les bons de commande accompagnés des pièces justificatives au superviseur pour signature, puis les transmettre aux fournisseurs.

Gestion du courrier et des communications téléphoniques :

- Préparer les documents et colis destinés à être expédiés par valise diplomatique ou par courrier express.

- Distribuer le courrier reçu du bureau de poste.

- Tenir un registre de tout le courrier entrant.

- Vérifier le courrier reçu et le transmettre au destinataire approprié.

- Assurer le classement et l’archivage appropriés de tous les documents entrants et sortants

Tâches administratives liées au fonctionnement du bureau

- Veiller au bon fonctionnement des services de nettoyage des bureaux.

- Assister à l’entretien des bureaux et des espaces de stationnement.

- Appuyer la préparation des badges d’accès et assurer le suivi de leur bon fonctionnement.

- Assister à la gestion du groupe électrogène et au suivi de sa maintenance périodique.

- Appuyer la planification de l’utilisation des salles de réunion (disponibilité, propreté et vérification de l’installation).

- Assurer le suivi de l’approvisionnement en fournitures pour les pause-café.

- Gérer l’approvisionnement et la distribution de l’eau potable (BA EAU BAB).

Gestion de l’inventaire des biens et du matériel de bureau

- Réaliser les inventaires conformément aux normes et procédures de l’organisation afin de garantir une traçabilité fiable.

- Enregistrer tous les articles d’inventaire dès leur acquisition, conformément aux normes et procédures applicables.

- Mettre régulièrement à jour les registres d’inventaire afin de refléter les mouvements des biens.

- Participer aux inventaires physiques annuels et aux processus de rapprochement (réconciliation) des inventaires.

Autres tâches administratives

- Fournir un appui administratif à l’organisation des ateliers, séminaires et événements organisés par OCHA.

- Assurer une gestion efficace des fournitures de bureau, ainsi que le contrôle et le maintien des niveaux de stock.

- Effectuer les réservations d’hôtel pour le personnel en mission pour le compte d’OCHA.

- Appuyer la gestion des documents administratifs relatifs aux véhicules : assurances, autorisations temporaires (AT), visites techniques, immatriculations, prolongations d’AT, ventes en franchise de droits et formalités de dédouanement.

- Mettre à jour le tableau de suivi de la consommation de carburant.

- Assurer le rapport quotidien de présence du personnel à des fins de sécurité.

Le titulaire exécute d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du bureau et de l'Organisation.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: N/A

COMPETENCES

Compétences corporatives :

- Obtenir des résultats: Niveau 1 : Est ouvert(e) aux idées créatives et aux risques connus, adopte une approche pragmatique de la résolution des problèmes et propose des améliorations.

- Penser de manière innovante: Niveau 1 : Est ouvert(e) aux idées créatives et aux risques connus, adopte une approche pragmatique de la résolution des problèmes et propose des améliorations.

- Apprendre en continu : Niveau 1 : Fait preuve d’ouverture d’esprit et de curiosité, partage ses connaissances, tire des enseignements de ses erreurs et sollicite des retours d’information.

- S’adapter avec agilité : Niveau 1 : S’adapte aux changements, gère de manière constructive l’ambiguïté et l’incertitude, et fait preuve de flexibilité.

- Agir avec détermination : Niveau 1 : Fait preuve de motivation et d’engagement, est capable de travailler avec sang-froid dans l’adversité et inspire confiance.

- Collaborer et développer des partenariats : Niveau 1 : Fait preuve d’empathie et de compréhension envers les autres et établit des relations de travail positives.

- Promouvoir la diversité et l’inclusion : Niveau 1 : Apprécie et respecte les différences, est conscient(e) des biais inconscients et s’oppose à toute forme de discrimination.

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Compétences fonctionnelles :

Achat:

- Approvisionnement et recherche de fournisseurs : Capacité à identifier, évaluer et mobiliser des fournisseurs de biens et de services.

- Analyse Financière : Connaissance des méthodes d’évaluation des entreprises, des projets, des budgets et d’autres opérations financières afin de déterminer leur performance et leur pertinence.

- Gestion des données : Connaissance du traitement, du stockage et de la validation des données relatives aux achats.

- Gestion des achats : Capacité à acquérir des biens, des services ou des travaux auprès de fournisseurs externes, conformément aux procédures établies.

Gestion des activités:

- Satisfaction client /Gestion de la relation client : Capacité à répondre rapidement et de manière appropriée avec un sens de l’urgence, à fournir des solutions cohérentes et à produire des résultats et services de qualité dans les délais requis afin de répondre aux besoins réels des clients. Contribuer à l’élaboration de stratégies de service à la clientèle. Rechercher des moyens d’apporter une valeur ajoutée au-delà des demandes immédiates des clients. Capacité à anticiper les besoins et les préoccupations futurs des clients.

- Communication : Capacité à communiquer de manière claire, concise et sans ambiguïté, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit, et à adapter les messages ainsi que les méthodes de communication en fonction du public cible. Capacité à gérer la communication interne et externe par le biais des médias, des réseaux sociaux et d’autres canaux appropriés.

QUALIFICATIONS

Formation :

- Un diplôme de fin d’études secondaires est requis.

- Une licence (ou un diplôme universitaire) en Administration des affaires, en Administration publique, en Finance ou dans une discipline équivalente sera prise en considération, mais ne constitue pas une exigence obligatoire.

- La certification CIPS niveau 2 est fortement souhaitée pour ce poste, et les candidats qui détiennent ce niveau de certification au moment de leur candidature bénéficieront d’un avantage certain. Si cette certification souhaitée n’est pas disponible au moment du recrutement, elle devra être obtenue au cours de l’année suivant le recrutement. Les candidats détenant, au moment de leur candidature, une certification CIPS d’un niveau inférieur bénéficieront d’un avantage proportionnel à leur niveau de certification.

Expérience professionnelle :

- Au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle avec un diplôme de fin d’études secondaires ou deux (2) années d’expérience avec une licence, dans les domaines de l’administration, du secrétariat, de la logistique ou dans tout autre domaine pertinent sont requises.

- Une expérience en logistique (gestion du personnel, sécurité incendie, transfert de biens et d’équipements, etc.), en particulier dans les zones touchées par des urgences humanitaires, est requise.

- Une expérience récente de travail dans l’approvisionnement et la logistique d’un bureau régional d’une agence des Nations Unies ou d’organismes internationaux constitue un atout.

- Une bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques est requise, notamment de Microsoft Office (Word, Excel et PowerPoint), Outlook et d’Internet.

Langues:

- Une maîtrise courante du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, est requise.

- La connaissance de l’anglais est souhaitable. La connaissance d’une autre langue officielle des Nations Unies constitue un atout.

Égalité des chances

En tant qu'employeur souscrivant au principe de l'égalité des chances, UNOCHA valorise la diversité en tant qu'expression de la multiplicité des nations et des cultures où nous opérons et, à ce titre, nous encourageons les candidats qualifiés de tous horizons à postuler à des postes au sein de l'organisation. Nos décisions d'embauche sont fondées sur le mérite et l'aptitude au poste, sans discrimination.

Le UNOCHA s'engage également à créer un lieu de travail inclusif où tout le personnel est habilité à contribuer à notre mission, est valorisé, peut s'épanouir et bénéficie d'opportunités de carrière ouvertes à tous.

Harcèlement sexuel, exploitation et abus d'autorité

Le UNOCHA ne tolère pas le harcèlement, le harcèlement sexuel, l'exploitation, la discrimination et l'abus d'autorité. Tous les candidats sélectionnés sont donc soumis à des contrôles pertinents et doivent respecter les normes et principes respectifs.

Période d’essai

Pour toutes les nouvelles nominations à durée déterminée (FTA) a UNOCHA, y compris pour les agents transférés ou détachés a UNOCHA dans le cadre de l’Accord inter-organisations concernant le transfert, le détachement ou le prêt de personnel, et pour toute nomination de plus d’un an, la poursuite du contrat au-delà des 12 premiers mois est conditionnée à la réussite de la période d’essai.

Droit de sélectionner plusieurs candidats

UNOCHA se réserve le droit de sélectionner un ou plusieurs candidats à partir de cette annonce de vacance de poste. Nous pouvons également retenir les candidatures et prendre en considération les candidats qui postulent à ce poste pour d'autres postes similaires a UNOCHA, au même niveau et avec une description de poste, une expérience et des exigences éducationnelles similaires.

Utilisation de l’IA par les candidats

Les candidats sont invités à consulter les directives du PNUD concernant l’utilisation responsable de l’IA dans les processus de recrutement et de sélection.

Alerte aux escroqueries

Le PNUD ne facture aucune redevance à aucun stade de son processus de recrutement. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Quantity Surveyor [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The KOICA-funded Abuja Centre for Entrepreneurship (ACE) Project, implemented through a partnership between KOICA, UNDP and SMEDAN, seeks to establish a functional, energy-efficient and accessible entrepreneurship centre in Abuja that strengthens Nigeria’s entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystem. The project involves the construction and development of the ACE facility at the SMEDAN Compound in Idu Industrial Area. The facility is designed to provide a conducive environment for youth development, entrepreneurship, innovation and lifelong learning, with a particular focus on young entrepreneurs, start-ups, MSMEs, women, persons with disabilities and other underserved groups. Direct beneficiaries include prospective youth entrepreneurs, start-ups across FinTech, EdTech, HealthTech and Agri Tech, and MSMEs, alongside professionals and workers engaged across the construction supply chain.

The project contributes to SDGs 4, 8, 9 and 17 and aligns with Nigeria’s Development Plan, Digital Economy Policy and Strategy, National MSME Policy and FCT Economic and Empowerment Development Strategies, as well as KOICA’s priorities on digital skills, youth empowerment, innovation, industrial development and women’s economic empowerment. Under the partnership, KOICA and UNDP are responsible for the design, construction, environmental and social safeguards, project supervision, installation of solar photovoltaic systems, landscaping and preparation of the facility for handover to SMEDAN, while SMEDAN will serve as the implementing/partner agency. The project is expected to deliver approved architectural and engineering designs, a completed ACE facility and associated services, and effective project communication and visibility, ultimately providing a green, energy-efficient and fully accessible entrepreneurship facility that can support the growth of Nigeria’s youth-led enterprises and MSMEs.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the National Programme Specialist/ the NJFP Project Manager, the Quantity Surveyor will be responsible for the following functions and tasks:

1.Actively support the assessment activities for infrastructure construction/rehabilitation activities in the targeted sites.

- Conduct site visits to assess the need for civil works;

- Prepare an analysis of the civil works intervention and cost estimate.

2. Actively support the preparation of technical documents for the civil works projects and prepare detailed BOQs, specifications and internal cost estimates

- Review and verify the designs of infrastructure facilities, such as police facilities, school buildings, toilet and WASH facilities, boreholes, housing units and others;

- Review and certify the government standard specifications, which are submitted by the respective authorities for civil works. Recommend the necessary adjustments, if any;

- Prepare detailed BOQs, specifications and cost estimate of infrastructure facilities.

3. Provide technical and civil engineering support for smooth procurement

- Work with the project team to produce project technical documents for the procurement unit for processing;

- Work closely with the procurement unit and support in advertising the civil works procurement cases, pre-bid meetings and bidders' clarifications;

- Support technical evaluation process. prepare bids arithmetic check and Financial Analysis (FA) reports;

- Provide advice on any procurement-related issues;

- Support the KOICA project in verifying the Variation Orders (VO) (if required);

- Assist UNDP as an expert witness in litigation arising from the development or construction of the project and in bearings before various approving and regulatory agencies.

4. Ensure the management of civil works projects

- Conduct construction inspection including inspection of materials, samples, and equipment to be installed are meeting the UNDP Contract specifications and standards;

- Ensure that the Contractors maintain safety on the site and clean the site after the completion of the rehabilitation work;

- Support monitoring progress of infrastructure construction/rehabilitation activities particularly from an engineering point of view and promptly report any abnormality or risks to the respective UNDP project managers and project teams;

- Discuss site issues with the Contractor for construction/renovation of civil works projects and promptly report back to UNDP if a problem arises that requires UNDP input;

- Verify payments submitted by the contracts and prepare valuation of work implemented;

- Identify and report risks or abnormalities related to civil works to the Senior Civil Engineer and the engineering team as well as respective project managers;

- Ensuring proper close-out of projects (site cleaning, payment of wages etc) by contractors before demobilisation.

5. Facilitate knowledge, capacity building and knowledge sharing.

- Assist in organizing training, workshops, and capacity building activities in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia;

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners;

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on project related issues;

- Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional arrangements:

The Quantity Surveyor would be reporting to the the National Programme Specialist/ NJFP Project Manager.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Management

- Results-based Management Ability to manage programmes and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results; Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools. Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Direction & Strategy

Strategic Thinking

- Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP's objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions.

- Ability to leverage learning from a variety of sources to anticipate and respond to future trends; to demonstrate foresight in order to model what future developments and possible ways forward look like for UNDP.

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Development

- Communication Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Partnership management

- Relationship Management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in the field of Construction Management, Quantity Surveying or closely related fields is required. Or

- A first university degree (bachelor’s degree) with a combination of additional two years of qualifying relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- CIPS level 3 is highly desirable for this position and candidates holding this level at the time of application will have a distinct advantage. If the desired certification is not available at the time of recruitment, it should be obtained within one year of recruitment. Candidates holding a CIPS certification at any level below at the time of application will have a proportionate advantage.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in quantity surveying for residential and public service infrastructures, including construction and renovation projects is required.

Required Skills

- Experience in Project management is required;

- Experience in Civil Works Procurement is required;

- Experience in handling tender documents for turnkey contracts, including technical inputs/specifications for the procurement of services using the conditions of international lending/funding agencies is required;

- Proven ability to work with multi-disciplinary teams and liaison with authorities is required.

Desired Skills

- Proficiency in preparing bills of quantities (BOQs), and cost estimates for structural items is desired;

- Experience with Quantum or similar systems is desirable;

- Experience in managing quantity surveying aspects of large-scale projects and solar power projects is desirable;

- Experience in accurately assessing project costs, analyzing construction materials and labor requirements, and ensuring cost-effectiveness throughout project lifecycles is desirable;

- Experience in the use of Microsoft Office packages, and ERP systems like Oracle, Quantum is desirable.

Languages

- Fluency in English is required.

Other Requirements

- Member of the Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria (QSRBN) is an asset.

- Member Nigeria Institute of Quantity Surveyors is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Humanitarian Affairs Officer
jobs.description:
The duty station is Rasuwa, Nepal.

Background

The Humanitarian Affairs Officer, UNOCHA, position is established to support the humanitarian response to the floods affecting Rasuwa and surrounding disaster-affected areas of Nepal. The position is intended to reinforce UN field-level coordination during the immediate response period, working closely with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, humanitarian partners, and affected communities. Under the direct supervision of the RCO/OCHA Bidur Hub lead and the overall supervision of the Resident Coordinator’s Office Nepal and the Head of OCHA’s Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP), the incumbent will work in close collaboration with the UN Resident Coordinator, Government and relief/recovery partners to support the formulation of strategies of engagement in support of the mandate of OCHA at both managerial and operational levels.

The Humanitarian Affairs Officer will provide on-site humanitarian coordination in flood-affected areas, with a particular focus in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. The incumbent will help ensure that operational agencies and local authorities have a common understanding of priority needs, response activities, constraints and gaps, and that field-level issues requiring attention are communicated promptly to relevant coordination and decision-making structures. The role is operational and field-facing and requires regular travel to affected communities and response locations. The incumbent will also be responsible for providing advice and support to the Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator and operational partners to consider the priorities of the most vulnerable communities in humanitarian and early recovery planning.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Ensures effective humanitarian coordination at field level in support of national authorities

•Provide a visible and sustained OCHA /RCO coordination presence in Rasuwa and other designated flood-affected areas.

•Facilitate and support field coordination meetings with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, Red Cross/Red Crescent actors and other operational partners.

•Promote complementarity among responders, identify duplication and gaps, and support practical follow-up on agreed coordination actions.

•Maintain regular liaison with affected communities and relevant local structures so priority concerns can inform coordination discussions.

•Support field partners to steer a collective approach to Accountability to Affected People (AAP). This means joint community consultations, harmonized messaging in local languages, and shared feedback and complaint mechanisms, whose findings inform response planning and are followed up with communities. Work with the PSEA Network and agency focal points so that these channels are safe and accessible for reporting sexual exploitation and abuse, and that survivor-centred referral pathways are in place and known to communities and responders.

2.) Monitoring, assessment and analysis of humanitarian needs

•Monitor humanitarian conditions, priority needs, access constraints, emerging risks and response coverage through regular field visits and engagement with partners.

•Support or participate in inter-agency rapid assessments and field missions as required.

•Consolidate field observations and partner inputs into concise situation updates, analysis and recommendations for OCHA and humanitarian leadership.

•Flag critical gaps, underserved locations and operational bottlenecks requiring coordinated action.

3.) Support to operational response and emergency preparedness

•Promote timely coordination around immediate life-saving priorities and evolving operational requirements following the floods.

•Support contingency and preparedness discussions where continuing rainfall, landslides, access disruption or other hazards may affect communities or response operations.

•Encourage partners to integrate relevant humanitarian policies and principles, protection considerations, accountability to affected people and inclusion in field-level response planning.

4.) Information sharing, reporting and coordination support

•Maintain regular information exchange between responders in affected areas and coordination structures at national and regional levels.

•Support partners to engage women, persons with disabilities, older persons and marginalized groups in response decisions, using safe and inclusive channels that also serve as entry points for PSEA reporting and referral.

•Track how community feedback is acted upon across partners, and flag recurring concerns, including SEA risks, to coordination forums and the PSEA Network so the response can adjust.

•Prepare meeting records, action points, field updates, briefing notes and inputs to humanitarian reporting products.

•Support mapping of operational presence, needs and response gaps in collaboration with information management colleagues and partners.

•Track agreed actions and follow up with responsible partners to support timely implementation

5) Partnership, advocacy and enabling humanitarian access

•Build constructive working relationships with local and district authorities, humanitarian organizations, civil society and community representatives.

•Identify operational or coordination issues that may impede assistance and elevate them through appropriate channels.

•Provide field evidence and analysis to support advocacy on priority humanitarian needs, equitable assistance and effective response coverage.

Work implies frequent interaction with the following:

Staff at all levels within RCO/OCHA Bidur Hub, UN RCO Nepal and Regional Offfice for Asia and the Pacific . Representatives of Nepal National Disaster Management Organizations, other UN agencies and other organizations that work on disaster risk managemet and related issues.

Results Expected:

Provides sound analytical inputs and advice that contributes to improving institutional capacity and articulates humanitarian response to the Nepal 2026 Flash Flood with a special focus in Rasuwa. Provides timely delivery of assigned tasks, maintains partnerships and interacts effectively with colleagues internally and externally.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

Show Managerial Courage

• Face up to organizational and people problems

• Not be afraid to take decisions and action when and as needed

• Not hold back anything that needs to be said, respectfully and diplomatically

• Address conflict in a timely manner, not allow conflicts in teams to linger

• Help others through emotional or tense situations, tactfully bringing disagreements into the open and finding solutions all can endorse

Demonstrate Empathy and Emotional Intelligence

• Genuinely care about people; demonstrate empathy with the joys and pains of others

jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

As the United Nations lead agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities, and to build resilience to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Our work is concentrated in three focus areas; sustainable development, democratic governance and peace building, and climate and disaster resilience. UNDP advocates for change, and connects countries to global knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life.

UNDP has supported Kyrgyzstan’s development progress since 1992 and supports the country in charting future pathways towards greater prosperity, resilience, and social cohesion. As an impartial policy advisor and integrator, UNDP works within the UN system and with all stakeholders in government, civil society, and private sector to advance inclusive, fundamentally sound development solutions and reforms in complex settings. Our United Nations identity ensures neutrality and respect for people’s choices. Transparency and accountability in operations makes us a trusted partner for national and international development stakeholders.

UNDP encourages and enables collective intelligence, collaboration, integration, critical thinking, and thought leadership. We mainstream innovation, digitalization opportunities, gender equity and diversity/inclusion principles in all aspects of our work. Our staff consistently strive for excellence, effectiveness, efficiency and inclusion across all areas of work.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Technical support: • Support for technical production of communication and advocacy materials and tools for UNDP projects; • Design communications products for social media channels: • Promote and strengthen UNDP’s presence in social media network; • Support with carrying out public events related to projects implementation; • Support with development and coordination of the production of weekly communications plans.

- Visual content production • Assist the team with providing high-quality writing/editing/proofreading social media content and conducting digital outreach in Kyrgyz/Russian and English; • Assist with producing video reels on UNDP key topics in simple way tailored for different social media platforms; • Assist with production of photo essays for UNDP key areas of work; • Contribute to writingstories, articles, blogs, and press releases in English and Kyrgyz/Russian languages.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

1. Contexte

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) en Tunisie accompagne la Cour des comptes dans la mise en œuvre de son plan stratégique 2022-2026. La Cour des comptes est une institution constitutionnelle clé, qui joue un rôle essentiel dans l'audit et la surveillance des finances publiques. Depuis l'indépendance de la Tunisie, la Cour a considérablement élargi ses fonctions, notamment en matière de contrôle des finances publiques, de surveillance du financement des partis politiques et d'évaluation des politiques publiques.

Pour répondre à ces nouvelles exigences, la Cour des comptes est en pleine transformation, d'une institution d'audit classique à une véritable juridiction financière. Cette transition nécessite une modernisation de son cadre institutionnel, de ses méthodes de gestion, ainsi qu'une meilleure interaction avec le public et les autres institutions. La mise en œuvre du troisième plan stratégique de la Cour est au cœur de cette transformation, visant à renforcer sa gouvernance interne, à améliorer son indépendance administrative et financière, et à moderniser ses méthodes de travail.

Le projet, financé par la Délégation de l’Union Européenne en Tunisie, a pour objectif d'accompagner la Cour des comptes sur une période de trois ans dans la mise en œuvre de ce plan stratégique. Il se concentre sur le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles, l'amélioration de l'évaluation des politiques publiques, le renforcement de la communication avec les parties prenantes, et l'introduction d'outils numériques pour garantir la transparence, la redevabilité et l'efficacité. L'objectif ultime est de renforcer la transparence et la redevabilité, pour une plus grande confiance des citoyens.

Dans ce cadre, le PNUD recrute un.e Analyste de projet pour appuyer la gestion de projet.

2. Devoirs et responsabilités

Sous la supervision directe du Conseiller(ère) Technique Principal.e (CTP) en sa capacité de chef(fe) de projet, l’Analyste de Projet intervient dans (i) la planification des ressources du projet, la coordination et la mise en œuvre efficace du projet, (ii) les activités de suivi du progrès et de rapportage sur la mise en œuvre du projet et (iii) la facilitation de la gestion, du renforcement et du partage des connaissances.

1- Appuyer la planification, la coordination et la mise en œuvre efficace du projet

- Appuyer le/la CTP dans l’élaboration des plans de travail incluant les allocations budgétaires nécessaires, en ligne avec le document de projet et conformément aux politiques et procédures relatives aux programmes et aux opérations (POPP) du PNUD en matière de gestion de programme et de projet.

- Contribuer aux processus de planification trimestrielles et annuelles des activités du projet.

- Soutenir le/la CTP dans la coordination et la gestion des activités quotidiennes du projet, tout en identifiant les problèmes potentiels, afin de mettre en oeuvre des mesures correctives.

- Assurer la gestion et le suivi budgétaire trimestriel, annuel et pluriannuels du projet en veillant à ce que les ressources financières soient allouées et utilisées d’une manière au aux plans de travail, au budget et aux procédures en vigueur.

- Préparer un calendrier clair de suivi des obligations du projet et veiller au suivi des différents échéances relatives aux contrats et missions engagés.

- Contribuer à l’élaboration des termes de références et notes conceptuelles nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des activités.

- Contribuer à l’organisation des ateliers et missions de terrain prévues, et tout autre activité définie dans le projet.

- Assurer et faciliter la coordination des opérations entre l’équipe du projet d’une part et les unités Ressources Humaines, Achats et Finances du bureau PNUD Tunisie d’une autre part.

2- Appuyer les activités de suivi du progrès et de rapportage de la mise en œuvre du projet

- Préparer les rapports financiers requis pour accompagner l’exécution des plans de travail et les rapports trimestriels et annuels du projet.

- Etablir un calendrier de reporting pour faciliter le suivi et l'évaluation du plan de travail approuvé.

- Soutenir le/la CTP dans la préparation des rapports, internes et externes, de progrès et l’état d’avancement des activités, des produits et des résultats conformément aux règles et procédures du PNUD.

- Soutenir le/la CTP dans le suivi, l’identification et l’actualisation de la matrice des risques liées à la mise en œuvre du projet.

- Identifier les changements dans l'environnement externe du projet et aviser le/la CTP sur les solutions/actions nécessaires.

3- Faciliter la gestion, le renforcement et le partage des connaissances

- Documenter et appuyer la diffusion des leçons apprises et des meilleures pratiques tirées de la mise en œuvre du projet.

- Maintenir dans les espaces dédiés la documentation du projet, y compris les plans de travail du projet, les procès-verbaux des réunions et les rapports d'avancement ainsi que toute autre exigence en matière d’archivage, conformément à la politique du bureau en vigueur.

- Renforcer la production de connaissances à travers les activités du projet.

- Soutenir la mise en place de plateformes de connaissances pour le projet, faciliter les mécanismes innovants de diffusion des connaissances issues du projet, et développer des ressources et des produits de connaissances à partager avec les partenaires du projet de sorte à soutenir l'engagement du PNUD.

Le/la titulaire sera amené(e) à exécuter d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel et jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

3. Dispositions institutionnelles

L’Analyste de Projet agira sous la supervision directe du CTP, sous la coordination programmatique et opérationnelle du Cluster Gouvernance démocratique, et en collaboration étroite avec l’équipe des Opérations du bureau de pays.

4. Compétences

Core

NIVEAU 1 : Ouvert aux idées créatives/risques connus, résolveur de problèmes pragmatique, apporte des améliorations

NIVEAU 1 : Ouvert d’esprit et curieux, partage ses connaissances, apprend de ses erreurs, demande du feedback

Agissez avec détermination :

NIVEAU 1: Fait preuve de dynamisme et de motivation, capable de livrer calmement face à l’adversité, confiant

NIVEAU 1 : Faire preuve de compassion et de compréhension envers les autres, établir des relations positives

jobs.title: Project Analyst-Medical Equipment and Health Systems, NPSA-9, DS - Kyiv, National Position
jobs.description:
Background

Empowered to work across the spectrum of human development, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) operates in about 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty, reduce inequalities and advance the Sustainable Development Goals. Guided by its Strategic Plan (2026–2029), UNDP focuses on prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience and a healthy planet. In Ukraine, and in alignment with its Country Programme Document (2025–2029) and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, UNDP supports emergency response and long-term recovery, including restoration of essential social infrastructure and inclusive access to health services.

Within this framework, UNDP Ukraine is implementing the Strengthening Civilian Health Service Delivery in Ukraine project, funded by the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief). The project supports civilian hospitals in Kyiv, Odesa and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts through the needs-based procurement, delivery, installation and operationalization of priority medical equipment and related supplies. Supported facilities serve high patient volumes and are selected in coordination with the relevant health authorities in accordance with the approved project criteria.

To ensure that project-supported equipment is clinically justified, technically appropriate, safely installed and sustainably operated, UNDP requires a Health Analyst-Medical Equipment and Health Systems. The Analyst will serve as the project’s technical health focal point and will coordinate technical inputs with the Ministry of Health of Ukraine, the National Health Service of Ukraine, regional health authorities, beneficiary hospitals, the UNDP Procurement Unit, engineering specialists and other relevant experts. The role covers needs validation, facility-readiness assessment, technical specifications and evaluation, delivery and commissioning, acceptance and handover, training, maintenance planning, monitoring and technical risk management. Project-supported investments will be aligned with national health reforms, regional hospital-network plans, referral pathways and applicable service-delivery, safety and regulatory standards.

Duties and Responsibilities

I. Coordinate effective project planning and implementation

• Provide technical inputs to the project work plan, procurement plan, implementation schedules and budget estimates for medical equipment and related activities, and monitor the timely completion of assigned technical actions.

• Validate hospital equipment needs through desk review, consultations and on-site assessment, confirming clinical justification, prioritization, cost-effectiveness and consistency with the approved project scope.

• Together with relevant engineering and technical specialists, assess facility readiness for each equipment item, including space and access; electrical supply, grounding, voltage stability and backup power; ventilation, cooling, water, drainage and medical gases; radiation protection and permits; infection prevention and waste arrangements; network connectivity, cybersecurity and software compatibility; physical accessibility; and the availability of qualified staff, consumables, licences and maintenance capacity. Documentary assurances shall not replace technical verification.

• Prepare and finalize performance-based, technology-neutral technical specifications, equipment schedules, technical evaluation criteria and compliance matrices, including documented justification for essential compatibility requirements.

• Participate as a technical member or adviser to evaluation committees; assess technical compliance, deviations, equivalencies and bidder clarifications; document findings in accordance with UNDP procedures; maintain confidentiality; disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest; and exercise no independent procurement or award authority unless formally delegated.

• Verify delivered quantities, models, serial numbers, accessories, software, consumables and technical documentation; witness or coordinate installation, calibration, commissioning and acceptance testing; verify correction of defects and missing items before acceptance; and support preparation of acceptance certificates, asset records and handover documentation.

II. Establish partnerships and open channels of communication

• Serve as the project’s technical health focal point and coordinate technical inputs with the Ministry of Health of Ukraine, the National Health Service of Ukraine, regional health authorities, beneficiary facilities, the Procurement Analyst/UNDP Procurement Unit, engineering specialists and other relevant experts.

• Facilitate technical coordination with hospital staff and suppliers while communicating with bidders and suppliers only through authorized procurement channels. Strategic partnerships, donor relations and overall stakeholder management remain the responsibility of the Project Manager.

III. Facilitate expert and technical advisory support to local authorities and communities

• Ensure that project-supported medical-equipment investments are aligned with national health reforms, regional hospital-network plans, referral pathways and applicable service-delivery, regulatory, quality and safety standards.

• Provide technical advice to regional and local authorities and beneficiary hospitals on the safe and effective integration of equipment into clinical workflows, referral arrangements, staffing, accessibility, infection-prevention measures and operational procedures, and support related capacity-development activities.

IV. Monitor and report on progress in implementing project activities and achieving the targets set

• Collect and validate baseline service-delivery data and monitor post-installation equipment utilization, functionality and contribution to the project’s approved results and indicators.

• Conduct regular field visits to supported facilities to verify readiness, delivery, installation, operational performance and compliance with applicable technical, safety and quality requirements.

• Compile technical monitoring information and provide substantive inputs for corporate, donor, government and project reports, as required by the approved reporting schedule.

• Identify, document and promptly escalate technical risks relating to facility readiness, supply and delivery, regulatory or licensing requirements, staffing, utilities, consumables and maintenance affordability, electrical and radiation safety, equipment compatibility, cybersecurity, warranty and after-sales service; recommend and follow up appropriate mitigation measures.

• Provide technical inputs required for project reporting, equipment acceptance, handover, sustainability planning and operational closure.

V. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the area of expertise

• Coordinate and verify supplier-provided training for doctors, nurses, technicians and other end users, covering safe operation, basic troubleshooting and routine maintenance, and retain evidence of completion.

• Support preventive-maintenance schedules, warranty administration and fault-escalation procedures; confirm local or regional servicing arrangements; transfer supplier and warranty contacts to recipient facilities; and obtain facility commitments for recurrent costs, consumables and continued operation.

• Identify and document lessons learned and good practices, and contribute technical inputs to knowledge products and capacity-development activities relevant to resilient civilian health service delivery.

VI. Ensure the mainstreaming of gender equality and women’s empowerment considerations in the healthcare sector, and promote a safe, enabling environment free of discrimination and abusive behaviour in line with corporate standards

• Support equitable access to project-supported health services for women and men, girls and boys, including persons with disabilities and other groups facing barriers to care.

• Apply gender-responsive and inclusive communication principles in line with UNDP standards.

• Identify relevant gender and inclusion issues in equipment planning, facility readiness, training, service access and monitoring, and raise them with the Project Manager.

• Promote a team culture of equality, respect and zero tolerance for sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, discrimination and other misconduct.

• Demonstrate respect for diversity and inclusion in all professional interactions.

• Support the communication of applicable UNDP safeguarding and prevention-of-sexual-exploitation-and-abuse requirements to relevant personnel and partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Analyst-Medical Equipment and Health Systems will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager and in close day-to-day coordination with the Procurement Analyst/UNDP Procurement Unit, relevant engineering and technical specialists, and other members of the project team.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:
