jobs.title: Associate Finance Officer
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) coordinates effective and principled humanitarian response and ensures that relief assistance reaches the people in need in a timely manner. OCHA-managed Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) is a multi-donor country-based pooled mechanism created in 2010 to allocate funding for the most urgent life-saving interventions in Somalia. Combining flexibility and strategic focus, the Fund ensures timely allocation and disbursement of resources, enables effective humanitarian action, and strengthens coordination.

The Associate Finance Officer - communication, under the guidance of the Head, Humanitarian Financing Unit (HFU), and direct supervision of the SHF Finance Officer, participates in the overall implementation of the SHF Accountability Framework and works in close collaboration with the HFU and other OCHA Somalia staff, as well as cluster coordination staff. He/she is expected to travel extensively to the SHF project locations within Somalia to assist with the implementation of the SHF Accountability Framework as well as provide support in communications and external relations activities of the SHF.

Duties and Responsibilities

1) Provide support in the allocation and financial management processes of the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF)

- Review and advise on the clearance of the project budgets and grant agreements;

- Review and advise on budget amendments or no-cost extension requests;

- Regular follow-up with IP to obtain financial reports;

- Review of interim and final financial reports and supporting documents to ensure compliance with the signed SHF agreements, budgets and guidelines;

- Follow up on disbursement of funds and refund of balances from partners;

- Review of grant agreements and supporting documents to ensure accuracy, consistency, reasonableness, compliance with the United Nations Financial Rules and Regulations (UNFRR) and the Country-based Pooled Funds (CBPF) Guidelines;

- Receipt & review of audit reports from contractors and ensure projects records are updated as necessary.

2) Provide support in implementing the financial aspects of the SHF Accountability Framework

- Conduct financial spot-checks in line with the SHF operational modalities;

- Facilitate and provide support during audits, at the project and fund level, as requested, including assistance with vendor contracting, supporting the planning process and assisting in the follow-up of critical audit findings;

- Liaise with partners, SHF/HFU staff and other third parties in verifying expenditure supporting documents during spot-checks, review of financial reports, capacity assessments and audits;

- Assist with the submission and return of Partners’ financial documentation for spot-checks in OCHA field offices.

3) Provide support to the implementation of the monitoring pillar of the SHF accountability framework.

- Contribute to the development and implementation of monitoring plans in line with allocation funding modalities;

- Participate in planning and actual field project monitoring together with other HFU/OCHA field staff;

- Participate in the request and review of partner due diligence information/document submissions and corresponding status update in Grant Management System (GMS);

- Assist with updating the project monitoring timelines, results and recommendations in the GMS.

4) Facilitate knowledge-building and knowledge-sharing on finance, monitoring & evaluation within OCHA Somalia, clusters and the SHF implementing partners

- Identify and synthesize finance, monitoring and evaluation best practices, lessons learned and recommendations to be integrated into fund management efforts and channeled into decision-making processes;

- Promote of awareness on SHF guidelines, operational manuals, clauses in partner agreements, UNFRR and best practices;

- Plan and participate in trainings to implementing partners and other stakeholders.

5) Provide support in communication and external relations activities

- Supports implementation of SHF communications activities, prepares public information and donor materials, and maintains the SHF website and social media.

- Serves as a focal point for the preparation of public information materials that feature information related to the implementation and impact of SHF-funded projects and interventions, including human interest stories that feature audio visual materials, text etc. across multiple platforms (website, bulletins and reports, social media). This includes proactive outreach to SHF Implementing Partners, cluster coordinators, OCHA communications teams locally and globally, HFU and other humanitarian stakeholders.

- Utilizes and analyses SHF monitoring data from SHF accountability mechanisms (OCHA field monitoring, third-party and call monitoring, cluster monitoring tools) as basis for SHF communications deliverables, including verification with partners and beneficiaries, to demonstrate impact and accountability to affected people.

- Supports with the preparation of donor communications materials, including briefing materials, presentations and info graphics on SHF and other humanitarian financing issues (HRP funding status etc.)

- Supports with the coordination of regular and ad hoc SHF donor meetings, including preparing relevant communications and briefing materials, drafting minutes and ensuring follow up on any action items.

- Supports with the production of the SHF annual and interim reports (development of the outline, drafting, data collection etc.).

- Supports with the regular update and management of the SHF section of OCHA Somalia website and OCHA Somalia social media presence

Competencies

- Professionalism : Knowledge of different aspects of humanitarian response, public information and communication. Ability to address a range of issues in the context of political developments, public attitudes and local conditions. Ability to conceptualize, design and implement major information campaigns. Ability to rapidly analyze and integrate diverse information from varied sources. Ability to diplomatically handle sensitive situations with target audiences and cultivate productive relationships. Ability to produce a variety of written communications products in a clear, concise style. Ability to deliver oral presentations to various audiences. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work.

- Communication : Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.

- Creativity: Actively seeks to improve programmes or services; offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs; promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas; takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas; thinks "outside the box"; takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things; is not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches.

- Accountability: Takes ownership for all responsibilities and honours commitments. Delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards. Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules. Supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments. Takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable.

- Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies. Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required. Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work. Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning. Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary. Uses time efficiently

jobs.description:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Liberia faces a complex and evolving humanitarian and protection context shaped by a combination of socioeconomic fragility, climate-related shocks, and pockets of recovery from past crises. Persistent poverty, high unemployment, food insecurity in vulnerable communities, and weak service delivery systems continue to expose significant segments of the population to heightened risk. Seasonal flooding, particularly in low-lying and densely populated areas such as Monrovia and surrounding counties, frequently leads to displacement, destruction of housing, disruption of livelihoods, and increased public health risks, further compounding household vulnerability.

Against this backdrop, protection risks remain significant, with Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (SEAH) continuing to be a critical concern within humanitarian and development settings. Liberia is consistently identified in regional safeguarding analyses as a context where SEA risks remain present due to structural vulnerabilities, limited access to complaint mechanisms in remote areas, power imbalances, and constrained institutional capacity. While awareness of Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards has improved across sectors, gaps remain in survivor-centered reporting systems, community trust in complaint mechanisms, and consistent accountability enforcement. Underreporting remains a key challenge, driven by fear of retaliation, stigma, and limited confidence that complaints will lead to meaningful action.

The UN and partners in Liberia have progressively strengthened collective safeguarding mechanisms through an inter-agency PSEA network composed of UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs/CSOs, donors, and relevant government counterparts. This network provides a coordinated platform for prevention, risk mitigation, and response to SEAH. It is typically chaired by an Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist, supported by rotating co-chairs, and links over 100 partner organizations across the humanitarian and development landscape. The network also engages a growing cadre of trained PSEA focal points to strengthen community outreach, awareness-raising, and safe referral pathways, while promoting survivor-centered approaches.

The inter-agency PSEA structure in Liberia reports to the UN Country Team (UNCT) and Humanitarian Country Team (HCT), which provide strategic oversight, guidance, and support for implementation of the collective PSEAH strategy and action plan. The Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist will report administratively to the Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) UNDP, to the Resident Coordinator/Humanitarian Coordinator, who holds system-wide accountability for advancing PSEA commitments across the UN and partners.

Investing in dedicated PSEA capacity in Liberia is essential to ensure that humanitarian and development assistance is delivered safely, ethically, and in line with “Do No Harm” principles. It strengthens accountability to affected populations, reduces reputational and operational risks, and supports donor expectations on safeguarding, gender equality, and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse.

Duties and Responsibilities

Strengthening Leadership, Accountability, and Coordination

- The role provides strategic leadership support to senior UN leadership in Liberia, particularly the Resident Coordinator (RC), UN Country Team (UNCT), and Humanitarian Country Team (HCT), to ensure effective Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH) across all UN and partner operations in Liberia.

- Provide strategic advisory support to senior leadership to ensure strong accountability for system-wide PSEAH implementation in Liberia.

- Collaborate closely with UN senior leadership to coordinate the inter-agency PSEAH Network in Liberia, including UN agencies, INGOs, national NGOs, civil society organizations, IFIs, and relevant Government of Liberia institutions.

- Represent inter-agency PSEAH priorities in key coordination platforms such as UNCT, HCT, OMT, Protection Cluster, Gender Theme Group, and other national coordination mechanisms.

- Work closely with Protection, GBV sub-sector, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Gender Theme Group, and sector leads to ensure PSEAH is fully integrated into programmes, policies, and joint planning frameworks in Liberia.

- Identify emerging risks, gaps, and trends related to SEAH in Liberia and advise RC/HC, UNCT/HCT, and the PSEAH Network on strategic and practical mitigation measures.

- Support senior leadership in developing resource mobilization strategies, Government of Liberia engagement strategies, and crisis communication and messaging strategies on PSEAH.

Leading Development of Liberia-Wide PSEAH Strategic Action Framework

- This function ensures a coordinated, country-wide strategic approach to PSEAH prevention and response across the UN system and partners in Liberia.

- Ensure annual inter-agency SEAH risk assessments are conducted in Liberia and that findings are integrated into sector assessments, UN planning frameworks (UNSDCF), and humanitarian response plans.

- Lead the development of a multi-year Liberia PSEAH Strategy with clear priorities, objectives, roles, and stakeholder responsibilities, including Government of Liberia and civil society engagement.

- Ensure alignment of PSEAH priorities with UNCT/HCT strategic planning processes and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) for Liberia.

- Develop a sustainability and exit strategy to ensure long-term national ownership and continued coordination of PSEAH mechanisms in Liberia.

- Promote integration of PSEAH within localization efforts and the humanitarian-development-peace nexus to strengthen national systems and institutions.

Oversight of Implementation of the Liberia PSEAH Programme

- This function focuses on ensuring effective coordination, implementation, and monitoring of PSEAH activities across Liberia.

- Support and advise Co-Chairs of the PSEAH Network in implementing the Network’s Terms of Reference (ToR) and Action Plan.

- Facilitate development and updating of the PSEAH Action Plan and Monitoring & Evaluation framework for Liberia.

- Conduct consultations with network members and senior leadership to assess gaps, strengths, and areas for improvement in PSEAH implementation.

- Support development of a sustainable resourcing plan for the Liberia PSEAH Programme.

- Provide regular updates and briefings to the PSEAH Network on emerging risks and implementation challenges.

- Strengthen national and in-country capacity by identifying skilled partners within the Network to lead training, mentorship, and capacity-building initiatives, including training of trainers (ToT) for PSEAH Network members.

- Promote collaboration between PSEAH Network, AAP, and CwC platforms to integrate community feedback into prevention and response systems.

- Assign and coordinate technical responsibilities within the Network to support information management, capacity building, and stakeholder engagement.

- Strengthening data systems to ensure risk assessment findings and case trends inform decision-making and programme improvements.

Strengthening Victim/Survivor-Centred Approach (VSCA) in Liberia

- This area ensures that all PSEAH interventions in Liberia prioritize dignity, safety, and rights of victims and survivors.

- Ensure coordination between the PSEAH Network and Protection Cluster, GBV sub-sector, and Child Protection actors in Liberia for a harmonized survivor-centred response.

- Serve in a senior advisory role supporting system-wide victim/survivor rights approaches within UN and partner agencies in Liberia.

- Coordinate with GBV and Protection actors to ensure consistency in prevention and response mechanisms across the UN system.

- Facilitate integration of community feedback mechanisms through AAP and CwC platforms to improve reporting and response systems.

- Support strengthening of Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs) across agencies to ensure safe, accessible reporting channels.

- Develop and support rollout of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for inter-agency SEAH referral pathways in Liberia.

- Ensure SOPs align with GBV and Child Protection referral systems and adhere to victim/survivor-centred principles.

- Support training of focal points and staff in safe reporting, complaint handling, and referral systems.

- Coordinate capacity-building initiatives on survivor-centred approaches across UN and partner organizations.

Stakeholder Engagement and Knowledge Sharing

- This function ensures strong coordination, advocacy, and knowledge sharing across national, regional, and global levels.

- Engage Government of Liberia institutions, UN agencies, NGOs, and civil society to strengthen PSEAH coordination and capacity-building.

- Represent inter-agency PSEAH priorities in UNCT, HCT, OMT, and regional coordination platforms.

- Provide regular briefings to UN leadership on PSEAH risks, progress, and implementation challenges in Liberia.

- Strengthen linkages with sub-national structures, including county-level actors, to ensure PSEAH integration across Liberia’s decentralized system.

- Liaise with regional and global PSEAH networks to ensure Liberia aligns with international standards and best practices.

- Support resource mobilization efforts for sustainable PSEAH programming in Liberia.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist will report administratively to the Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) UNDP, directly to the Resident Coordinator (RC) with a dotted-line reporting responsibility to the Chair of the UN PSEA Network. In carrying out their duties, the Specialist will work closely with the UN Country Team (UNCT) and relevant partners, including UNDP programme units, PSEA and safeguarding focal points, and other staff and consultants supporting the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) agenda.

The Specialist will collaborate across UN agencies, technical teams, and coordination structures to ensure effective coordination, strong alignment, and successful implementation of PSEAH-related activities within the UN system.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

- Act with Determination : LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

Cross Functional and Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system.

- Negotiation and Influence Ability to reach an understanding, persuade others, resolve points of difference, gain advantage in the outcome of dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions through compromise and create win-win situations.

Business Management

- Results-based Management Ability to manage Programme and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results.

- Partnerships Management Ability to build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Communications

- Creative direction and copywriting Ability to creatively communicate concepts in an engaging and simple way.

- People Gender Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Social Work, Public Health, Gender Studies, Law, Human Rights, Humanitarian Studies, International Relations, and/or another related social science discipline is required. OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of five (5) years of experience (with a Master’s degree), or seven (7) years of experience (with a Bachelor’s degree), in Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), protection, human rights, and/or gender-based violence or a related field is required.

Required skills:

- Experience in coordination and stakeholder engagement skills: Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-agency or multisectoral groups, evidenced by successfully facilitating at least 4–6 inter-agency coordination meetings per year and ensuring actionable follow-up on agreed recommendations, is required.

- Experience in data analysis and reporting skills: Ability to collect, analyze, and interpret PSEA-related data, with proven experience producing at least quarterly analytical reports that inform decision-making and risk mitigation strategies, is required.

- Experience in capacity-building and training skills/experience: Experience designing and delivering PSEA training sessions, demonstrated by conducting a minimum of 3–5 training or awareness sessions annually for staff, partners, or community stakeholders, is required.

- Experience in communication and advocacy skills: Strong ability to develop clear messaging and advocacy materials on PSEA, demonstrated through the production of regular communication products—such as briefings, awareness materials, or campaigns—at least 2–4 times per year and engagement with diverse audiences, is required.

- Experience in field experience in humanitarian and/or development settings in PSEAH is required.

Desired knowledges and skills:

- Experience in risk assessment and safeguarding skills: Ability to conduct PSEA risk assessments across programmes or operations, evidenced by completing at least 1–2 formal risk assessments per programme cycle, including mitigation recommendations, is desired.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Country Office in Tajikistan has been active since 1994 and is guided in its work by the Country Programme Document, which in turn builds upon the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP has made a significant contribution to developing the National Development Strategy, with an outline of policies and investments necessary to reach the SDGs by 2030. Together with the Government of Tajikistan, civil society and the people of Tajikistan, UNDP works towards identifying local solutions to global and national development challenges. Its main focus is reaching sustainable development by enhancing accountability of the current governance system, mitigating natural disaster threats, and contributing to environmental sustainability and biodiversity conservation.

The Climate Change, Energy and Environment (CCEE) Cluster of UNDP Tajikistan manages a diverse and growing portfolio of various projects currently under implementation across the country. The Cluster provides strategic, technical, and operational support to national counterparts in addressing Tajikistan’s key environmental, climate, and energy challenges, in line with national development priorities and international commitments. The Cluster’s programmatic focus spans several interrelated thematic areas, including climate change adaptation and mitigation, integrated water resources management, sustainable land management, urban resilience to disaster and climate risks, promotion of renewable and green energy solutions, and biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration.

In particular, with regard to biodiversity conservation and it’s biodiversity portfolio, UNDP's Country Office in Tajikistan is currently supporting the country’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) update and implementation in alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). As countries move from updating their NBSAPs towards implementation, targeted support is required to translate national biodiversity priorities into concrete actions and address critical implementation gaps.

In this context, the NBSAP Accelerator Action Account Multi-Partner Trust Fund (NBSAP AAA MPTF) provides targeted support to countries to accelerate implementation of their NBSAP priorities and translate national biodiversity commitments into concrete action. The Fund supports high-priority interventions that address critical policy, institutional, technical and financing gaps and that have not been sufficiently covered through other available resources. Its support is intended to strengthen national readiness for sustained biodiversity action, increase implementation ambition and create foundations for further investment in achievement of national biodiversity priorities and the KMGBF.

In Tajikistan, the project directly contributes to the objectives of the NBSAP AAA MPTF by providing targeted support for NBSAP implementation, with a particular focus on operationalizing KMGBF Target 6 on invasive alien species (IAS). The project will strengthen the scientific, technical and policy basis for the prevention, monitoring and management of IAS, including through establishment of a national IAS database and development of the country’s first State Programme and Action Plan on Invasive Alien Species. These interventions will help address critical data and policy gaps, strengthen national capacities for ongoing biological risk monitoring and management, and establish a more coherent framework for coordinated action on invasive alien species.

The project further contributes to strengthening the core functions of NBSAP implementation through institutional capacity development and strategic policy support, applying a “whole-of-government” and “whole-of-society” approach. It also contributes to KMGBF Target 23 on gender equality by integrating gender-responsive approaches and promoting the equitable participation of women and vulnerable groups within IAS knowledge, monitoring and policy systems. The initiative will additionally promote youth engagement and digital innovation in biodiversity information management, thereby supporting an inclusive, sustainable and potentially scalable approach to implementation of KMGBF priorities in Tajikistan.

Under the direct supervision of UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment, and overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Project Coordinator will coordinate project interventions, liaise with national partners and support effective teamwork and strong partnerships. The Project Coordinator will provide technical and programmatic support to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality project results that strengthen national capacities, data systems and policy frameworks for the prevention and management of invasive alien species, in line with Tajikistan’s NBSAP and the KMGBF.

He/she will ensure implementation mechanisms and technical working groups are established and meet regularly, that all planned workshops, technical studies and other activities are organised in a timely manner, and that they meet expected quality standards. He/she will also specifically be responsible for outreach activities to relevant stakeholders, and the preparation of synthesis reports, policy briefs, press releases and briefing notes for Government, donor, UNDP, etc.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure effective technical support to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- General coordination and liaison of project activities with national counterparts, scientific institutions and relevant stakeholders.

- Coordinate the development and validation of the National IAS Catalogue and Database.

- Facilitate the development, testing and validation of standardized IAS risk assessment protocols.

- Coordinate the development of the multi-sectoral National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Ensure alignment of the project’s technical outputs with the NBSAP, the KMGBF, national biodiversity reporting processes and other relevant national policies and strategic frameworks.

- Facilitate technical assessments, field data collection, consultations and other analytical work required for the development of the National IAS Catalogue, risk assessment protocols, IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide substantive support to project stakeholders in reviewing and validating technical methodologies, assessments, databases, policy documents and other project outputs.

- Coordinate project activities among relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre under the Committee for Environmental Protection, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry Agency, Customs Service, Food Security Committee, other relevant ministries and agencies, civil society organizations, academia and local communities, as specified in the Project Document.

- Facilitate the establishment and effective functioning of the Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group for technical coordination, policy dialogue and development and validation of project outputs.

- Ensure the elaboration of the Stakeholder Engagement and Gender Action Plan before the kickstart of project implementation, and further ensure their effective implementation and regular monitoring.

- Ensure that gender-responsive approaches and meaningful participation of women, youth and vulnerable groups are appropriately integrated into IAS assessments, data systems, consultations and policy development in line with the project’s Results Framework.

- Coordinate and follow up on implementation of relevant environmental and social safeguard measures.

- Review all technical reports as required. Fulfil substantive activities under the Project Work Plan which are not covered by consultants or other contracted experts.

- Support the timely technical review, validation, finalization and submission to relevant national authorities of key project outputs, including the National IAS Catalogue, standardized risk assessment protocols, national IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide necessary inputs to showcase project’s experience at national, regional and international forums/events as required.

- Upon request of the Programme Specialist, participate in and make presentations at conferences, working meetings, workshops, round-table discussions and other relevant events on the IAS project and its linkages with biodiversity conservation, NBSAP and KMGBF implementation.

2. Ensure effective operational and programmatic support for the project:

- Ensure operational and programmatic coordination of the project in accordance with the Project Document, approved work plans, Results Framework and applicable UNDP rules and procedures.

- Support the overall management and coordination of project implementation, ensuring timely and proper execution of activities by consultants, experts, contractors and project partners.

- Prepare Terms of Reference (ToR) for national and international consultants, experts, contractors and other service providers in line with the Project Document and relevant UNDP procedures; coordinate and guide their work and ensure compliance with agreed work plans and respective ToRs and the quality and timely delivery of outputs.

- Facilitate organization of the project Inception Workshop and support the establishment and functioning of the Project Steering Committee, Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group.

- Support communication and coordination with government institutions, scientific organizations, civil society organizations, local communities and other stakeholders involved in implementation of activities specified in the Project Work Plan.

- Prepare meeting agendas and background materials, take notes/minutes of project meetings and ensure timely follow-up on decisions and agreed actions.

- Support preparation and implementation of annual and detailed project work plans, including monitoring of implementation progress and follow-up on planned activities and deliverables.

- Monitor project progress against the Results Framework, including achievement of indicators and targets, and coordinate collection, verification and consolidation of supporting evidence.

- Collect and analyze project-related data and information from government counterparts, consultants, scientific institutions, implementing partners and other relevant sources for project monitoring and reporting purposes.

- Assume responsibility for the timely preparation of project progress reports and other required inputs in line with the reporting requirements of NBSAP AAA MPTF and corporate standards of UNDP.

- Support preparation of the project’s final report and project operational closure upon completion of project activities.

- Monitor project risks and issues in accordance with the Project Document and risk framework and ensure that emerging risks are promptly brought to the attention of the Programme Specialist and relevant project governance bodies.

- Support regular updating of project risk log and follow up on agreed risk mitigation measures.

- Monitor project expenditures, commitments and balances against approved project budget lines and work plans and bring potential deviations requiring management attention to the Programme Specialist.

- Coordinate project activities with other relevant biodiversity, climate and environmental initiatives and programmes in Tajikistan to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication and promote synergies, including with NBSAP update and national reporting.

- Provide assistance and substantive inputs to the Programme Specialist in preparation of project briefs, presentations, reports, talking points and other relevant materials.

- Ensure effective dissemination of and access to information on project activities and results, and support project outreach and communication activities in coordination with UNDP communications staff.

- Liaise with the NBSAP AAA MPTF focal point and relevant UNDP regional focal point(s) to ensure effective project implementation, seek and follow up on technical and operational guidance, address project-related issues and queries, and ensure alignment with applicable programme requirements and guidance.

- Support resource mobilization efforts by providing inputs to the new project ideas, concept notes, funding proposals, and other relevant resource mobilization materials.

3. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area.

- Organize trainings, technical workshops, consultations, awareness-raising events and capacity-building activities in a participatory manner, involving relevant government institutions, scientific / academic institutions, civil society organizations, local communities, women and youth groups, and other stakeholders.

- Support capacity building of decision-makers and relevant technical institutions on IAS identification, risk assessment, Geographic Information System (GIS)-based monitoring, data management, use of the national IAS Database to be established under the project, and relevant NBSAP and KMGBF frameworks.

- Support development and dissemination of technical guidance, IAS field guides, training materials, project briefs, factsheets, awareness materials and other knowledge products generated under the project.

- Identify, synthesize and document good practices, lessons learned and implementation experience generated by the project and its partners, including through maintenance of relevant project knowledge and lessons-learned records.

- Participate in and ensure substantive contributions to relevant knowledge networks, communities of practice and technical exchanges on IAS management, biodiversity conservation and implementation of the NBSAP and KMGBF.

- Promote awareness and advocacy on IAS-related biodiversity risks, prevention and management measures, and opportunities for collaboration in coordination with project partners, stakeholders and UNDP communications staff.

- Support engagement of women, youth and local communities in knowledge generation, awareness raising and dissemination of biodiversity information, in line with the project’s whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will be based in Dushanbe, at the premises of either the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Center or the National Academy of Sciences, subject to management decision with frequent visits to the UNDP Country Office. Background and Organizational Context

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994. UNDP has a strong track record and comparative advantage to support the achievement of national priorities and United Nations Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNMSDCF). It is one of the leading United Nations agencies present in Suriname in terms of programmatic scope, partnerships and financial footprint. The advantage of UNDP is illustrated by the achievements during the program cycle 2022-2026, which supported the priorities around democratic governance, sustainable development and climate action. The Country Program 2027-2031 will focus on supporting Suriname around two strategic programme areas: (a) democratic governance for inclusive transformation; and (b) resilience and environmental protection.

UNDP’s support to the Democratic Governance for Inclusive Transformation will include four interlinked priorities: a) electoral support; b) decentralization and local governance; c) revenue governance and public financial management; and d) digitalization and innovation. In addition, UNDP Suriname will continue as the funding recipient of the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Suriname and facilitates the CCM Secretariat. Other programmatic priorities may be included in consultation with the development partners and stakeholders in Suriname. In its interventions, UNDP prioritizes participation of all, including women, youth, and ITPs as a way to increase institutional effectiveness and improve transparency, accountability, and inclusion in public decision-making.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative/Head of Office, the Programme Analyst (Effective Governance and Inclusive Transformation) is responsible for managing and further expanding the programme portfolio and creating synergies, complementarities and linkages with the resilience and environment protection work of UNDP, applying a portfolio approach.

Specifically, the role includes executing and expanding current projects, building a pipeline of new initiatives that are aligned with Suriname’s national priorities, and UNDP’s policies, programmatic and operational offer globally and in the region. Importantly, the incumbent will be responsible for maintaining and expanding UNDP’s partnerships with the Government, bilateral donors, UN agencies, vertical funds (GEF, GCF, others), the EU, IFIs and other partner organizations.

The incumbent will support the senior management of the UNDP Suriname in the design and execution of thematic and sectoral strategies, knowledge management, partnerships, and support the implementation of other strategic initiatives.

The Programme Programme Analyst (Effective Governance and Inclusive Transformation) will supervise the Programme Associate and be a part of a multidisciplinary team working closely with other thematic portfolio and the Operations team at UNDP Suriname, the Regional Bureau for LAC, the Regional Hub in Panama and the technical and operational teams across UNDP.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Resident Representative (RR), Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) the Programme Analyst is responsible for management of UNDP programme within the thematic/sectoral areas assigned. The Programme Analyst analyzes political, social and economic trends; leads formulation, management and evaluation of programme activities within his/her portfolio; and provides policy advice services.

The Programme Analyst supervises and leads the Programme Associate and coordinates activities of the project’s staff. The Programme Analyst works in close collaboration with the Programme and Operations teams in the CO, programme staff in other UN Agencies, UNDP staff in HQs and Regional Hubs, technical advisors/experts, external specialists, government officials and partners, donors, and civil society to ensure successful implementation of the UNDP programme.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

1. Contribute to formulation and Implementation of UNDP Programme Strategies and policies

- Analyze socio-political, governance, and social development trends and identify areas for UNDP support.

- Lead the development and execution of thematic strategies on governance, poverty reduction, social services, and SDG integration.

- Provide technical input to national planning processes (e.g., CCA, UNMSDCF, CPD).

- Promote inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches in programme design and delivery.

2. Ensure effective management of the CO programme within the assigned thematic/sector areas focusing on quality assurance and risk management from formulation to implementation of the country programme

- Design and formulate programme/project proposals, ensuring alignment with national development goals and UNDP priorities.

- Apply RBM tools and manage project implementation, financials, and reporting.

- Ensure programme results and indicators are met in a timely and efficient manner.

- Organize and support evaluations, audits, and strategic reviews.

3. Build strategic partnerships and resource mobilization

- Develop and strengthen partnerships with government, UN agencies, donors, NGOs, civil society, and the private sector.

- Identify funding opportunities and contribute to the office’s resource mobilization strategy.

- Contribute to joint programming and inter-agency collaboration, especially around social development and governance reform.

4. Policy Advisory Services and Knowledge Management

- Facilitate the development of evidence-based policies and institutional reforms related to governance and inclusive transformation.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Objetivo do Cargo e Contexto Organizacional

O projeto “Fortalecimento e monitoramento das ações de inovação e aperfeiçoamento dos sistemas penal e socioeducativo, em linha com princípios e diretrizes nacionais e internacionais de direitos humanos”, tem por objetivo atuar no desenvolvimento de metodologias e ações inovadoras com foco em restabelecer o regular e adequado funcionamento do sistema prisional e socioeducativo, além de produzir subsídios para fortalecer o monitoramento e a fiscalização das intervenções oficiais sobre esses sistemas, alinhado aos princípios e diretrizes nacionais e internacionais de direitos humanos. Em especial, o projeto atuará de forma a instrumentalizar o Conselho Nacional de Justiça – CNJ para: (i) o fomento ao desenvolvimento dos mandatos e das capacidades (constitucionais, convencionais e legais) do Poder Judiciário para a superação de gargalos e dos entraves que dificultam a performance individual e uma melhor atuação coletiva de magistrados diante dos sistemas penal e socioeducativo, notadamente para a proteção das posições de populações mais vulneráveis, e (ii) a atuação na viabilização do pleno e integral cumprimento da decisão (de mérito) proferida pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal na ADPF 347, que consolidou o entendimento acerca da existência de um estado de coisas inconstitucional das prisões brasileiras, determinando a pactuação e o monitoramento de um plano nacional e de planos estaduais e distrital voltados à superação de um quadro de desarranjos estruturais e de violação massiva e sistemática a direitos fundamentais – cenário que impede a realização da gramática e dos programas de princípios presentes na Constituição Federal, nos Tratados Internacionais de Direitos Humanos e na Legislação ordinária.

Para o alcance desses objetivos, o projeto se organiza em 6 linhas de atuação, que correspondem aos resultados intermediários esperados:

1 Implantação, fortalecimento e acompanhamento/avaliação de ações que garantam o regular funcionamento do sistema penal;

2 Implantação, fortalecimento e acompanhamento/avaliação de ações que garantam o regular funcionamento do sistema socioeducativo;

3 Aperfeiçoamento e incremento quantitativo e qualitativo da coleta e produção de dados oriundos dos sistemas penal e socioeducativo;

4 Aperfeiçoamento, fortalecimento e acompanhamento de estratégias de atenção a populações mais vulneráveis em contato com os sistemas penal e socioeducativo;

5 Assessoria técnica ao CNJ para incidência junto à magistratura de 1º e 2º graus, por meio de criação de canais de sensibilização e comunicação, disseminação de conteúdos, formação, treinamento, estratégias de interação, diálogo e outras ações que permitam melhor instrumentalizar o cabedal das opções de atuação dos juízes brasileiros, viabilizando-lhes práticas mais compreensivas quanto à população e suas desigualdades;

6 Gestão eficiente e gestão de conhecimento do projeto realizadas.

Nesse contexto, o Núcleo de Dados e Evidências do Programa Fazendo Justiça vem desenvolvendo e mantendo o sistema de monitoramento do Plano Pena Justa, ferramentas de gestão da informação e de visualização de dados, com vistas a apoiar a governança, o reporte institucional e o acompanhamento da implementação do Plano e de outras políticas implementadas e/ou acompanhadas pelo programa. Considerando a necessidade de apoio técnico para o desenvolvimento, manutenção e evolução de soluções, torna-se necessária a contratação de profissional especializado para apoiar a consolidação da camada analítica dos dados coletados, a estruturação de fluxos de ETL, o desenvolvimento de serviços de publicação de dados e a construção de painéis de visualização voltados tanto ao monitoramento da implementação do Plano quanto ao acompanhamento da coleta de informações das demais políticas. Tal apoio técnico é necessário para fortalecer a confiabilidade, a usabilidade e a transparência das informações produzidas, em consonância com as diretrizes de governança e monitoramento estabelecidas.

Os resultados-chave esperados para este posto visam garantir a qualidade, eficiência e efetividade na implementação do projeto, em linha com as metas acordadas e com as prioridades do CNJ.

O projeto tem vigência até 31/12/2027.

Deveres e responsabilidades

A/o Associado/a Técnico/a de Monitoramento Analítico será responsável por, sob supervisão da Coordenação de Pesquisa em Direitos Humanos e Acesso à Justiça, realizar assessoria técnica ao planejamento, implementação e acompanhamento de ações de desenvolvimento de sistemas previstas nessa iniciativa, colaborando para o cumprimento do cronograma estabelecido e a qualidade das entregas realizadas. A pessoa contratada atuará ainda em estreita articulação com a equipe do CNJ e do PNUD. Para o alcance desse objetivo, estão previstas as seguintes atividades indicativas:

1.Desenvolvimento da Aplicação Web e Tratamento de Dados

a) Atuar no desenvolvimento do front-end e do back-end da aplicação web dos formulários de coleta de dados.

b) Produzir testes unitários e documentação da aplicação web correspondente.

c) Organizar e limpar os dados coletados para construção de relatórios analíticos.

2. Estruturação e Análise de Bases de Dados

a) Estruturar, armazenar e organizar as diversas fontes de dados utilizadas pelo DMF/CNJ.

b) Contribuir na elaboração de diagnósticos e análises dessas bases.

c) Produzir relatórios e painéis com estatísticas descritivas e utilização de gráficos, tabelas, mapas, infográficos.

3. Saneamento e Regularização dos Fluxos de Dados

a) Articular com os atores necessários para o saneamento e a regularização dos fluxos de dados.

4. Desenvolvimento de Modelos Preditivos e de Classificação

a) Elaborar modelos preditivos e/ou de classificação.

5.Implantação e Monitoramento das Atividades do Eixo

a) Atuar nas atividades de implantação, acompanhamento técnico e monitoramento qualitativo dos produtos e metas previstas no Eixo sob sua responsabilidade.

b) Contribuir na sistematização de novas metodologias e conhecimentos desenvolvidos no âmbito do projeto.

c) Facilitar a transferência de conhecimentos ao CNJ.

d) Realizar o planejamento, cronograma e relatório de suas atividades e dos projetos que está envolvido.

6. Avaliação e Uso de Soluções Tecnológicas

a) Colaborar e apoiar o programa na avaliação e uso de soluções tecnológicas para aprimoramento da qualidade dos dados.

7. Apoio à Produção, Análise de Dados e Gestão do Conhecimento

a) Desenvolver ferramentas de coleta, armazenamento e gestão de dados.

b) Colaborar com a equipe de dados no atendimento às demandas da Coordenação Geral do Programa Fazendo Justiça e do DMF/CNJ.

c) Apoiar a produção, organização e preparação de conjuntos de dados, estatísticas e análises.

d) Organizar e manter atualizados registros e materiais de referência relacionados às bases de dados, fluxos de tratamento, metodologias de análise e soluções desenvolvidas no âmbito do projeto.

e) Contribuir para a elaboração de documentação técnica que favoreça a compreensão, a replicabilidade e a continuidade das soluções e processos desenvolvidos.

f) Apoiar a disseminação e transferência de conhecimentos técnicos à equipe do CNJ, por meio da elaboração de materiais, orientações e outros recursos de apoio.

O titular desempenha outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do Projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

A/o Associado/a Técnico/a de Monitoramento Analítico integrará o Núcleo de Dados e Evidências e estará submetido/a à supervisão direta do/a Coordenador(a) de Pesquisa em Direitos Humanos e Acesso à Justiça.

Competências

- Alcançar Resultados - NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora seu próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes e entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo.

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas e riscos conhecidos, é um solucionador de problemas prático e faz melhorias.

- Aprender Continuamente - NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curioso, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros e pede feedback.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se às mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidades e incertezas, e é flexível..

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra determinação e motivação, mantém a calma diante da adversidade e tem confiança.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão e compreensão em relação aos outros, formando relacionamentos positivos.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios / Pensamento Estratégico

- Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e estratégia de negócios / Pensamento Sistêmico

- Capacidade de usar análise objetiva e julgamento de problemas para entender como os elementos inter-relacionados coexistem dentro do todo de um processo ou sistema, e considerar como a alteração de um elemento pode impactar outras partes do sistema

Desenvolvimento de negócios/ /Design centrado no humano

- Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de negócios / Gestão de Projetos

- Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

Gestão de negócios / Conhecimento e Alfabetização Digital

- Capacidade de acompanhar tecnologias novas e emergentes, bem como de compreender sua utilização, potencial, limitações, impacto e valor agregado. Capacidade de adotar e utilizar novas tecnologias de forma rápida e ágil nas atividades profissionais, e de capacitar outras pessoas a utilizá-las conforme necessário. Conhecimento sobre o uso de tecnologias digitais e tendências emergentes.

Agenda 2030: Engajamento e Eficácia / Inovação

- Ecossistema de Inovação

Habilidades e experiência necessárias

Requisitos mínimos de educação:

- Diploma do Ensino Médio é requerido.

- Diploma Universitário (Ensino Superior) em Ciências Sociais, Tecnologia da Informação, Gestão Pública, Administração Pública, Economia, Estatística ou áreas afins será dada a devida consideração, mas não é um requisito.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

- Mínimo de 7 anos (para Ensino Médio) ou 4 anos (para Ensino Superior) de experiência profissional relevante em análise quantitativa de dados sociais e econômicos, incluindo programação para análise de dados e/ou desenvolvimento de soluções ou sistemas de informação, bem como produção, análise, publicação e/ou visualização de dados.

Habilidades desejadas:

- Experiência em elaboração de documentação técnica e sistematização de metodologias e conhecimentos relacionados às soluções desenvolvidas.

- Experiência no uso de tecnologia da informação, incluindo o pacote Microsoft Office

Habilidades desejadas, além das competências abordadas na seção Competências:

- Experiência no uso de ferramentas de relatório (Tableau, Power BI, R Shiny etc.);

- Experiência em ciências de dados e linguagem de programação em R ou Python;

- Experiência em um ou mais sistemas gerenciadores de banco de dados, linguagem SQL, modelagem estatística e modelagem de bases de dados (relacionais e dimensionais);

- Experiência em linguagem de desenvolvimento web (HTML + CSS);

- Experiência anterior em projetos com bases de dados do sistema judiciário.

Idiomas exigidos:

jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. In December 1991, the General Assembly adopted Resolution 46/182 designed to strengthen the United Nation's response to both complex emergencies and natural disasters. In addition, it aimed at improving the overall effectiveness of the UN's humanitarian operations in the field.

OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to:

- Alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies.

- Advocate for the rights of people in need.

- Promote preparedness and prevention.

- Facilitate sustainable solutions.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Fleet Dispatcher the incumbent will undertake the tasks below;

- Provision of reliable and secure driving services.

- Proper use of vehicle.

- Day-to-day maintenance of the assigned vehicle.

- Availability of documents/ supplies.

- Vehicle Cleanliness, Security, and Serviceability.

- Vehicle Inspection and Preventive Maintenance.

- Accident Reporting and Compliance.

- Other Related Duties.

1- Provision of reliable and secure driving services:

- Ensures provision of reliable and secure driving services by a) driving office vehicles for the transport of authorized personnel and delivery and collection of mail, documents and other items and b) meeting official personnel and visitors at the airport, visa and customs formalities arrangement when required.

- Ensures cost-savings through proper use of vehicle through accurate maintenance of daily vehicle logs, provision of inputs to preparation of the vehicle maintenance plans and reports

2- Proper use of vehicle

- Ensures proper day-to-day maintenance of the assigned vehicle through timely minor repairs, arrangements for major repairs, timely changes of oil, check of tires, brakes, car washing, etc

3- Day-to-day maintenance of the assigned vehicle

- Ensures availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, vehicle logs, office directory, map of the city/country, first aid kit, necessary spare parts.

4- Availability of documents/ supplies

- Ensures that all immediate actions required by rules and regulations are taken in case of involvement in accidents.

5- Vehicle Cleanliness, Security, and Serviceability

- Ensures that the assigned vehicle is clean, secure, properly equipped, and maintained in a roadworthy condition. Monitors fuel and fluid levels and coordinates scheduled servicing and repairs with the Fleet/Transport Unit

6- Vehicle Inspection and Preventive Maintenance

- Conducts routine inspections of assigned vehicles, checking engine oil, coolant, battery, brakes, tyres, lights, and other essential components. Performs minor maintenance when appropriate and reports technical defects promptly.

7- Accident Reporting and Compliance

- Ensures that all required procedures are followed in the event of a vehicle accident, including notifying the office immediately, completing the necessary reports, and cooperating with the relevant authorities as required.

8- Other Related Duties

Performs other duties in support of UN/OCHA operational requirements.

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Compound management in terms of electricity, water, generator and cleanness.

jobs.description:

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Republic of Moldova's EU accession process and decentralization reform require stronger inter-communal cooperation to improve the planning and delivery of essential public services that benefit equally men and women, including from marginalized/vulnerable groups. While Intercommunal Development Associations (IDAs) have significant potential to support integrated territorial development, they continue to face legal, institutional, and capacity constraints. The project will support the Government of the Republic of Moldova, through the State Chancellery and partner local authorities, to strengthen the inter-communal cooperation framework by improving the regulatory framework, developing and piloting an integrated strategic planning methodology for IDAs, and establishing a digital platform for coordination and knowledge sharing. The project will also facilitate peer exchange with French local authorities to strengthen capacities in territorial governance, essential and inclusive public service delivery, and access to EU funding, contributing to more effective people-centered local governance and enhanced readiness for EU integration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the PRIM Project Manager, the Public Services Improvement Analyst ensures the effective and efficient implementation of local public service improvement at local level. The incumbent applies and promotes the principles of results-based management (RBM), as well as a client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations.

Public Services Improvement Analyst works in close collaboration with the Programme Specialist/Cluster Lead and other Project Managers for effective achievement of results and resolving complex project- related issues and information delivery.

The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies, as well as implementation of the effective internal control systems.

The incumbent will ensure the provision of development services and products (commensurate with the scope of the project) of the highest quality and standards to national counterparts and clients through applying HRBA and GE approaches. More specifically:

1. Support to local public service improvement issues, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Advise and assist targeted local public authorities to develop and implement capacity building plans in the area of local public service improvement, through participatory community involvement processes.

- Promote a participatory, human rights and gender sensitive approach to service provision at local level in close coordination with other local and national partners.

- Support the implementation of jointly selected service improvement initiatives, with active participation of community members (using inter-municipal cooperation, PPPs and other tools) and through expansion of the services currently rendered in the urban centers towards the neighboring communities.

- Support in general project development, implementation and project-related strategic processes.

2. Ensure provision of top-quality advisory services and facilitation of knowledge building and management, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Provide policy options and high-quality advisory inputs to the project from local development perspective to ensure these are responsive to national policies, priorities and strategic plans, and advance UNDP's corporate goals.

- Provide training and capacity building support on local public service improvement.

- Make sound contributions to local development-related knowledge networks and communities of practice

- Provide solid inputs to project’s analytical products, work plans and progress reports, etc.

- Identify and synthesis of best practices and lessons learnt from the field.

- Conduct analytical work (e.g. institutional and risk analyses, capacity assessment, policy reviews) community development highlighting UNDP support and strategy. Play an active role in policy advice, strategic thinking, knowledge sharing.

3. Ensure creation of strategic partnerships, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Liaise, synergy and coordination with project partners on common service provision issues.

- Prepare substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation with development partners, contribute to the resource mobilization efforts.

- Ensure wide dissemination and visibility of project achievements. Participate in national and international fora, making substantive contributions as appropriate.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

The key results have a direct impact on the overall successful achievement of the Project. Accurate analysis and presentation of information enhances UNDP's position as a strong development partner. The information provided facilitates decision-making of UNDP management.

Institutional Arrangement

Direct supervisor: PRIM Project Manager.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional and Technical Competencies

Business Management

- Partnerships Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Customer Satisfaction and Client Management: Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Development

- Knowledge Facilitation: Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Digital

- Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

2030 Agenda: Peace

- Governance: Governance for Public Goods and Services

2030 Agenda: People

- Gender: Inclusive governance and women’s participation and representation

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Local Public Administration, Economics, Public Finances, Public Law, or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of 2 years of experience at the national or international level in the field of policy development, with substantial recent work experience local development projects with focus on services provision.

Desired skills:

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and advance knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages, experience in handling of web-based management systems.

- Previous experience in development assistance or related work for a donor organization, governmental institutions, NGO or private sector / consulting firm.

- Practical experience in inter-municipal cooperation, initiation and implementation.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and Romanian is required.

- Working knowledge of one or more additional languages relevant for Moldova, including Russian, Bulgarian, Gagauzian, Romani, Ukrainian or sign language would be and asset.
